## Square-zero polynomial hosts: exact edge partitions and uniform thinning obstruction

This continuation completed the congruence-ring branch left pending after the
cubic-jet work. These theorems are obstructions to a construction family, NOT
a proof or disproof of Erdős 714. Spec.lean has not changed.

### Arbitrary hosts partitioned into complete bipartite blocks

`Submission/BicliquePartition.lean` is complete, has no sorry, compiles, and
has its olean installed. Log: `/tmp/BicliquePartition.final2.log`.
The printed audits of `density_bound` and `fourth_density_bound` use only
propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

For a finite graph G with copies of K_(L_i,R_i), the hypothesis is explicitly
that the map from the disjoint union of the blocks' EDGE SETS to G.edgeSet is
bijective. Thus this is a partition of actual edges, not merely a cover of
vertices, and no unaccounted edge multiplicity is allowed. If both block
parts have size at least t and H<=G is K_(r,r)-free, then

    t^2 * e(H) <= ex(2*t,K_(r,r)) * e(G).

`density_bound` uses edge-transitive averaging on each complete block and an
explicit bijection counting all retained edges. `extremal_fourth` applies the
existing integral KST bound to an extremal graph on 2*t vertices:

    ex(2*t,K44)^4 <= 10368*t^7.

Raising the density bound to the fourth power and cancelling t^7 (with t=0
handled separately) proves `fourth_density_bound`:

    t * e(H)^4 <= 10368 * e(G)^4.

### Every polynomial is affine on a square-zero ideal coset

`Submission/SquareZeroPolynomial.lean` is complete, has no sorry, and has its
olean installed. Clean final log: `/tmp/SquareZeroPolynomial.final2.log`.
Audits of `affine_on_coset`, `block_partition`, `polynomial_thinning`, and
`full_polynomial_thinning` use only the permitted axioms.

Let R be a commutative ring and I an ideal with a*b=0 for all a,b in I.
For every multivariate polynomial P and base vector x, `affine_on_coset`
constructs an additive homomorphism L:I^sigma -> I satisfying

    P(x+u)=P(x)+L(u).

The proof is direct MvPolynomial induction: constants, sums, and multiplication
by one variable. The sole quadratic error term vanishes by I^2=0. It does
not assume bounded polynomial degree or a derivative theorem.
`split_affine` splits the variables into row and column variables:

    P(x+u,y+v)=P(x,y)+L(u)+M(v).

`fiber_card_bound` translates every nonempty additive-hom fiber to the kernel
and applies AdditiveCoding's kernel cardinality bound. In particular, every
nonempty fiber I^sigma -> I has at least |I|^(|sigma|-1) elements when
|sigma|>=1. The corresponding coercion-to-R fibers have the same size.

`separatedGraph` permits arbitrary base indices s,t and independently varying
homomorphisms L_(s,t), M_(s,t), with adjacency

    C(s,t)+L_(s,t)(u)+M_(s,t)(v)=0.

`Block` records s,t,a,b satisfying C+a+b=0 and nonempty fibers at a,b.
`blockCopy` constructs the ACTUAL complete bipartite graph copy on those
fibers. `block_partition` proves bijectivity of the mapped-edge function:
every edge determines s,t and both hom values, and conversely each block
edge satisfies the original equation. `separated_thinning` applies the
integral relative-density bound above.

`cosetGraph` is defined by the original polynomial evaluation, not by an
assumed separable replacement. `polynomial_thinning` uses `split_affine` to
prove graph equality and then applies the separated theorem. It holds for
arbitrary families of base vectors, with at least d+1 coordinates on each
side:

    |I|^d * e(H)^4 <= 10368 * e(cosetGraph)^4.

Finally, `representative`, `cosetEquiv`, and `vectorCosetEquiv` construct exact
finite-set coordinates

    R = (R/I) x I,
    R^sigma = (R/I)^sigma x I^sigma.

`polynomialCosetIso` identifies the full polynomial incidence graph with its
coset parametrization; there are no repeated vertices. Pulling H back through
this isomorphism and transferring edge cardinalities proves
`full_polynomial_thinning` on the FULL ring-valued graph, with the same bound.
No polynomial-host degree estimate is assumed or asserted by this theorem.

### All square moduli, not only prime squares

`Submission/SquareZeroCongruence.lean` is complete, no sorry, clean compile,
olean installed. Log: `/tmp/SquareZeroCongruence.final.log`.
Audits of `squareIdeal_mul`, `squareIdeal_card`, and
`four_dimensional_thinning` use only the permitted axioms.

For any nonzero natural number m, use the ideal

    I = ker(ZMod(m^2) -> ZMod(m)).

The reduction is surjective. Elements of I have integer representatives
divisible by m, so products vanish modulo m^2. The quotient-kernel ring
isomorphism and the coset equivalence give |I|=m. Hence for EVERY polynomial
P in four row and four column variables over ZMod(m^2), and EVERY K44-free
spanning subgraph H of its zero-incidence graph G,

    m^3 * e(H)^4 <= 10368 * e(G)^4.

Equivalently, for a nonempty host its retained edge fraction is at most
10368^(1/4)*m^(-3/4). This excludes constant-density arbitrary edge thinning
as m grows. It is independent of P's degree and coefficients. It does not
exclude non-polynomial relations, carefully restricted vertex sets, or
constructions whose host density is much greater than the desired scale.
The full theorem also applies to any other finite commutative ring with a
large square-zero ideal, but no additional valuation-ring cardinality
specialization was formalized in this continuation.

## Multiplicative Gold-plus-linear trace: three-ray theorem and subgroup failures

This continuation returned to the semilinear three-root ingredient. It did not
produce a K44-free construction, and Spec.lean remains unchanged.

### Candidate and the intended root argument

For q=2^k, E=F_(q^4), sigma=2^s with gcd(s,4*k)=1, use two copies of E*,
with adjacency

    Tr_(E/Fq)((x*y)^(sigma+1)+x*y)=1.

This is a multiplicative Cayley presentation of a Gold-PLUS-LINEAR trace
level. It differs from the previous polarized kernels
Tr(x^(sigma+1)*y+c*x*y^(sigma+1)). Its proposed scale is q^4 vertices and
q^3 degree, but no uniform degree or freeness theorem was asserted.

The four-term semilinear root bound does not automatically apply. Even when
four row points are Fq-linearly independent, solving the four trace equations
for y gives a relation of the form

    y = y0 + L(y^(sigma+1)),

where L is a general Fq-linear operator E->E, not necessarily multiplication
by a scalar or a single Frobenius term. Thus it is not the already proved
four-term scalar equation. No claim of a root bound for this general operator
is made.

### A real three-ray exclusion (Lean verified)

New `Submission/GoldTraceRays.lean` (about 75 lines), sole import
FormalConjecturesUtil. No sorry, clean compile, installed olean. Log:
`/tmp/GoldTraceRays.final.log`. The audit of `three_ray_no_common` uses only
propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

It works in ANY characteristic-two field with commuting ring endomorphisms
tau,sigma and an element omega satisfying

    omega^2+omega+1=0,
    tau(omega)=omega^2, sigma(omega)=omega^2.

Define Tr4(z)=z+tau(z)+tau^2(z)+tau^3(z). The theorem proves that the three
rows 1,omega,omega^2 cannot share a column y with kernel value 1. No finite
field/cardinality assumption or implicit trace API is needed.

Proof: the Gold term is unchanged on these three rays. Adding their equations
forces Tr4(y*sigma(y))=1 and Tr4(y)=Tr4(omega*y)=0. The latter two equations
imply y+tau^2(y)=0. Commutation then makes the four terms in
Tr4(y*sigma(y)) cancel, contradiction. This is only an exclusion of one
specified triple, NOT a K44-freeness theorem.

## Positive unbalanced parabola construction, selection bound, and quartic-invariant lift

The main conjecture remains unsolved. This continuation formalized the positive
unbalanced construction previously described informally, then proved why merely
selecting its vertices cannot produce the balanced exponent. A new nonlinear
parabola-to-parabola relation was also checked and has exact finite failures.

### Full unbalanced construction (Lean verified)

New `Submission/UnbalancedParabolas.lean`, importing Submission.Packing.
Complete, no sorry, clean compile, installed olean. Final log:
`/tmp/UnbalancedParabolas.final2.log`. Printed audits of
`full_four_point_bound`, `fullGraph_free`, `full_edge_count`, and
`pair_intersection_bound` use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

The first chart consists of quadruples (m,b,c,d), with d in F*, and equation

    d*x = (m*x+y)^2 - b*(m*x+y) - c.

There are q^3*(q-1) such rows. The parameter t=m*x+y gives the exact point
parametrization

    x=(t^2-b*t-c)/d, y=t-m*x.

`point_on`, `point_parameter`, and `parameter_injective_on` check both
membership and uniqueness, so each row has exactly q distinct points.

For two rows r0,r put h=m-m0, D=d0, P=t^2-b0*t-c0. Substitution of r0's
parametrization into r gives, after multiplying by D^2,

    (D*t+h*P)^2 - b*D*(D*t+h*P) - c*D^2 - d*D*P.

Its leading coefficients are h^2 and 2*h*D-2*h^2*b0. `intersection_value`
checks the complete polynomial identity with all five coefficients. Four
roots of a cubic force all coefficients to vanish (`cubic_coefficients`).
If r and s both pass through four distinct points of r0, and neither equals
r0, their direction differences are nonzero. Subtracting their intersection
polynomials with weights cancelling the leading term yields a cubic whose
leading coefficient is

    2*D*(m-m0)*(m'-m0)*(m'-m).

In odd characteristic it vanishes only when m=m'. `linear_values_unique`
then recovers all remaining coefficients. This proves `other_unique` and
`four_point_bound`: at most two rows in this chart pass through four points.

The missing direction chart has triples (b,c,d), d!=0, with

    d*y=x^2-b*x-c.

It has q^2*(q-1) members. `vertical_other_unique` handles intersections
between the charts: after parametrizing a vertical row by x=t, two other
chart rows give quartics with equal leading coefficient 1; their difference
has cubic coefficient 2*d0*(m-m'). This forces the rows equal. Two vertical
rows through four points are likewise equal. Therefore
`full_four_point_bound` proves the actual TWO-row bound for the FULL family.
`fullGraph_free` turns this into an actual SimpleGraph.Free K44 theorem,
including the possibility that an embedding swaps the two bipartite sides.

Exact cardinalities, writing q=|F|:

    parabola vertices = q^2*(q+1)*(q-1) = q^4-q^2,
    point vertices    = q^2,
    every row degree  = q,
    graph edges       = q^3*(q+1)*(q-1) = q^5-q^3.

These are counts of the actual normalized row types and actual undirected
edges, not incidence multiplicities. The graph theorem assumes (2:F)!=0.
It is a positive UNBALANCED construction, not the required q^7-edge graph.

`pair_intersection_bound` additionally proves that two distinct full-family
rows share at most four points. Five common points would force the leading
coefficient of a quartic to vanish; the same-direction case reduces to row
uniqueness. This pair-intersection result itself works in every characteristic.

### Arbitrary vertex selections cannot balance this family (Lean verified)

The general `Erdos714PairSelection.edge_square_bound` states: if S:A->Finset B
has |S(a) intersect S(a')|<=c for every distinct pair, then

    e(incidence S)^2 <= (c+1)*(|A|+|B|)^3.

No balance or regularity is assumed. Put D(b)=#{a:b in S(a)} and e=sum D(b).
The proof double-counts

    sum_b D(b)^2 = sum_(a,a') |S(a) intersect S(a')|
                 <= e+c*|A|^2,

applies Cauchy--Schwarz e^2<=|B|*sum D(b)^2, and uses e<=|A||B|.

`selected_edge_square_bound` accepts arbitrary injections of selected row and
point types into the full parabola construction, AND arbitrary retained edge

Thus this applies even when selections depend on q and are followed by any
edge deletion. It is not merely an estimate for random sampling.

The exact integer corollary `selected_critical_scale_bound` says: if q>0,
N<=D*q^4 and q^7<=C*e, then

Hence no unbounded sequence of such selections realizes the desired fourth-

needed; this is not an obstruction to all possible uses of parabolas.

### General small-doubling condition (Lean verified)

New file `Submission/SmallDoublingPacking.lean`, 142 lines, importing the
previously verified EnergyThinning. It compiles cleanly without sorry or
warnings, and its olean is installed. Log:
`/tmp/SmallDoublingPacking.final2.log`. Audits of all five theorems use only
propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

For arbitrary finite abelian V, finite row type Y, and neighborhoods N(y),
put e=sum_y |N(y)|. Assume the actual incidence graph is K44-free.

* `cubic_energy`: |S+S| <= K|S| implies |S|^3 <= K E(S), including S empty.
* `cubic_incidence_bound`: if every neighborhood has doubling at most K,

      e^3 <= |Y|^2 K (3 |V|^3 + 4 |V| e).

  This uses the existing general `neighborhood_energy_bound`, not any
  linear-code or homogeneous-space assumption. The cubic moment bound is
  Mathlib's `pow_sum_le_card_mul_sum_pow`.
* `critical_cubic_bound`: if |V|=q^4 and |Y|<=q^4, then

      e^3 <= 7 K q^20.

* `required_doubling`: if additionally q>0 and q^7<=C e, then

      q <= 7 K C^3.

* `large_doubling_edges`: if q>56 K C^3, WITHOUT a uniform doubling
  hypothesis, the neighborhoods satisfying |N(y)+N(y)|>K|N(y)| contribute
  at least q^7/(2C) edges, in the precise integer form

      q^7 <= 2 C sum_y (if K|N(y)| < |N(y)+N(y)| then |N(y)| else 0).

  The proof deletes all other rows' neighborhoods, proves freeness of the
  restricted incidence graph via the no-rectangle criterion, and applies
  `required_doubling` to the complementary family with constant 2C.

Thus attaining the conjectured fourth-case scale requires a substantial
edge contribution from neighborhoods with doubling growing linearly in q.
This is a necessary condition, NOT a universal extremal upper bound: general
neighborhoods can have such large doubling. No identification of the failed
trace hosts below with the small-doubling hypothesis is asserted.

## Coupled semilinear norm axes and a uniform GL2 trace--determinant fusion obstruction

The conjecture remains unresolved. The new matrix theorem below excludes an
entire class of proposed constructions, but is NOT an upper bound for arbitrary
K44-free graphs and NOT a disproof of Erdős 714.

### Coupled semilinear quadratic norms (exact failure, not Lean)

An ordinary Frobenius twist in a separated quadratic norm sum can be removed
by an additive change of variables. A nonlinear separated sum instead has
large circle-by-circle grids. To avoid these immediate issues, a coupled
relation was derived on two copies of E x E, E=F_(q^2), q=3^m with m odd:

    f(x,y)=N(x)+N(y)+Tr(x^2*y^(2*sigma)), sigma=3^((m+1)/2),
    adjacency f(row+column)=1,
    extra edge condition: 1-4*N(y)^(2*sigma) is a NONZERO square in Fq,

where y is the SECOND COORDINATE OF THE SUM. The extra condition makes the
quadratic form in x anisotropic: its determinant is 1-4*N(y)^(2*sigma),
and -1 is nonsquare in Fq. Sigma restricts to a Tits-type Frobenius on Fq;
it is NOT asserted to have fixed field F3 or square equal to cubing on E.

The axis restriction (rows (x,0), columns (0,y)) is invariant under both
sign changes. Thus two distinct antipodal row pairs and two distinct
antipodal column pairs suffice for K44. This gives a structured test, without
enumerating arbitrary quadruples of the full graph.

Script `/tmp/semilinear_coupled_norm_axes.sage`, log
`/tmp/semilinear_coupled_norm_axes27.log`, finds a failure at q=27, sigma=9.
Field:

    E=F3[z]/(z^6+2*z^4+z^2+2*z+2).

Rows and columns below use base-three coefficient encoding, NOT discrete logs:

    rows [[243,0],[486,0],[157,0],[206,0]],
    cols [[0,279],[0,558],[0,243],[0,486]].

Equivalently the positive row representatives are z^5 and
z^4+2*z^3+2*z^2+z+1, and the positive column representatives are
z^5+z^3+z^2 and z^5. Both signs are used. The tested axis quotient has
364 row classes and 168 admissible nonzero column classes; each column has
14 row classes. The found two-by-two quotient rectangle therefore lifts
to the displayed actual K44.

Independent verifier `/tmp/verify_semilinear_coupled_norm.sage`, log
`/tmp/semilinear_coupled_norm_axes27.checked.log`, checks all sixteen ORIGINAL
norm/trace equations, both part injections, and explicit nonzero base-field
square roots of every determinant condition. JSON certificate:
`/tmp/semilinear_coupled_norm_axes27.json`.

It also checks every x-fiber at every admissible y. At q=27 there are 337
admissible y, each with exactly 28 x values. Each full bipartite part has
531441 vertices, each vertex degree is 9436, and the edge count is 5014677276.
These finite counts have the intended scale. No uniform degree theorem or

### A genuinely cubic generic elimination, and why it is insufficient

A separate matrix candidate used actual G,H in GL2(Fq), with

    tr(G^-1 H) = det(G^-1 H)^2 + det(G^-1 H),

and required the relative characteristic polynomial to be irreducible.
There is a valid INFORMAL three-root argument for independent row constraints:
write D=det(H), d_i=det(G_i). If the four linear forms
H -> tr(G_i^-1 H) are independent, then

    H=D^2*A+D*B

for uniquely determined matrices A,B. Since D!=0, its determinant equation is

    D*det(D*A+B)-1=0.

This is a nonzero polynomial of degree at most three, and H is uniquely
recovered from D. Therefore independent rows have at most three common
columns. This calculation was not separately formalized in Lean, and DOES
NOT HANDLE dependent rows.

The new theorem below proves that dependent rows are fatal to this approach.
As an exact illustration, the verifier above counts 18 elliptic determinant
values for this trace law over F27. Its characteristic discriminant is
D^4+2D^3+D^2-4D. Thus the generic bound cannot prove graph freeness even at
this one field size.

### All trace--determinant fusions on GL2 (Lean verified)

New `Submission/EllipticClassFusion.lean`, 512 lines, sole import
FormalConjecturesUtil. Clean compile with NO sorry or warnings; olean installed.
Log `/tmp/EllipticClassFusion.final4.log`. All twelve printed axiom audits use
only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

Vertices are actual `Matrix.GeneralLinearGroup (Fin 2) F`, not merely matrix
coordinates or class labels. For a finite set S of (determinant,trace) pairs,
the two-part graph has the ORIGINAL group edge condition

    (det(g^-1*h), tr(g^-1*h)) in S.

`Elliptic (d,t)` is defined by d!=0 and X^2-tX+d having NO FIELD ROOT.
This definition, and all the final theorems, work in EVERY characteristic;
there is no hidden odd-characteristic or nonsquare assumption.

For each elliptic pair (d,t), choose x different from 0,t and put

    k=x*(t-x)/d.

Then k is neither 0 nor 1. The latter follows because k=1 would make x a
root of X^2-tX+d. There are at least q-2 choices of x for each pair and
exactly q-2 possible nontrivial k's. `large_fiber` proves that some k has
at least |S| parameter pairs. This is finite pigeonhole counting, not a
character-sum estimate.

For every parameter in that fiber put y=t-x and use row and column matrices

    row(x,y) = diag(1/x,1/y),
    col(k,b) = [[1,b],[(1-1/k)/b,1]],  b in F*.

Their relative determinant and trace are xy/k=d and x+y=t. The column
determinant is 1/k, so every displayed matrix is invertible. `fiberRow_injective`
and `column_injective` check both embeddings, and `fiberCopy` constructs the
ACTUAL complete bipartite copy on the full fiber and F*. In particular:

* `not_free`: if r>=2, q>=r+1, and |S|>=r, an elliptic fusion is not Krr-free.
* `class_bound`: for q>=5, a K44-free elliptic fusion has |S|<=3.

There is also a full q-by-q grid for ANY split accepted pair. If x is a root
and y=t-x, then xy=d!=0. Use rows [[1,a],[0,1]] and columns [[x,b],[0,y]]
for arbitrary a,b in F. Every relative matrix has determinant d and trace t.
`splitCopy` checks this exact construction. Hence `free_pairs_elliptic` shows
that every nonzero-determinant pair accepted by a Krr-free fusion is elliptic
whenever q>=r.

The file also checks the real counts:

* `connectionEquiv` gives a bijection from the actual connection matrices to
  S x F x F*. For a fixed elliptic (d,t), the matrix is

      [[a,b],[(a*(t-a)-d)/b,t-a]],   a in F, b in F*.

  A root-free characteristic polynomial guarantees the off-diagonal entry b
  cannot vanish, so this parameterization misses no connection matrix.
* `connection_card`: |connection|=|S|*q*(q-1).
* Left and right neighbor equivalences verify regularity, even without
  inverse-closure of the connection set.
* `edge_count`: the ACTUAL undirected edge count is |GL2(F)|*|connection|.
* `fusion_edge_bound`: for ANY S with all determinants nonzero, q>=5, if its
  graph is K44-free, then e<=3*q^6. Ellipticity is NOT an assumption here.
* `fusion_critical_size_bound`: additionally q^7<=C*e implies q<=3*C.

This uniformly excludes the entire displayed trace--determinant fusion family
at the fourth-case scale, including the nonlinear trace law motivating it.
It does NOT exclude arbitrary edge thinnings that are no longer fusions,
arbitrary vertex selections, non-class-invariant Cayley graphs, or arbitrary
graphs. In particular it does not cover the old semilinear tr(M*M^sigma)

## SL2 semilinear additive cover: exact failures at q=8 and q=32

The main conjecture remains unresolved. This section records two counterexamples
TO A PROPOSED CONSTRUCTION, not to Erdős 714. No complete proof was submitted.

### Candidate and intended local argument

For q=2^k with k odd, sigma=2^((k+1)/2), let G=SL2(Fq), let tau be the
absolute binary trace, and put phi(M)=tr(M*M^sigma), with entrywise sigma.
The row vertices are (g,a) with tau(a)=0, the column vertices (h,b) with
tau(b)=1. The ORIGINAL adjacency requirements are

    phi(g^-1*h)=a+b,
    the characteristic polynomial of g^-1*h is irreducible over Fq.

Each part has (q^4-q^2)/2 vertices. The degree equals the number of elliptic
M in SL2(Fq) with tau(phi(M))=1. This is a growing-sheet additive cover of
a dense group graph, not an ordinary constant-sheet norm-graph cover.

There is a useful local INFORMAL calculation for unipotent rows U(t):

    U(t)=[[1,t],[0,1]], h=[[a,b],[c,d]], det(h)=1, c!=0,
    A=a/c, D=d/c, P=A^sigma+D, Q=A+D^sigma.

Then

    phi(U(t)*h)=phi(h)+c^(sigma+1)*(t*P+t^sigma*Q+t^(sigma+1)),
    phi(h)=c^(sigma-1)+c^(1-sigma)+c^(sigma+1)*P*Q.

The four-term semilinear root bound suggests that four distinct t's determine
c,P,Q from the sheet equations. The map (A,D)->(P,Q) has kernel
{(0,0),(1,1)} because sigma^2 is squaring. Thus these structured quadruples
have at most two common columns. This calculation is NOT a theorem about
arbitrary four group rows and has not been separately formalized in Lean.
The counterexamples below use rows outside a single unipotent coset.

## Reciprocal semilinear-arc codes: a uniform period obstruction and filtered failures

The original conjecture remains unresolved. This continuation produced a new
complete auxiliary Lean obstruction and exact certificates against a distinct
candidate. None is a disproof of Erdős 714.

### Candidate and scaling

Let q=2^k, k odd, F=Fq, K=F_(q^2), E=F_(q^4), sigma=2^((k+1)/2), and
choose z of degree four over F. Rows are a in E\K. Coordinates are (b,t) in
K x F, and a column includes an output c in F. Put

    X(t)=1+t*z+t^sigma*z^2+t^(sigma+1)*z^3,
    edge(a,(b,t,c)) iff Tr_(E/F)(X(t)/(a-b))=c.

Thus there are q^4-q^2 rows, q^4 columns, row degree q^3, and
(q^4-q^2)*q^3 actual incidences. Every denominator is nonzero because a is
outside K and b belongs to K. The intended ingredient was the already verified
semilinear four-term root bound: every four distinct t values give independent
vectors (1,t,t^sigma,t^(sigma+1)). This does NOT, by itself, control the free
K-valued offset b or all common neighborhoods.

This is distinct from the old unweighted trace-of-reciprocal Cayley graph and
from the weighted cubic reciprocal norm graph. Excluding all K rows avoids
the immediate old subfield-row circle template. It does not suffice.

### Uniform period obstruction (Lean verified)

The general translation-code graph has rows u in a binary ring G and columns
(v,c) in G x C, with f(u+v)=c. It has these verified results:

* `fiberCopy` embeds the actual Cayley graph of any output fiber.

The field application uses a subfield K of a characteristic-two field E,
an involution rho:E->E whose fixed field is exactly K, an outside element a,

    f(u)=T(1/(a+u)), u in K,

## Gluing additive Sidon norm-circle fibers: uniform norm-ratio obstruction

The original conjecture remains unresolved. This continuation investigated a
balancing mechanism with strong LOCAL freeness, rather than assuming that a
local common-neighbor bound survives union of many pieces. It produced a new
complete Lean theorem excluding the specified gluing, not arbitrary gluings
and not Erdős 714.

### Proposed family

Let q=2^m, m odd, E=F_(q^2), F=Fq, sigma(x)=x^(2q), and choose a noncube
D in E*. Then sigma squared is fourth powering, and its fixed field is F4.
For a in E* define the ACTUAL quotient weight

    r(a)=sigma(a)/a.

The proposed weight set W is the image of r, not a list containing three
representatives of every image element. By the usual cyclic-group exponent
calculation this image is the cube subgroup of E*, of size (q^2-1)/3. That
exact image/cardinality identification is not separately proved in the new
Lean file; its graph uses the exact image subtype throughout.

Vertices on each side are (x,s) in E x W. Put

    L_alpha(z)=z+alpha*sigma(z),
    edge((x,s),(y,t)) iff N_(E/F)(L_(D*s*t)(x+y))=1.

Each alpha=D*s*t is a noncube. Its additive map L_alpha is bijective. Every
local connection set is an additive-linear inverse image of a norm-one
circle, hence is Sidon: a nonzero pair sum determines the unordered pair.
Thus there are q+1 points in every local fiber, each part has
q^2*(q^2-1)/3 vertices, and the degree is (q+1)*(q^2-1)/3. These are the
intended q^4/q^3 scales. The exact counts were checked at q=8; the general
count formulas are mathematical deductions, not new Lean counting theorems.

The map (u,a) -> (u/a,r(a)) explains the need to quotient. Keeping all a would
retain three identical copies of a vertex and create artificial obstructions.
The new theorem is about the quotient graph itself, so it does not make this
mistake.

### Local Sidon property and the global grid (Lean verified)

New `Submission/SidonFiberGluing.lean`, sole import FormalConjecturesUtil.
Clean compile with no sorry or warnings, olean installed. Final log:
`/tmp/SidonFiberGluing.final.log`. All fourteen printed axiom audits use only
propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

Positive local results:
* `norm_circle_pair_unique`: over a characteristic-two field, if
  x*rho(x)=y*rho(y)=z*rho(z)=w*rho(w)=1, x!=y, and x+y=z+w, then x=z or x=w.
  Here rho is a ring endomorphism. The proof derives xy=zw and factors the
  resulting quadratic; no finite search or generic-position assumption.
* `form_add`, `form_injective`, `local_form_identity`, `local_form_injective`:
  every local L_(D*r(a)*r(b)) is additive and injective, since

      L_(D*r(a)*r(b))(z) = L_D(a*b*z)/(a*b).

* `local_fiber_pair_unique` transports the Sidon property to every local
  norm fiber. `quadratic_norm_formula` discharges its norm identity for
  actual finite fields of sizes q and q^2 and rho(x)=x^q, using
  `FiniteField.algebraMap_norm_eq_pow`.

These local facts STILL DO NOT establish global K44-freeness. The following
norm-ratio argument instead produces growing bicliques.

For every a in E* put

    c(a)=N(L_D(a)/a) in F*.

The additive nonsingularity of L_D guarantees c(a)!=0. Pigeonhole gives a
fiber of c(a) larger than 3*(r-1) whenever

    |F*|*3*(r-1) < |E*|.

There are at most three a with any prescribed r(a)=s: applying sigma to
sigma(a)=s*a gives

    a^3=s*sigma(s).

`ratio_cube`, `ratio_fiber_bound`, and `ratio_image_bound` prove these facts,
using the actual cubic root bound and counting all quotient multiplicities.
Thus the large c-fiber contains r DISTINCT QUOTIENT WEIGHTS.

Choose r such a values. For columns use DISTINCT b in the norm fiber N(b)=c.
All norm fibers have the same size; norm surjectivity and this cardinality
identity are discharged via Mathlib, not treated as implicit assumptions.
The actual quotient vertices are

    rows (0,r(a)), columns (1/b,r(b)).

Columns are injective already in their point coordinate, so there is no
threefold loss on the column side. The ORIGINAL kernel identity is

    L_(D*r(a)*r(b))(1/b) = L_D(a)/(a*b),

whose norm is c/N(b)=1. `kernel_identity`, `grid_edge`, and `gridCopy` check
this and both part embeddings. The result is a genuine biclique in `graph`,
not merely a coincidence of profiles in an enlarged host.

Main uniform theorems:
* `not_free_of_card`: the displayed unit-cardinality inequality gives Krr
  in the quotient graph, assuming sigma squared is fourth powering and
  L_D is nonsingular.
* `form_ne_zero`: nonsingularity follows if D*sigma(D) is a noncube.
* `noncube_product`: when q is 2 modulo 3 and sigma(x)=x^(2q), D noncube
  implies D*sigma(D) noncube. This is proved by an explicit exponent argument.
* `sigma_square_of_power`: the fourth-power identity follows from |E|=q^2.
* `quadratic_scale_not_free`: if |F|=q, |E|=q^2, and 3*(r-1)<q+1, the graph
  is not Krr-free, with the stated noncube-product hypothesis.
* `noncube_gluing_not_free`: for the specified power law, any noncube D and
  q>8, q=2 mod 3, give a K44.
* `binary_odd_not_free`: with q=2^(2*k+1), k>=2, sigma the ACTUAL iterated
  Frobenius `iterateFrobenius E 2 (2*k+2)`, all these hypotheses are discharged
  except the explicitly stated finite-field cardinalities and chosen noncube.
  Thus the entire intended odd-degree family fails from q=32 onward.

No theorem excludes arbitrary nonseparable dependence of the local linear
maps on both weights, arbitrary edge thinning, or arbitrary graphs.

### A possible stronger compatibility test (derived, not yet Lean)

For a GENERAL partial-translation graph with row labels A, column labels B,
additive point group G of characteristic two, and local connection sets
S_(a,b) in G, fix h!=0. Form a graph H_h whose vertices are the h-orbits
{x,x+h} with their labels. Join two orbits exactly when all four original
cross incidences hold. Equivalently x+y and x+y+h both belong to S_(a,b).

A C4 in H_h lifts to an ACTUAL K44 in the original graph. Therefore every
H_h must be C4-free in a successful construction. If all local fibers are
Sidon, each label-pair block in H_h is at most a matching. Exact counts are

    4*e(H_h)=|G|*sum_(a,b) |S_(a,b) intersect (S_(a,b)+h)|,
    4*sum_(h!=0)e(H_h)=|G|*sum_(a,b) |S_(a,b)|*(|S_(a,b)|-1).

At |G|~q^2, |A|,|B|~q^2, |S|~q, these shadows themselves must operate at
the C4 extremal scale. This is a useful compatibility requirement beyond
individual-fiber Sidon bounds. It is NOT sufficient for general K44-freeness:
it only excludes copies assembled from h-pairs, and no implication in the
opposite direction is claimed. This observation is not yet a Lean theorem.

### Binary bilinear thickening

`Submission/BilinearThickening.lean`, 106 lines, sole import
`FormalConjecturesUtil`. Clean compilation and installed olean. Log
`/tmp/BilinearThickening.final.log`; all three printed audits use only the
permitted axioms.

Graph on `(G x A) disjoint-union (G x B)`:

    (x,a) ~ (y,b) iff x+y+beta(a,b) belongs to S.

For biadditive beta and a nonzero u with beta(u,-) injective,

    |S|*|B| > |G|

forces K44 in characteristic two. The proof uses a collision of
`(s,b) -> s+beta(u,b)`, not quotient-group machinery. Its explicit grid is

    rows    (0,0), (s+t,0), (0,u), (s+t,u)
    columns (s,0), (t,0),   (s,v), (t,v),

where beta(u,v)=s+t and s,t are distinct connections. `gridCopy` checks the
sixteen incidences and both injections. `not_free_of_card` and
`connection_card_bound` discharge the collision/counting argument. The row
label type only needs an additive monoid; characteristic two is used in the

### Arbitrary nonlinear voltage tables, not just bilinear ones

`Submission/TranslatedFibers.lean`, 229 lines. Imports BilinearThickening,
BinaryLift, Packing. Clean compilation and installed olean. Log
`/tmp/TranslatedFibers.final.log`; all eight audits use permitted axioms.

The same graph is defined for COMPLETELY ARBITRARY beta:A x B -> G. If
there are two distinct row labels and |S|>=2, K44-freeness implies

    |S|*|B| <= |G|.

For a voltage rectangle define

    d=beta(a0,b0)+beta(a0,b1)+beta(a1,b0)+beta(a1,b1).

A row/column gauge transformation makes three corners zero and the fourth d.
If d=0 or d=s+t for two distinct s,t in S, an actual paired K44 results.
Pigeonhole on `(s,b) -> s+beta(a0,b)+beta(a1,b)` supplies such a rectangle.
If the two colliding S-values coincide, d=0 and a separate pair from S is
used. This is why no injectivity hypothesis on beta is needed.

### Exact growing-biclique partition: arbitrary edge thinning, every characteristic

`Submission/TranslatedFiberThinning.lean`, 155 lines. Imports TranslatedFibers
and BicliquePartition. Clean compilation, installed olean. Log

For ANY voltage table in ANY ring characteristic, fix z in G and b in B.
The actual vertices

    rows    (z-beta(a,b),a),  a in A,

form K_(|A|,|S|). Every original edge has the UNIQUE block index
`(z,b)=(x+beta(a,b),b)`. The blocks can share vertices, but do not share edges.

`blockCopy` and `block_partition` prove the copies and a bijection on actual

    t * e(H)^4 <= 10368 * e(host)^4.

`density_budget`: if H is nonempty and e(host)<=K*e(H), then

    t <= 10368*K^4.

Thus arbitrary edge deletions CANNOT retain a fixed positive fraction as
both the row-label size and connection-set size grow. This genuinely

### Exact reciprocal-evaluation block partitions (Lean verified)

`Submission/EvaluationInterchange.lean`, 145 lines. Import BicliquePartition.
Clean compilation, installed olean; log `/tmp/EvaluationInterchange.final.log`.
Five audits use only permitted axioms.

For arbitrary tables f:C x I -> A and g:D x J -> A, define the graph on
(C x J) disjoint-union (D x I) by

    (c,j) ~ (d,i) iff f(c,i)=g(d,j).

The block indexed by (j,i,a) is the ACTUAL complete graph between the two
nonempty evaluation fibers f(-,i)=a and g(-,j)=a, with their fixed coordinate
labels. `blockCopy` and `block_partition` prove a bijection on unordered
edges. Only nonempty blocks are indexed.

`density_bound` applies to every forbidden balanced Krr and arbitrary edge
subgraphs. `fourth_density_bound` says that if every nonempty fiber on both
sides has size at least t, then every K44-free subgraph H satisfies

    t*e(H)^4 <= 10368*e(host)^4.

`transposeIso` gives the second partition obtained by exchanging messages
and coordinates in both tables. No algebraic assumptions on the tables are
needed. These are not construction results for the conjecture.

### Arbitrary finite group actions and commutator covers (Lean verified)

`Submission/ReciprocalAction.lean`, 202 lines. Import EvaluationInterchange.
Clean compilation and installed olean; log `/tmp/ReciprocalAction.final.log`.
Eight printed audits use only the permitted axioms.

For ANY finite group Gamma acting on a nonempty finite set Omega, use
vertices (g,a), (h,b) and adjacency

    g • b = h • a.

Neither transitivity nor faithfulness is assumed.
* `transporterEquiv` identifies every nonempty transporter fiber with the
  actual stabilizer of its source point.
* `group_card_bound` uses orbit-stabilizer to prove
  |Gamma| <= |Omega|*|Stab(x)| for every x.
* `edges` checks e(host)=|Gamma|^2*|Omega|. Each row has |Gamma| neighbors.
* `fourth_power_bound`: take a smallest stabilizer t, apply the exact block
  density theorem, multiply by |Omega| and cancel |Gamma|. Every K44-free
  edge subgraph H obeys

      e(H)^4 <= 10368*|Gamma|^7*|Omega|^5.

* `normalized_bound`, for the ACTUAL total vertex count
  n=2|Gamma||Omega|:

      |Omega|^2*e(H)^4 <= 81*n^7.

* `critical_scale_budget`: n^7<=K*e(H)^4 forces |Omega|^2<=81*K.
  Thus even arbitrary edge thinning cannot attain a fixed n^(7/4) lower
  constant along a sequence with unbounded action-set size. This is an
  absolute exponent-scale obstruction, not merely a statement that the
  full graph has a biclique.

`commutatorGraph` explicitly uses voltage h^-1*g^-1*h*g, rather than relying
on a convention for commutator notation:

    b=(h^-1*g^-1*h*g) • a.

`sheetGauge` sends (g,a) to (g,g•a), and `commutatorIso` proves the exact
isomorphism with reciprocal evaluation. `commutator_normalized_bound`
transfers the same bound to EVERY K44-free edge subgraph of this permutation
cover. This completes and strengthens the old informal PGL2 degeneracy
observation. Bounded action sets are NOT excluded by the normalized bound.

### Free cubic-extension evaluations: Brown-incidence variant (exact tests)

To avoid transporter fibers, considered PGL2(F) acting on a degree-three
point theta in E/F. Its stabilizer is trivial: a nonidentity fractional
linear transformation fixing theta would give a quadratic equation for theta.
The big cell has unique parameters

    g(z)=A+B/(z+C),   A,C in F, B in F*,

represented by the actual invertible matrix [[A,A*C+B],[1,C]].
A graph vertex is (A,B,C,t), t in F, giving q^3(q-1) vertices per side.
Adjacency is

    Q(g(theta+s)+h(theta+t))=1,

where s,t are the opposite vertex tags. For the first variant,
Q(w)=Tr_(E/F)(w^2), q=7 mod 12, theta^3=d with d a noncube.

The intended degree scale is q^3. The reason for choosing this relation,
rather than equality, is that the fixed-tag blocks can use the standard
Brown K33-free quadratic relation in three dimensions. This positive local
observation is a mathematical motivation, not a new Lean theorem here.
For q=7 mod 12 the trace form in the Kummer basis is

    3*x0^2+6*d*x1*x2.

Its unit sphere has no affine isotropic lines (the relevant discriminant
class is nonsquare). This avoids the large affine-stabilizer grids of the
initial equality model. It also gives

    Q(a*theta+b)=3*b^2,

so the affine-cell sum plane has no unit values when 3 is nonsquare. The
scripts verify this identity and the nonsquare condition exactly.

The derived test fixes only the row family

    r_t=(0,1,t,t), t in F,

and evaluates ALL big-cell columns (A,B,C,s). It works with exact base-field
tables for the trace of 1/(theta+c), its square, and cross products. No random
search or floating-point approximation is used.

* q=7, d=2: no K44 in this one row family. This is NOT graph freeness.
* q=19, d=2: a genuine K44 is

    rows [(0,1,8,8),(0,1,13,13),(0,1,15,15),(0,1,18,18)],
    columns [(0,18,8,17),(0,18,17,8),(1,2,14,11),(1,5,0,1)].

  Part size 123462, modulus X^3+17.
* q=31, d=3:

    rows [(0,1,5,5),(0,1,6,6),(0,1,13,13),(0,1,16,16)],
    columns [(4,9,28,5),(11,16,30,25),(12,23,11,2),(18,13,0,3)].

  Part size 893730, modulus X^3+28.

reconstruct the matrices and fields, check nonzero determinants and all

These are finite exact certificates, not a uniform theorem in all field sizes.

### A cancellation in the cubic adjoint form: another finite failure

Also considered the genuinely different quadratic form

    Q_kappa(x0+x1*theta+x2*theta^2)=kappa*(x0^2-d*x1*x2),

with kappa nonsquare and -d square, retaining d noncube. It avoids the same
affine sum plane and has the appropriate nonsquare class for the Brown-type
local argument. The reason for this variant was the algebraic cancellation

    Q_kappa(1/(theta+c))=kappa*c/(c^3+d),

and more generally

    Q_kappa(A+B/(theta+c))
      =kappa*A^2+kappa*(2*A*B*c^2+B^2*c)/(c^3+d).

This is the constant coefficient of the cubic norm adjoint, up to scale.
The scripts check the reciprocal identity at every base-field value before
using it. It still does NOT yield the needed full common-neighbor bound.

The same r_t row family has no witness at q=7 (d=3,kappa=3) or q=19
(d=2,kappa=2). These passing restricted tests do not prove freeness. At q=31,
d=3,kappa=3, there is an actual copy:

    rows [(0,1,12,12),(0,1,14,14),(0,1,25,25),(0,1,28,28)],
    columns [(1,14,13,1),(4,28,29,6),(6,22,18,7),(7,10,0,17)].

### Independent norm coordinates: arbitrary nonlinear laws still lose density

A related attempted repair replaced a norm-graph coordinate by a nonlinear
permutation, hoping to make translation of the evaluation tag nontrivial.
That whole independent-coordinate model is already constrained by quadratic
code profiles; this application is now formalized rather than only inferred.

`Submission/QuadraticNormWeightLaw.lean`, 123 lines. Import
QuadraticProfileThinning. Clean compilation and installed olean. Log
`/tmp/QuadraticNormWeightLaw.final.log`; four permitted-axiom audits.

For ANY field F, ANY delta in F, and ANY k:U x V -> F, use

    rows ((a,u),alpha),       alpha in F,
    columns ((b,v),beta),     beta in F*,
    (a+b)^2-delta*k(u,v)^2=alpha*beta.

The law k can be arbitrary, nonlinear, and nonseparable. Excluding zero row
weights, choosing opposite square classes, or deleting any other vertices
or edges is covered by taking a subgraph on this ambient vertex set.

`codeIso` identifies the actual graph, with both parts and all weights, with
its quadratic code representation after exchanging the sides:

    alpha=((a+b)^2-delta*k(u,v)^2)/beta.

For fixed u this is quadratic in a, with all three coefficients explicit.
`code_quadratic` checks the expansion. Applying the already verified general
profile-thinning theorem gives, whenever |U|,|V|<=q^2, q=|F|,

    e(H)^4 <= 165888*q^27

for EVERY K44-free edge subgraph H. `critical_scale_budget` says that
q^7<=K*e(H) then forces q<=165888*K^4. No square-class or characteristic
assumptions are needed for this obstruction.

For example k((c,t),(C,s))=f(c+s)+f(C+t) is excluded for EVERY f, not merely
monomials or additive maps. This theorem does NOT automatically apply to
the free-action Möbius Brown/adjoint graphs above, which have no independent
output weight; those are only excluded at the recorded finite parameters.

## Norm-graph fiber Jacobian signs do not give a three-neighbor bound

This continuation examined a sign attached to the COMMON-NEIGHBOR SYSTEM,
not the previously failed edge discriminant sign. The main conjecture remains
unresolved, and Spec.lean was not changed.

### Normalization and the proposed shortcut

Normalize the first row of the cubic norm graph to (0,1). A common column
(y,b) has b=N(y), and, putting z=y^(-1), the other three equations become

    N(1+x_i*z)=a_i,  i=1,2,3.

One possible way to try to reduce six solutions to three is to keep a fixed
quadratic-character class of the Jacobian determinant of these three equations
in three Fq coordinates. This sign depends on the whole row quadruple, not
just on an edge; even a successful sign bound would require additional work
to define a graph. In fact the proposed sign bound itself is FALSE.

The recorded positive-edge-sign q7 certificate was examined first. Its fiber
has six simple points, and its Jacobian signs happen to split three-three.
A different old q7 certificate has four simple points split two-two and one
double point. Neither check establishes a general sign-count rule.

Artifacts: `/tmp/norm_jacobian_parity.sage`,
`/tmp/norm_jacobian_parity.log`, `/tmp/norm_jacobian_parity2.sage`,
`/tmp/norm_jacobian_parity2.log`.

### Two exact q13 counterexamples, independently verified

Use F=F13 and E=F[theta]/(theta^3+2*theta-2). Coordinates below are ordered
(1,theta,theta^2). Fix row points 0,1,theta,theta^2 in that order. The norm is

    N(u,v,w)=u^3+2*u*v^2+2*v^3-4*u^2*w-6*u*v*w
                 +4*u*w^2+4*v*w^2+4*w^3.

The actual partial derivatives are taken with respect to (u,v,w) in

    N(1+u,v,w),
    N(1+2*w,u-2*w,v),
    N(1+2*v,2*w-2*v,u-2*w).

Subtracting the target weights does not change this Jacobian.

NONSQUARE certificate:

    row weights: 1,8,1,10
    column points: (9,4,1), (0,9,12), (4,2,0), (11,11,10)
    column weights: 11,8,8,10
    inverse points: (9,4,2), (10,10,12), (3,12,7), (9,4,12)
    Jacobian determinants: 7,8,7,8 (all nonsquares).

SQUARE certificate:

`/tmp/norm_jacobian_fibers.sage` computes complete fibers for the fixed points

nonzero Jacobian character (six of each character). This is an exact test of

## Opposite weight rows and polarized quintics: two uniform norm-graph obstructions

This continuation returned to the exceptional-quintic root bound and looked
for a different incidence relation. It produced two uniform construction
obstructions and a new positive circle/character-sum lemma, but NO proof or
disproof of Erdős 714. Spec.lean was not changed.

### Arbitrary opposite rows in characteristic three (Lean verified)

New `Submission/NegativeRowNorm.lean`, 109 lines, imports CharThreeNorm.
Clean compile, installed olean, three permitted-axiom audits. Log:
`/tmp/NegativeRowNorm.final.log`. The dependency CharThreeNorm.olean was also
rebuilt; log `/tmp/CharThreeNorm.refresh.log`.

Let H:U×V->F be COMPLETELY ARBITRARY, F any finite characteristic-three field.
Suppose there are two row labels a,A with

    H(A,b)=-H(a,b) for every b,

and the row H(a,-) attains every NONZERO field value. Then an irreducible
Artin-Schreier coordinate norm graph

    N_d(x+y)=H(a,b),  H(a,b)!=0

contains K44. Zero-norm edges are explicitly excluded in the Lean graph.
Neither label type needs to be finite. The surjectivity hypothesis need not
include zero. The two opposite labels are supplied by the hypotheses, not
assumed present in an arbitrary weight restriction.

Choose c outside the Artin-Schreier image and d=-c^3-c. Then d!=0 and
X^3-X-d is irreducible. Choose column labels b,B satisfying

    H(a,b)=d, H(a,B)=-c^3.

Opposition supplies H(A,b)=-d and H(A,B)=c^3. The copy is

    rows:  (0,a), (1,a), (-1,a), (theta,A)
    cols:  (theta,b), (theta+1,b), (theta-1,b), (c-theta,B).

All original norm identities, nonzero edge values, and vertex injections
are proved. `parameter_not_free` only requires the four displayed table
values, making it usable without global opposition.

`opposite_rows_obstruction` packages the finite-field existence result.
`additive_rows_obstruction` specializes to H:U ->+ (V -> F): additivity is
required ONLY in the row label, not in the column label. Thus every
semifield-style bilinear weight law with a nonzero surjective row is covered
when both a and -a are retained. This is substantially broader than ordinary
multiplication or the specific earlier Frobenius-twisted laws.

Scope: arbitrary edge thinning, non-negation-stable row restrictions, and
laws without an opposite pair are NOT excluded. The theorem gives an
irreducible coordinate presentation; it does not construct an isomorphism
from every preselected cubic extension to that presentation.

### Polarized fifth-power weights: a different candidate

The next candidate was

    H(a,b)=(a+b)^5-a^5-b^5,
    N_(E/F)(x+y)=H(a,b), [E:F]=3, char F=3.

In characteristic three,

    H(a,b)=-a*b*(a+b)*(a-b)^2.

This is not the previously excluded law (a+b)^5. The new opposite-row
obstruction cannot simply be applied: H(a,b)+H(-a,b) vanishes only at
b=0,+/-a, and H vanishes at those nonzero candidate intersections too.

A DERIVED symmetric interpolation test nevertheless gives K46. Use scalar
row points and weights t in {u,-u,v,-v}. Set U=u^2,V=v^2 and

    Q(T)=(T^2-U)*(T^2-V),
    P(T)=T^3+(1-U-V)*T^2-T+U*V.

Then

    H(T,1)+Q(T)=P(T),
    H(T,-1)-Q(T)=-P(-T).

If P is irreducible and the four row values are distinct, the three negatives
of its conjugate roots, with weight 1, and the three conjugate roots, with
weight -1, are six common columns. All edge values are nonzero because P
has no base-field root.

Exact initial certificates:

* q27, F=F3[z]/(z^3+2z+1), u=z, v=z+2:
  P=T^3+(z^2+2z)*T^2+2T+2z^2+2.
* q243, F=F3[z]/(z^5+2z+1), u=z, v=z^2:
  P=T^3+(2z^4+2z^2+1)*T^2+2T+z^2+2z.

### Positive circle parameter lemma (Lean verified)

New `Submission/NormCircleTrace.lean`, 264 lines, sole import
FormalConjecturesUtil. Clean compile and installed olean. Three permitted-
axiom audits, log `/tmp/NormCircleTrace.final.log`.

`exists_circle_parameter` proves that for ANY finite characteristic-three
field F of order 3^m, m>=3 ODD, there are u,v in F such that

    u^2+v^2=1,
    -u^2*v^2 is outside {x^3-x : x in F}.

In particular u,v are nonzero; and u^2!=v^2 follows because -1 is nonsquare.
This is a genuine general arithmetic lemma, independent of the failed graph.

Proof: in an algebraic closure choose a primitive (q+1)-st root zeta. For
w=zeta^j, form d(w)=w^4+w^(-4)+1 and tau_m(z)=sum_{i<m}z^(3^i). Exact finite
character orthogonality gives

    sum_{j=0}^q (zeta^j)^(-4) * tau_m(d(zeta^j)) = 1.

The necessary frequency exclusions are proved as `not_dvd_positive` and
`not_dvd_negative`:

    q+1 does not divide 4*3^i-4 for 0<i<m,
    q+1 does not divide 4*3^i+4 for 0<=i<m.

The positive i=0 frequency contributes q+1=1 in characteristic three.
Thus some w has nonzero trace. Choose iota^2=-1 and define

    u=-(w+w^(-1)), v=iota*(w-w^(-1)).

Since w^q=w^(-1) and iota^q=-iota, both u,v are fixed by q-Frobenius.
`pow_fixed_mem_range` descends them to F using the splitting and root set of
X^q-X. Direct identities give u^2+v^2=1 and -u^2*v^2=d(w). Telescoping the
Artin-Schreier trace excludes d(w) from the base-field AS image.

The proof uses actual roots of unity in AlgebraicClosure F, not an assumed
quadratic extension or a postulated character-sum estimate.

## Cubic norm/trace shear: every nonzero retained weight fails

New `Submission/CubicTraceShear.lean` (253 lines), importing CharThreeNorm and
AffineSlices. Clean compile and installed olean; six permitted-axiom audits
in `/tmp/CubicTraceShear.final.log`. This is a construction obstruction, NOT
a disproof of Erdős 714.

The investigated code was

    f_(a,x)(t) = k(a) + Tr(tx) + N(x+a*t)

in a characteristic-three cubic extension. On scalar coordinates its profile
is cubic, so the previous quadratic-profile obstruction does not directly
apply. Nevertheless the full code contains K44 even at any ONE fixed nonzero
weight a, with arbitrary offset k, and after deleting zero message points
and zero coordinates.

For theta^3-theta=d, any nonzero d,a, put l=(a^2*d)^(-1) and choose
s outside {0,1,-1}. Use row points

    a*l*s, a*l*(s+1), a*l*(s-1), a*l*(s+theta)

and coordinates

    l*(theta-s), l*(theta+1-s), l*(theta-1-s), l*(d-theta-s).

The common symbols are k+a*l^2 at the first three coordinates and
k+a*l^2+a^3*l^3*d^3 at the fourth. All row/coordinate points are nonzero;
both four-element parametrizations are injective. This works over every
finite characteristic-three field with at least four elements (hence q>=9).

## Trace-one Gold code: scalar-line obstruction and an existing nonzero certificate

Investigated the previously untested trace-one restriction of

    f_x(y)=Tr_(E/F)(x^3*y+x*y^3),
    E=F_(q^4), F=F_q, char(F)=2, Tr_(E/F)(y)=1.

The exponent here is specifically sigma=2, not every Gold exponent.
This continuation did NOT produce a new Lean theorem or settle Erdős 714.

### Uniform scalar-line derivation (informal algebra)

Let K=F_(q^2), q>=4. Choose d in K* with d^3 not in F; a multiplicative
generator works since q+1>3. Let t2=Tr_(K/F) and put

    U=d^(-3)/t2(d^(-3)),  W=d*U^3.

Then t2(U)=1, t2(d^3*U)=0, and W is not in F. The last claim follows from
W=d^(-8)/t2(d^(-3))^3 and injectivity of the eighth-power Frobenius.
For each v in K with

    t2(W*(1+v))=0,  Tr_(K/F2)(v)=1,

the polynomial Y^2+U*Y+U^2*v is irreducible over K and has two roots in E.
There are exactly q/2 such v. Indeed the first equation cuts out an affine
F-line in K. Its direction is W^(-1)*F, and the absolute trace is nonzero
on that direction because t2(W^(-1)) is nonzero. Thus half the q points
have absolute trace one.

The resulting q distinct roots y satisfy

    Tr_(E/F)(y)=1,
    Tr_(E/F)(d^3*y)=0,
    Tr_(E/F)(d*y^3)=0.

Consequently all q rows x=t*d, t in F, agree with symbol ZERO at all q
coordinates. This is a K_(q,q) in the full evaluation graph, not a freeness
argument. Crucial scope: deleting zero-symbol columns removes this particular
copy, so the uniform derivation alone does not exclude that modification.

Exact checks of the prescribed construction (not arbitrary graph searches):
`/tmp/gold_trace_one_slice.sage`, logs
`/tmp/gold_trace_one_slice{4,8,16,32}.log`. They verify the exact q/2 count,
all q^2 original trace equations, trace-one conditions, and injections.

### The old q8 certificate already avoids zero symbols

Revisiting `/tmp/gold_quartic_slice8.log` showed that the A=B=C=1 certificate
from the older quartic Gold investigation already has trace-one columns.
The four row roots in K obey x^3+x+x^q=1. For every quadratic pair used there,
U=y+y^(q^2) has t2(U)=1 and y^3+y^(3*q^2)=1. Thus the common code symbol is
one, not zero. The new q8 script independently rechecks all 16 original code
equalities, all coordinate trace-one conditions, and both injections.
This is only a finite q8 obstruction to the nonzero-symbol modification;
no all-q or all-exponent claim is made.

## Tensor-code review: a conditional first-moment barrier (Lean verified)

New `Submission/TensorSampling.lean`, sole import FormalConjecturesUtil.
Clean compile and installed olean. All five printed axiom audits use only
propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Log `/tmp/TensorSampling.final.log`.

This continuation reviewed sparse code restrictions of tensor products, not
only positive-density selections. The previous even_power_edge_bound does
NOT exclude every sparse restriction. No suitable code was constructed.

The new results isolate the arithmetic limit of a PARTICULAR first-moment
certificate. They are not universal bounds on free graphs, arbitrary code
selections, or actual random-copy counts. Every monomial assumption below
is explicitly present in the theorem type.

* first_moment_bound: for r>=2, n,p>0,

      n^(2*r)*p^(r*r) <= n^2*p

  implies

      (n^2*p)^(r+1) <= n^(2*r).

* copy_budget_bound: same conclusion if an explicit budget b is bounded
  below by the copy monomial and above by the edge monomial. No assertion
  that every tensor code has this lower bound is made.

* first_moment_bound_with_constant permits

      n^(2*r)*p^(r*r) <= K*(n^2*p)

  and concludes

      (n^2*p)^((r+1)*(r-1)) <= K*n^((2*r)*(r-1)).

  This accommodates fixed multiplicative losses without using real roots.

* critical_size_budget: if n,c>0, e>=0,

      c*n^(2*r-1) <= e^r,  e^(r+1) <= n^(2*r),

  then c^(r+1)*n^(r-1)<=1. Thus the unit first-moment certificate and the
  target scale cannot both persist at unbounded orders with fixed c.

* fourth_case_size_budget: the explicit r4 specialization c^5*n^3<=1.

The nonnegativity of e is an explicit hypothesis: the odd-power bound alone
would not exclude negative e, while the target fourth-power bound is
insensitive to sign. This was corrected during development before the final
clean compile. No auxiliary sorry remains.

The key identity is

    (n^2*p^(r+1))^(r-1)*(n^2*p) = n^(2*r)*p^(r*r).

Cancelling the positive edge monomial gives the normalized first-moment
bound. Combining powers in the target inequality leaves exactly n^(r-1).
These are elementary arithmetic lemmas, not a new extremal construction.

## Projective Hermitian evaluation on unital coordinates: review only

A further positive-construction attempt used q^3 affine unital points as
coordinates and nonisotropic affine projective points x=(1,s,t) over F_(q^2)
as messages. The proposed symbol was

    f_x(u)=N(h(x,u))/h(x,x),
    h(x,u)=bar(u0)+s*bar(u1)+t*bar(u2),
    h(x,x)=1+N(s)+N(t) != 0.

This does NOT evade the earlier HermitianProfiles obstruction merely because
the coordinate set is a unital. For a fixed s, put
A0=bar(u0)+s*bar(u1). The symbol-b equation expands as

    (N(u2)-b)*N(t) + Tr(A0*u2*bar(t))
      + N(A0)-b*(1+N(s)) = 0.

This is exactly the previously verified arbitrary-coefficient Hermitian
slice model. The denominator condition is an allowed arbitrary selection of
rows in each slice; restriction of u to any q^3 coordinate vectors is an
allowed column selection. There are q^2 row slices and q^4 coordinate-symbol
columns. Thus that existing model bound would give at most 18*q^6 edges if
free, rather than the proposed q^7 scale. The count of nonisotropic affine
messages is at least q^4-q^3-q^2, by the degree-(q+1) bound on each norm fiber.
The resulting edge lower bound is q^7-q^6-q^5 and contradicts 18*q^6 once
q>=20. This paragraph is a mathematical specialization; a new bundled
projective/unital Lean application was NOT added or claimed.

No positive construction or negation of the conjecture resulted. Spec.lean
was not modified and still has its one r>=4 sorry. No proof was submitted.

## Quadratic cone charts: arbitrary edge-thinning obstruction (Lean verified)

New `Submission/QuadraticConeThinning.lean`, importing the already checked
QuadraticProfileThinning file. Clean compile and installed olean; all six
printed axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Log
`/tmp/QuadraticConeThinning.final.log`. No sorry remains in this auxiliary file.

### Motivation and scope

The characteristic-three reduction of the earlier degree-five threefold
chart was investigated as a possible source of exceptional-quintic common-
neighbor equations. Its explicit chart is

    v(a,b,c)=(1,a,b,c,b^2-a*c,a^2*c-a*b^2-b*c,c^2+b^3-a*b*c).

It is quadratic in c at fixed a,b. This is fatal to the bilinear cone
incidence model before any quintic-elimination argument is needed. The new
result applies to this explicit chart and arbitrary linear column
functionals; it is NOT a classification theorem for all threefolds or an
assertion about an unformalized global projective boundary.

### Abstract weighted quadratic theorem

weightedGraph f has rows indexed by C and opposite vertices ((x,t),s), with
adjacency

    s * f(c,(x,t)) = 1.

If f is quadratic in t, there are <=q^2 slices x, and |C|<=q^4, then every
K44-free edge subgraph H satisfies

    e(H)^4 <= 165888*q^27.

`weighted_quadratic_thinning` proves this by the actual vertex equivalence
s -> s^(-1), leaving all other coordinates fixed. Pulling H back gives an
edge subgraph of the quadratic-profile CODE host. Scale zero causes no gap:
it has no edges in weightedGraph; inv_weight_imp proves the required
implication without assuming nonzero scales silently. Freeness and edge
counts are transported by the actual graph equivalence. Thus arbitrary edge
thinning, not just induced vertex restrictions, is covered.

### Checked chart application

* chart_expansion writes v=v0+c*v1+c^2*v2 explicitly.
* quadrics and chart_quadrics_zero verify all five equations

      -x2^2+x1*x3+x0*x4,
      x2*x3+x1*x4+x0*x5,
      x3^2+x2*x4-x0*x6,
      x3*x4+x2*x5+x1*x6,
      -x4^2+x3*x5+x2*x6.

  These match the earlier reduced quadrics in characteristic three. The
  displayed chart identities themselves hold over every field; the final
  theorem does not require characteristic three.
* conePoint_injective proves that nonzero scalar multiples of v have an
  injective parametrization. The obstruction is not due to accidental
  duplicate geometric vertices.
* coneCode_quadratic and scaled_chart_equation verify evaluation by arbitrary
  column functionals L(c):F^7 ->_F F, including every bilinear pairing with
  arbitrarily selected column points. The geometric equation
  L(c)(s*v(a,b,t))=1 is identified with the weighted graph equation.
* cone_thinning gives the fourth-power bound for every free edge subgraph
  with at most q^4 indexed columns. Any subset of the chart rows is included
  by deleting edges incident with omitted rows.
* cone_size_budget: q^7<=K*e(H) forces q<=165888*K^4.

Thus this particular degree-five chart cannot give the fourth-case critical
scale even by arbitrary edge repair. The exceptional-quintic ingredient
still has no successful graph application. None of these theorems bounds
arbitrary K44-free graphs, and none negates the original conjecture.

## Random finite-group covers: exact counts and conditional deletion budget

New `Submission/RandomVoltage.lean`, 240 lines, sole import
FormalConjecturesUtil. Clean compilation and installed olean; log
`/tmp/RandomVoltage.final.log`. All eight printed axiom audits use only
propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry or native_decide.

This continuation considered density-preserving conversion of a weaker
forbidden-biclique host into a diagonal-free graph. The existing growing-grid
thinning obstructions explicitly do NOT apply to the ordinary cubic norm
graph. No new deterministic extraction theorem was established. The concrete
new result concerns the exact uniform RANDOM-cover distribution.

### Exact noncommutative counts

Use rows Option I and columns Option J, with none as the anchor. For an
arbitrary finite GROUP Gamma, define flatness by

    M(i,j)=M(i,none)*M(none,none)^(-1)*M(none,j).

`flatEquiv` gives an explicit equivalence of flat matrices with normalized
row potentials and all column potentials. `Lifts M` consists of actual sheet
assignments (a,b) satisfying b(j)=a(i)*M(i,j).

* `liftsEquiv`: if M is flat, Lifts M is equivalent to Gamma, by the sheet
  on the distinguished row. Otherwise there are no lifts (`flat_of_lift`,
  `card_lifts`). Thus a flat rectangle contributes L lifts, not just one.
* `allLiftsEquiv`: jointly choosing M and a lift is equivalent to freely
  choosing both sets of vertex sheets; then M(i,j)=a(i)^(-1)*b(j) is forced.
* `card_flat`, `card_flat_mul`, `flat_fraction`: an r-by-s rectangle has
  L^(r+s-1) flat labelings among L^(r*s) labelings. Flat probability is
  exactly L^(-(r-1)*(s-1)).
* `sum_card_lifts`, `sum_card_lifts_mul`, `average_lifts`: exact expected
  number of lifts is L/L^((r-1)*(s-1)).
* `fourth_average_lifts`: for r=s=4 this is 1/L^8.

These are finite counting equalities, including exact rational averages.
No commutativity assumption, asymptotics, numerical enumeration, or heuristic
independence assumption among overlapping rectangles is used. The file
counts one indexed rectangle; it does not silently assert a theorem counting
all base copies in a particular norm graph. The connection with actual
biclique copies and injective projection is in the earlier Voltage.lean.

### Conditional monomial budget

`budget_requires_sheets` assumes r>=2, q>0, L>=0, and explicitly

    q^(r*r) <= q^(2*r-1)*L^((r-1)*(r-1)).

This is the cleared-denominator elementary deletion budget for base copy
scale q^(r*r), base edge scale q^(2*r-1), and the exact lift expectation.
It proves q<=L.

`budget_alteration_scale` then proves

    (q^(2*r-1)*L)^(r+1) <= (q^r*L)^(2*r).

Thus this particular unit-constant first-moment certificate yields the usual
alteration exponent 2*r/(r+1); in the fourth case e^5<=n^8, not the target
7/4 exponent. A base-copy lower bound is NOT proved for every proposed host,
and the monomial hypothesis is NOT asserted for every deterministic cover.
The new results therefore do not exclude every bounded-sheet labeling,
every smarter alteration procedure, or ordinary norm-graph edge thinning.

Technical note: specializing the finite function sum directly to I=J=Fin 3
caused expensive definitional reduction during elaboration. The checked
fourth-case statement instead takes arbitrary I,J with card I=card J=3;
this is mathematically the same four-row/four-column count and avoids that
elaboration issue.

### General trace-slice criterion (Lean verified)

New `Submission/QuadraticTraceSlice.lean`, 230 lines, sole import
FormalConjecturesUtil. Clean compile, installed olean; log
`/tmp/QuadraticTraceSlice.final.log`. All eight printed axiom audits use
only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry or native_decide.

Namespace Erdos714QuadraticTraceSlice works over ANY commutative ring E,
with a ring endomorphism tau and arbitrary function f:E->E. Write

    trace2(z)=z+tau(z), halfTrace(z)=z+tau^2(z),
    trace4(z)=trace2(halfTrace(z)).

* `row_reduction`: if x and f(x) are tau^2-fixed, then the original polarized
  four-term trace reduces to trace2(f(x)*halfTrace(y)+x*halfTrace(f(y))).
* `profile_identity`: the stated row/column profiles imply that this equals
  trace2(C*halfTrace(y)). Its hypotheses include tau^2(B)=B and tau^4(y)=y.
  Cancellation follows from trace2(x*tau(u)-tau(x)*u)=0 when x,u are
  tau^2-fixed. No characteristic-two assumption is needed.
* `profileCopy`: an actual K_(r,s) copy in the bipartite trace graph, with
  explicit row and column embeddings. Side injections are checked, and the
  sum-type vertex set prevents silently identifying the two parts.
* `not_free_of_profiles`, `monomial_not_free`: freeness obstruction for
  any common-profile injections, specializing f(x)=x^d. Root existence,
  column existence, and distinctness are all explicit hypotheses; this
  theorem does NOT assert that every choice of A,B,C has enough solutions.

The same file's namespace Erdos714MonomialScaling proves an ACTUAL graph

c=u^(d*d-1), u!=0, the relabeling

### Singer translates of a Denniston maximal arc (exact finite failures)

This was a new proposed family, not the previously tested Singer unitals.
Let q=2^m, Q=q^2, E=F_(Q^3), K=F_Q, and take a primitive alpha in E. Use the
K-basis 1,alpha,alpha^2. Choose nu in K with absolute trace one, so that
A^2+A*B+nu*B^2 is anisotropic over K. The affine arc consists of projective
points

    [A+B*alpha+alpha^2],  A,B in K,
    A^2+A*B+nu*B^2 in F_q.

Its size is (q-1)*(Q+1)+1. In the Singer quotient E*/K*, of order
v=Q^2+Q+1, write S for its point set. The bipartite graph has rows and columns
in this cyclic quotient and incidence c-r in S. It has v vertices per side
and degree (q-1)*(Q+1)+1, giving the intended q^4/q^3 scale. These counts
motivated the model but do not establish freeness.

Exact script `/tmp/denniston_singer.sage` constructs the arc from actual
field coordinates and checks its cardinality. It normalizes the first row
to zero, forms common neighborhoods with a second row, and hashes four-point
intersections for two further distinct rows. This yields copies immediately
for the specified first difference one at both tested sizes:

* q4, Q16, v273, degree52:

  Rows [0,1,37,60], columns [463,1570,2992,3214].

Row/column labels here are EXPONENTS in the Singer quotient: i means
[alpha^i]. By contrast, alpha,nu and the stored A,B,lambda witnesses are

## Positive matrix recovery arguments: cubic and semilinear, with their hypotheses checked

This continuation revisited the positive root-count tools rather than testing

### Cubic recovery (Lean verified)

New `Submission/MatrixCubicRecovery.lean`, 176 lines, sole import
FormalConjecturesUtil. Complete, installed olean. Final log:
`/tmp/MatrixCubicRecovery.final.log`. All five printed audits use only
propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. It does not import Spec.

For 2x2 matrices A,B, define mixed(A,B) by

    det(t*A+B)=det(A)*t^2+mixed(A,B)*t+det(B).

`pencil_det` checks the identity. Let e be an explicitly supplied linear
EQUIVALENCE from 2x2 matrices to F^4. Suppose an invertible H satisfies

    e(H)=D^2*u+D*v, D=det(H).

Then `recover` proves H=D^2*A+D*B with A=e^-1(u), B=e^-1(v). Taking its
determinant and cancelling NONZERO D gives

    D*det(D*A+B)-1=0.

The polynomial is

    det(A)*T^3+mixed(A,B)*T^2+det(B)*T-1.

Its constant term is -1, so it is never the zero polynomial; `cubic_ne_zero`
and `cubic_degree` prove this explicitly. `determinant_is_root` checks the
cancellation. `solution_card_le_three` proves recovery makes determinant
injective on the solution set, then bounds its cardinality by three.
Neither nonzero elimination nor injective parametrization is assumed merely
from a generic degree count.

`constraintMap R` is the ACTUAL linear map H -> (tr(R_i*H))_i. The theorem
`trace_det_common_bound` applies the preceding argument to

    tr(R_i*H)=det(R_i*H)^2+det(R_i*H), for all four i,

assuming constraintMap R is bijective and H is invertible. For a relative
matrix graph the R_i are the inverse row matrices. This formalizes the
valid independent-row calculation recorded earlier for trace--determinant
fusions. It does NOT handle dependent rows and does not contradict the
previous EllipticClassFusion obstruction.

### Size limit for using only independent rows (Lean verified)

In the same file, `same_first_row_not_injective` proves that four matrices
with a common first row (a,b) cannot give an injective constraintMap. If
(a,b)!=(0,0), the explicit nonzero kernel matrix is

    [[b,0],[-a,0]].

The zero-first-row case uses [[1,0],[0,0]]. All trace and nonzero assertions
are checked, in arbitrary characteristic.

`independent_rows_card_bound` proves: if R:V->Mat2(F), F and V finite, and
EVERY injectively indexed four rows gives an injective constraintMap, then

    |V| <= 3*|F|^2.

The proof pigeonholes the first-row pair and constructs the forbidden
four-row slice from a fiber of size at least four. Thus keeping only rows
for which the full-rank argument is always applicable cannot retain a
positive fraction of a q^4-row family. This is a limitation of that precise
strategy, NOT a bound for arbitrary K44-free graphs or every possible
construction using matrices. It does not exclude handling dependent rows
by a different argument.

### Conditional semilinear recovery (Lean verified)

New `Submission/SemilinearMatrixRecovery.lean`, 95 lines, imports the checked
SemilinearRoots and MatrixCubicRecovery files. Complete, no warnings, installed
olean; log `/tmp/SemilinearMatrixRecovery.final.log`. All four audits use only
the three permitted axioms. SemilinearRoots was refreshed and installed too,
log `/tmp/SemilinearRoots.refresh.log`.

Let sigma:F->F have fixed field {0,1}. If

    e(H)=D*sigma(D)*u+D*v, D=det(H)!=0,

then H=D*(sigma(D)*A+B), A=e^-1(u), B=e^-1(v). The theorem REQUIRES

    det(A)=0.

Under that explicit singular-leading-matrix hypothesis, taking determinants
gives the four-term equation

    mixed(A,B)*D*sigma(D)+det(B)*D-1=0.

`determinant_equation` proves it, and `solution_card_le_three` uses the
already verified four-term semilinear root bound plus determinant recovery.
Again, the coefficient of the constant term is nonzero, and the parameter
is injective on the actual solution set.

`trace_det_common_bound` specializes to the law

    tr(R_i*H)=det(R_i*H)*sigma(det(R_i*H))+det(R_i*H).

The recovered leading vector has coordinates det(R_i)*sigma(det(R_i)). Its
inverse image under the row-constraint equivalence must have determinant
zero; this rank hypothesis remains in the theorem type. There is NO claim
that arbitrary rows, ordinary ellipticity, or the Tits exponent imply it.
There is currently no qualifying balanced family to which this lemma can be
applied. A full trace--determinant fusion is in any case already excluded by
the earlier uniform obstruction.

accepted trace is zero. Such a class has q-1 parameters. Thus the displayed
exact sum and the proposed sharp density formula below were NOT established.

For an accepted elliptic set S of trace--determinant pairs, its grid with
parameter k has m_k rows and q-1 columns. The existing parametrization gives

    sum_k m_k = (q-2)*|S|.

For each accepted pair separately there are exactly q-2 row parameters

facts suggest that translating/conjugating ALL grids gives a uniform cover
of the union of the class-edge orbits, even though a single grid or a single
class does not cover all accepted pairs uniformly.

Combining such a rigorously bundled cover with the UNBALANCED KST estimate
and the concavity estimate for sum m_k^(3/4) would suggest the density bound

    e(free thinning)/e(full elliptic fusion)

The multi-orbit averaging multiplicities and the unbalanced estimate still
need formal verification before this can be asserted as a Lean theorem.
Split pairs, particularly scalar relative matrices versus nontrivial Jordan
matrices, require separate treatment. No blanket statement about arbitrary
edge thinnings of all trace--determinant fusions is claimed here.

## Asymmetric quadratic/quartic recovery: valid local bounds, but a rank-three fiber copy

The original conjecture is still unresolved. This continuation investigated
a new asymmetric model suggested by the verified cubic recovery argument.
It is NOT the earlier GL2 trace--determinant fusion. The model passes several
meaningful local tests, now proved in Lean, but a derived dependent-row test
finds K44. No candidate construction has been promoted to a conjecture proof.

### The new relation and why it was considered

Let q=3^m with m odd, E=F_(q^4), K=F_(q^2), and write bar(x)=x^(q^2). Define

    n2(x)=x*bar(x),
    Q(x)=n2(x)+n2(x)^q,
    N(x)=n2(x)^(q+1),
    B(x,y)=Tr_(E/Fq)(x*bar(y)).

Q is a nondegenerate quadratic form on the four-dimensional Fq-space E,
N is the quartic norm, and B is the polar form of Q. Use TWO copies of the
vertex set on which Q(x) and N(x) are both nonzero squares. The asymmetric
row-column relation is

    B(x,y)=Q(x)^2*Q(y)^2+Q(x)*N(x)*Q(y).

It must not be described as a symmetric unipartite relation.

For four independent row constraints, write D=Q(y). The equations recover

    y=D^2*A+D*B0,

for uniquely determined A,B0. Applying Q and cancelling D!=0 gives the
nonzero cubic

    D*Q(D*A+B0)-1=0.

Thus this independent-row part genuinely has at most three common columns.
Unlike the earlier determinant-only calculation, it applies to the actual
quadratic norm-trace form here.

There are also two valid ray properties in characteristic three with -1
nonsquare. Put A=Q(x), N0=N(x), D=Q(y), L=B(x,y).

* A column scalar t!=0 satisfies the incidence iff

      t^3+(N0/(A*D))*t=L/(A^2*D^2).

  If A,N0,D are nonzero squares, the coefficient N0/(A*D) is a nonzero
  square. The additive cubic t^3+a*t is injective: a nonzero kernel element
  would square to -a, making -1 square. Over a finite field it is bijective.
  Hence every nonorthogonal allowed column ray has EXACTLY one incident
  nonzero scalar. An orthogonal ray has none.

* A nonzero row scalar t satisfies

      t*L=t^4*A^2*D^2+t^6*A*N0*D.

  Dividing by t*A*N0*D gives

      t^5+(A*D/N0)*t^3-L/(A*N0*D)=0.

  This is precisely the previously proved exceptional quintic, so there are
  at most three such row scalars. This argument needs nonzero A,N0,D, not
  an unsupported bound on arbitrary sextics.

These facts did NOT settle dependent non-collinear row configurations.

### The exact dependent-row failure at q27

Use the fixed norm fiber n2(x)=-1. In characteristic three every such row
has Q(x)=N(x)=1, hence it satisfies both vertex restrictions. Four affinely
coplanar points in this fiber with linear rank three have a nonzero affine
linear dependence. For all four rows both right-hand-side coefficient
profiles are constant, so the fourth row equation is redundant.

The script `/tmp/quadratic_norm_recovery_planes.sage` searches only these
derived planes, not arbitrary graph quadruples. It fixes a first point of
the norm circle, considers two secant directions, and enumerates the F27
plane they span. It excludes planes through zero (the obvious antipodal
configuration). For a four-point plane it computes the two-dimensional
orthogonal complement of its direction space and solves the ORIGINAL
incidence equation there, retaining BOTH nonzero-square conditions.

The first successful secant pair has indices1,3. It supplies four rows and
four allowed columns. Over

    E=F3[z]/(z^12+z^6+z^5+z^4+z^2+2),

with primitive generator z, use BASE-THREE POLYNOMIAL coefficient encoding:

    rows    [348525,427938,67519,338340],
    columns [16407,353186,260605,184522].

All sixteen original equations hold; Q and N are nonzero squares at all
eight vertices. Rows have linear rank3 and affine rank2. Neither side has
two F27-projectively equal points. Thus the failure is not a duplicated
scalar ray, and it is not repaired merely by deleting antipodal duplicates.

`/tmp/quadratic_norm_recovery_planes27.{log,json}`.

independent relative-trace formula it builds the nonsingular symmetric Gram
matrix for Q, then evaluates Q as a quadratic matrix form. The quartic norm
is recomputed as the product of all four q-Frobenius conjugates.

It checks all original incidences and restrictions, both injections, the two

projective duplicates on BOTH sides. This is exact Sage verification, NOT a

`/tmp/count_quadratic_norm_recovery27.sage`, log

Two new complete auxiliary Lean files:
