  Log `/tmp/MultiOrbitAveraging.final.log`; installed olean.
* `Submission/EllipticFusionThinning.lean`, 476 lines, imports
  EllipticClassFusion, MultiOrbitAveraging, UpperBounds, and Packing.
  Log `/tmp/EllipticFusionThinning.final.log`; installed olean.

All eight printed axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
There is no sorry or native_decide in either file. These files are NOT imported
into the main Spec and do NOT prove or disprove Erdős 714.

### Correction to the earlier speculative counting identity

For a class c=(d,t), the existing Parameter type has one row parameter for each
x!=0,t. This is exactly q-2 when t!=0 but q-1 when t=0. Consequently the earlier
speculative identity sum_k m_k=(q-2)*|S| is generally false. The completed proof
does not assume it. It uses at least (q-2)*(q-1) block-edge incidences for every
accepted class, together with an upper bound m_k<=2*|S|. The originally proposed
sharp real density bound involving |S|^(-1/4) has not been formalized or asserted
as a consequence of the erroneous equality.

### General multi-orbit averaging theorem

`Erdos714MultiOrbit.bound` concerns a finite permutation-group action on E,
with a color map that is constant under the action and transitive on each
color fiber. Suppose every fiber has size N. For a family B_i of blocks, assume
that its aggregate intersection with EACH color fiber has size at least t.
Individual blocks need not have equal sizes, and need not meet colors equally.
If a selected set A meets every translate of B_i in at most b_i points, then

    t*|A| <= N * sum_i b_i.

The proof double-counts coverage separately on each orbit and then sums over
the selected points. No transitivity of the full union is assumed.

### Actual matrix and edge bookkeeping

Namespace `Erdos714EllipticThinning`, q=|F| and G=GL(2,F):

* `invariants_conjugate`, `transform`, `transforms`, and `edgeAction` give the
  honest action (p,q): g -> p*g*q^(-1) on both vertex parts.
* `cyclicBasis` is the invertible matrix [[0,g01],[1,g11]]. The root-free
  characteristic polynomial makes g01 nonzero. `cyclic_identity` proves its
  conjugacy identity with [[0,-det(g)],[1,tr(g)]]. `elliptic_conjugate` then
  proves conjugacy of matrices with equal elliptic invariants.
* `edgeEquiv` encodes an undirected host edge uniquely by a left vertex and
  an actual connection matrix. `color` is its accepted invariant pair, not
  a choice of a transporter.
* `transitive_on_color` proves action transitivity within each color.
  `color_card` proves each actual edge-color fiber has exactly
  |G|*q*(q-1) members.
* `gridEmbedding` and `block` use the existing injective fiberCopy. Their
  colors are calculated by `color_grid`.
* `block_meeting_lower` proves the corrected (q-2)*(q-1) lower bound for
  aggregate incidence in each color, INCLUDING trace-zero classes.
* `rows_card_bound` proves m_k<=2*|S| from the nonzero quadratic
  X^2-t*X+k*d. It verifies injectivity of the x parameter in each class fiber;
  merely counting roots without that injection would not suffice.
* `selected_block_bound` applies the extremal number to the surviving edges
  of every translated block. The selected graph need not contain any full
  block, and need not itself respect conjugacy classes.

### Completed global bounds

Let S consist entirely of elliptic invariant pairs, q>2, and let H be ANY
K44-free spanning subgraph of the two-part graph defined by
invariants(g^(-1)*h) in S. Then `thinning_extremal_bound` proves

    e(H) <= |G|*q*ex(2*|S|+q, K44).

Using the existing verified KST bound and |G|<=q^4,
`thinning_fourth_power` proves the exact natural-number inequality

    e(H)^4 <= 81*q^20*(2*|S|+q)^7.

In particular, `critical_size_bound` states that for natural constants C,D,

    |S| <= C*q   and   q^7 <= D*e(H)
       imply
    q <= 81*D^4*(2*C+1)^7.

This rules out every arbitrary-edge-thinning repair of an elliptic fusion
with O(q) accepted classes along unbounded fields. Its scale is O(q^(27/4))
edges, rather than the target Omega(q^7). It is stronger than the old theorem
that ruled out only full class fusions. It does not rule out all graphs, and
it does not treat arbitrary thinnings of split/Jordan/scalar class unions.
No such extension or sharp unbalanced real formula is claimed here.

## Positive Vandermonde edge signs in characteristic three: exact q27 failure

### Why this variant was investigated

For a cubic extension E/Fq put

    Delta(x) = (x-x^q)(x^q-x^(q^2))(x^(q^2)-x).

Keep only norm edges N(x+y)=ab with Delta(x+y) nonzero square. In
characteristic three, with q=3 mod 4, the old scalar-row Artin--Schreier
counterexample has two branches of opposite orientation. Thus this edge
restriction eliminates that particular template. It does NOT eliminate all
K44 copies, even when both weights and point norms must also be nonzero squares.

### Exact certificates and independent checks

Flat coefficient encoding: E=F3[e]/(e^9+2e^3+2e^2+e+1), base-three coefficients.
These integers are NOT multiplicative logarithms.

* Positive orientation only: rows (0,1),(1,1),(3,2),(12979,1632);
  columns (671,12801),(5571,16611),(15229,16612),(16020,11198).
  Producer `/tmp/norm_positive_char3.py`, log/JSON
  `/tmp/norm_positive_char3_27.{log,json}`.

  (12801,11197); columns (1831,836),(5455,17436),(16144,12802),(18063,16612).
  Opposite translation by 485 makes every point norm a nonzero square too.
  Final rows (485,1),(483,1),(479,12802),(13034,11197);

  Producer `/tmp/norm_positive_char3_square.py`, corresponding log/JSON
  `/tmp/norm_positive_char3_square_27.{log,json}`.

The search was structured: fix rows (0,1),(1,1), exploit Delta(y+1)=Delta(y),
derive their common columns, and group exact incidence masks by row weight.
The certificates were found after 19 and 10 tested row quadruples respectively.
The producer's 511758 count is the UNRESTRICTED part size. The graph with both

## Complementary linear blocks: uniform arbitrary-thinning obstruction for quadratic recovery

### What was investigated

The valid independent-row cubic recovery argument was revisited. Rather than
try another choice of the quartic norm, this continuation asks whether ANY
choice of the row function N, or ANY edge thinning of the model, can fix its
dependent-row problem. The resulting obstruction is uniform, not a new finite
counterexample search.

Five complete, installed auxiliary files (807 lines total):

* `Submission/BlockSecondMoment.lean`,112 lines.
* `Submission/LinearBlockCounts.lean`,202 lines.
* `Submission/LinearBlockMoments.lean`,123 lines.
* `Submission/LinearBlockThinning.lean`,166 lines.
* `Submission/QuadraticRecoveryThinning.lean`,204 lines.

They are NOT imported into Spec. All25 printed axiom audits use only propext,
Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No proof placeholders or native_decide occur.
Logs `/tmp/{BlockSecondMoment,LinearBlockCounts,LinearBlockMoments,
LinearBlockThinning,QuadraticRecoveryThinning}.log` are the final clean-check
logs (some harmless linter warnings remain).

### General complementary-block chart (Lean verified)

Let V have dimension3 over a finite field F of orderq. An indexed row is
R(c)=(u_c,w_c) in VxV; an indexed column is T(d)=(phi_d,psi_d) in V* x V*.
Assume all u_c and phi_d are nonzero, and each indexed family is projectively
injective (`RayInjective`: R(c)=a*R(c') implies c=c', likewise T).
The host relation is

    phi_d(w_c)=psi_d(u_c).

Every linear endomorphism A of V defines a complete bipartite block:

    rows:    A(u_c)=w_c,
    columns: phi_d composed with A = psi_d.

Exact kernel-verified counts:

* There are q^9 linear endomorphisms.
* Each indexed row/column lies in q^6 blocks.
* A distinct indexed pair on either side lies in at most q^3 blocks.
  If a common block exists, projective injectivity proves the two projected
  inputs independent; this crucial hypothesis is not inferred from distinctness
  alone. If no common block exists, its count is zero.
* Every compatible row-column pair lies in exactly q^4 blocks.

For the last count, the map A -> (A u, phi composed with A) surjects onto the
five-dimensional compatibility hyperplane phi(w)=psi(u). Surjectivity is
explicit: choose alpha(u)=1 and phi(w0)=1, then set

    A(x)=alpha(x)*w + (psi(x)-alpha(x)*phi(w))*w0.

The common fiber has dimension4 by rank-nullity. Fiber cardinality is proved
via an honest translation equivalence with the kernel, followed by the finite
vector-space cardinal theorem. Dualization is proved to be a linear equivalence
of full ENDOMORPHISM spaces (not merely invertible transformations), and is
used to transfer the two column-count statements.

The block-size moments therefore satisfy

    sum_A m_A <= q^6*|C|,
    sum_A m_A^2 <= q^6*|C|+q^3*|C|^2,

and the analogous column estimates. The auxiliary moment theorem proves this
from point and distinct-pair coverage, with diagonal terms counted separately.

### Averaging actual selected edges (Lean verified)

For any selected edge set E with no injective4x4 rectangle, its restriction to
a block is the incidence graph on the actual selected row and column subtypes.
A sigma-type equivalence checks that its edge count is precisely
`(blockEdges E S T).card`. The earlier unbalanced ordered-star bound gives

    (e_A-3*m_A)^4 <= 3*m_A^3*n_A^4

with truncated natural subtraction. No complete block is assumed to survive
in E. Double counting gives exact selected-edge coverage

    q^4*|E| = sum_A e_A.

The new integer-parameter Holder substitute says: for q^3<=u^4,

    q*e_A <= 3*q*m_A + 2*u*(m_A^2+n_A^2+q^2).

It follows using m^3*n^4*q <= (m^2+n^2+q^2)^4. If both indexed part sizes are
at mostq^4, summing yields `chart_bound`:

    |E| <= 13*u*q^6.

A rounded fourth root u=floor(fourth-root(q^3))+1 satisfies
q^3<=u^4<=16*q^3, including all positive small orders. Therefore
`chart_fourth_power` proves

    |E|^4 <= 456976*q^27.

Scope matters: this theorem assumes the stated chart's nonzero projections
and projective injectivity. A preliminary discussion of averaging over all
six-dimensional coordinate splittings was NOT needed and has NOT been bundled
as a theorem about every arbitrary rank-six graph.

### Application to the actual quadratic-recovery law (Lean verified)

Take F of characteristic3, X=F^4, an arbitrary quadratic form Q, an ARBITRARY
function N:X->F, and an invertible linear pairing-coordinate map B:X~=X.
Vertices on BOTH sides are all x with Q(x)!=0. The asymmetric relation is

    dot(B(x),y) = Q(x)^2*Q(y)^2 + Q(x)*N(x)*Q(y).

It fits ONE complementary-block chart, with

    u_x=(B(x)_0,B(x)_1,-Q(x)^2),
    w_x=(B(x)_2,B(x)_3,-Q(x)*N(x)),
    phi_y=dot((y_2,y_3,Q(y)), -),
    psi_y=dot((-y_0,-y_1,-Q(y)^2), -).

Thus no unproved coverage over coordinate splittings is used. The required
nonzero projections follow from Q(x),Q(y)!=0. Projective injections are proved:

* For rows, equality up to scalara first gives x=a*x'. Comparing the Q^2
  coordinate gives a^4=a. Nonzeroness cancelsa, and characteristic3 makes
  a^3=1 implya=1 by Frobenius injectivity.
* For columns, recovering their vector coordinates gives y=a*y'. Comparing
  the Q coordinate gives a^2=a, hencea=1. This part needs no characteristic3.

`lift_compatibility` checks the ORIGINAL incidence equality by polynomial
identities. `arbitrary_thinning` applies the chart bound to ANY free spanning
subgraph H of this host, identifies the actual undirected graph edge count,
and proves

    e(H)^4 <= 456976*q^27.

`critical_size_bound` consequently proves

    q^7 <= K*e(H)  ==>  q <= 456976*K^4.

No nonsquare-minus-one assumption, no square vertex restrictions, no quartic
homogeneity, and no particular norm function N is needed. Deleting edges
incident with omitted vertices includes arbitrary vertex restrictions. This
rules out all density-preserving repairs of the earlier quadratic-recovery
model, and in fact rules out attaining its q^7 target by ANY edge thinning.
It remains consistent with the valid independent-row bound of at most3 common
neighbors: the unavoidable dependent configurations are the issue.

`bilinear_thinning` writes the same result directly for a bundled pairing
P:X ->_F X*, assuming P bijective. The coordinate change is explicitly proved
using `dotProductEquiv`; it is not left to an informal matrix identification.
This covers the nondegenerate-pairing version of the generic relation from
QuadraticNormRecovery. The specific F27 norm table has NOT been reclassified
as Lean verified by this argument; its arithmetic certificate remains Sage-only.

## Asymmetric quartic/cubic resultant code: positive line bound, but independent-row failures

### A different code candidate

After the six-dimensional quadratic-recovery obstruction, a new model was
investigated rather than another modification of its row function. Rows are
monic irreducible quartic polynomials P over Fq. Coordinates are monic irreducible
cubic polynomials Q, and the q-ary code symbol is Res(P,Q). Thus the bipartite
columns are (Q,a), a in Fq*, with adjacency Res(P,Q)=a. There is no extra row
weight. The two irreducible degrees are different, so all symbols are nonzero.
This is NOT the earlier symmetric cubic/cubic weighted-resultant graph.

There are (q^4-q^2)/4 rows and (q^3-q)/3 coordinates. Each row has exactly one
neighbor at every coordinate. The row and column orders are both Theta(q^4),
and the degree is Theta(q^3), as required for the intended r4 scaling.

A genuinely positive local feature motivated it: four scalar shifts P+t*R,
with distinctt, can agree at a cubic coordinate Q only if Q divides R. For a
nonzero direction of degree at most3, there is at most one such monic Q.
Consequently the old scalar-line obstruction does not apply. This local feature
does NOT imply the full code is K44-free.

### A caution about elimination degrees

`/tmp/resultant_plane_elimination.sage` derives the universal characteristic-two

monic Q define a zero-dimensional ideal of degree42. The log contains an exact

all graph open conditions. It neither produces a witness for that plane nor
proves a uniform generic degree statement. It does warn against applying a
cubic root bound to the full three-variable elimination merely because the
resultant is cubic along scalar polynomial lines.

## Translated quadratic-norm fibers: uniform arbitrary-thinning obstruction

This continuation tried to obtain a positive construction by translating
quadratic-norm curves with nonlinear shifts. A structural complete-block
cover prevented this family from working; no numerical search was used.
This is NOT a disproof of Erdős 714.

Two complete, installed files:

* `Submission/TranslatedNormFibers.lean`, importing ProfileThinning.
  Log `/tmp/TranslatedNormFibers.log`.
* `Submission/TranslatedNormCounts.lean`, importing TranslatedNormFibers.
  Log `/tmp/TranslatedNormCounts.log`.

All TWELVE printed audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
Both files compile without warnings or placeholders.

### General translated-level-set theorem

Let G be a finite abelian additive group, T a finite type,
|G|<=q^2, |T|<=q, and nu:G->T have every fiber of size <=q+1.
For ARBITRARY functions f:G->G and g:G->T use two copies of G^2 and relation

    nu(x_1+y_1-f(x_2+y_2)) = g(x_2+y_2).

For EVERY K44-free edge subgraph H, `thinning_fourth_power` proves

    e(H)^4 <= 21233664*q^27.

`critical_size_bound` proves q^7<=K*e(H) implies q<=21233664*K^4.
No polynomial, linearity, balanced-fiber, or nonzero-level assumption is
needed for these upper bounds.

The blocks are explicit: fix the row's second coordinate v, a center w,
and a level r. Rows are (w+z,v) with nu(z)=r; columns are
(f(t)-w,t-v) with g(t)=r. Every cross pair is a host edge, and every host
edge occurs in such a block. Split the t-fibers into chunks of size q+1.
The chunk budget gives at most 2q^5 blocks, each with <=2(q+1) vertices.
The checked KST block-cover bound then yields the exponent 27.
The implementation uses the block COVER theorem, so it does not rely on an
unproved assertion that the chunk cover is a disjoint edge partition.

### Actual field norms and exact size counts

For E/F finite fields with |E|=|F|^2, the file proves

    algebraMap F E (norm F x) = x^(q+1),

and bounds every norm fiber by q+1 using polynomial roots, including zero.
`arbitrary_thinning` and `critical_size_bound` give the actual quadratic-norm
specialization with no extra algebraic hypotheses.

The count file supplies a full neighborhood equivalence with
Sigma_t {z:nu(z)=g(t)}, giving the exact host edge count

    |G|^2 * sum_t |nu^(-1)(g(t))|.

For the field norm, the zero fiber has size one; summing the fiber upper
bounds over the whole field forces every nonzero fiber to have exactly q+1
points. Therefore, if g never vanishes, the host has exactly

    vertices = 2q^4,    edges = q^6(q+1).

`relative_thinning_bound` proves

    q*e(H)^4 <= 21233664*e(host)^4.

Thus the host really does have the target initial size; the obstruction is
the vanishing retained edge fraction, not an insufficient initial degree.

### Scope and connection to earlier examples

This applies, in particular, to the earlier shifted-parabola N(u+u'-t^2)=N(t)
model (the absolute bound allows g(0)=0). Deleting the t=0 edges only gives
a subgraph, so that restriction is also covered. The earlier finite q3/q5
failures for the norm-circle variant are now superseded by a uniform bound
for all shifts and levels, allowing arbitrary edge deletion.

It does NOT cover the other shifted-parabola model using a general Sidon
curve in place of a norm circle, arbitrary quadratic forms varying with
the second coordinate, ordinary cubic norm graphs, or arbitrary graphs.
No new positive construction has been obtained.

Spec.lean was not changed. Its original type and sole import were checked
exactly. Compilation still reports the one sorry in the r>=4 branch at

proof or disproof has been submitted, and no computation is pending.

## Varying quadratic-form slices: a structured quartic copy and full norm semantics

A new candidate was investigated beyond the translated-fixed-norm family.
It failed; it does not prove or disprove the original extremal conjecture.

### Candidate and derived test

Let E/F be quadratic, q=|F|=3^k with k odd, bar(x)=x^q, N the field norm.
Use two copies of E^2 and let X,Z be the coordinatewise row-column sums.
The relation is

    N(Z) != 1,      N(X+Z*bar(X)) = 1+N(Z)^2.

For each admissible Z, X->X+Z*bar(X) is invertible, so the quadratic form
is nonsingular and anisotropic. Its SHAPE varies with Z, unlike the previous
translated-fixed-norm family. No classification claiming that this cannot
be recoded in some other model was proved.

Take i^2=-1, b,c in F, U=c(1+i), V=b*i, and rows (0,t) for scalar t.
The common-neighbor equation is exactly

    P_(b,c)(t)=t^4+(c^2-b^2)*t^2+b^4+1+c^2*(b+1)^2=0,
    t^2+b^2 != 1.

Four distinct roots give four columns

    (U,V), (-U,V), (bar(U),bar(V)), (-bar(U),bar(V)).

This algebraic reduction preceded the finite check; no arbitrary graph
quadruple search or floating-point experiment was used.

At q=27 use F3[a]/(a^3-a+1), b=a, c=a^2+a+1=(a-1)^2, d=a(a-1).
The quartic has the four roots c,-c,d,-d, all satisfying the open condition.
The first actual certificate was found after six (b,c) template cases.

(a,b)*(c,d)=(ac-bd,ad+bc), not the search's extension representation. It

## Exact fourth-order designs: a checked combinatorial limitation

This continuation reviewed the set-system/packing formulation rather than
testing another algebraic graph. No construction attaining the conjectured
exponent, and no general upper bound disproving it, was found.

New standalone file `Submission/ExactFourthDesign.lean`, sole import
FormalConjecturesUtil. It is complete, installed, and compiles without
warnings. All EIGHT printed audits use only propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound. Log `/tmp/ExactFourthDesign.log`. No numerical experiment was
used. The theorem is the known fourth-order Ray-Chaudhuri--Wilson bound,
not a claimed new extremal exponent.

### Exact uniformity versus packing

For an indexed block family S:A->Finset V, `coverage S T` counts the blocks
containing T, as a real number. Indexed repeated blocks are counted, not
deduplicated. Suppose every block has size k, 4<=k<=|V|-2, and EVERY
four-element point set lies in exactly l indexed blocks, with l>0.

`fourth_design_block_bound` proves

    choose(|V|,2) <= |A|.

Thus `not_balanced_exact_design` excludes such an exact design whenever
|A|<=|V|. With A nonempty, `exists_unequal_quadruple_coverage` proves that
any regular block family with those size assumptions has two quadruples
with different coverage. This conclusion does not even assume K44-freeness.

### Checked proof

* `extensionEquiv` double-counts a block containing T together with one extra
  point as an extra point together with a block containing its extension.
  `uniform_downward` descends exact uniform coverage from order s+1 to s.
* Write v=|V|. The derived triple and pair counts are

      l3=l*(v-3)/(k-3),
      l2=l3*(v-2)/(k-2).

* M is the actual block-versus-point-pair incidence matrix over R; Z is
  point-versus-point-pair incidence; O is a single row of ones.
  `pair_gram_decomposition` proves

      M^T M = (l2-2*l3+l)*I + (l3-l)*Z^T Z + l*O^T O.

* The coefficient of I is

      l*(v-k)*(v-k-1)/((k-2)*(k-3)) > 0,

  and l3-l=l*(v-k)/(k-3)>=0. `gram_rank_bound` proves positive
  definiteness, invertibility, and full column rank using actual Mathlib
  matrix rank and Gram positivity. The number of columns is choose(v,2).
* `pair_fisher_bound` exposes the uniform pair/triple/quadruple-count
  version separately, with its positivity hypotheses explicit.

### Important scope

This does NOT imply that the packing conjecture is false. K44-freeness
requires only that four-point coverage be AT MOST THREE; it allows all
values 0,1,2,3 in a nonuniform pattern. Such partial packings do not satisfy
the exact-uniformity hypothesis used by this Gram proof. No stability or
approximate-design extension, and no general edge bound, is asserted.

## Binary Witt norm circles: a uniform field-norm obstruction

A new characteristic-four candidate was investigated algebraically. No graph
quadruple search or numerical experiment was used. The full candidate fails
uniformly; this is NOT a disproof of Erdős714.

### Candidate and symbolic copy

For E/F quadratic, q=|F|=2^k, use length-two binary Witt coordinates with

    (x,y) +_W (u,v) = (x+u, y+v+x*u).

The two vertex parts are E^2. An edge requires that the first Witt-sum
coordinate s be nonzero and that its second coordinate z satisfy

    N_(E/F)(z) = N_(E/F)(s)^2.

Equivalently the connection set is {(s,s^2*c):s!=0,N(c)=1}, using the norm
CIRCLE, not the earlier APN cubic curve. The elementary fiber count gives
q^4 vertices per part and (q^2-1)(q+1) neighbors per vertex. These size
formulas are mathematical bookkeeping here; no separate Lean degree-count
theorem was added for this new candidate.

For every k>=4, choose nonzero a in F with both absolute traces
Tr(a)=Tr(1/a)=0. Choose u,v with u^2+u=a, v^2+v=1/a, and x with Tr(x)=1.
Choose y in E with y^2+y=x^4, so y^q=y+1. Set b=u^4+a*x. Four rows are

    (0,0), (0,1), (a,b), (a,b+1),

and four columns are

    (x,y), (x,y+1),
    (x+1/a,y+v^4), (x+1/a,y+v^4+1).

All sixteen original norm equations and nonzero FIRST SUM coordinates hold.
In particular Tr(x)=Tr(x+1/a)=Tr(x+a)=Tr(x+a+1/a)=1, so none of those sums
vanishes. Each part embeds injectively. No assertion that every vertex's
individual first coordinate is nonzero is made: the displayed rows include
first coordinate zero. Vertex-restricted or edge-thinned versions are not
uniformly excluded by this theorem.

### Uniform reciprocal-trace parameter, without a Weil bound

Write tau(t)=sum_{i<k} t^(2^i), with values 0 or1 in F. Multiplicative
orthogonality gives the EXACT FIELD-VALUED identity

    sum_{t in F*} t^3 * (1+tau(t)) * (1+tau(1/t)) = 1

when k>=4. Single-trace terms vanish. In the double sum, the only surviving
pair is 3+2^i=2^j, namely (i,j)=(0,2). The bounds k>=4 exclude wraparound
modulo q-1. Therefore some nonzero t has both traces zero. This does NOT
state a real-valued count or an abundance estimate for the parameters.

2. `Submission/BinaryArtinSchreier.lean`, 123 lines, imports BinaryInverseTrace.

3. `Submission/WittNormCircle.lean`, 133 lines, imports BinaryArtinSchreier and

## Witt norm circles: arbitrary edge thinnings now excluded in both parities

This continuation strengthened the preceding full-host obstruction. It still
does not prove or disprove Erdős714.

### First: an odd-degree projective block chart

For q=2^k with k odd, choose eta in E/F quadratic with
eta^2+eta=1 and eta^q=eta+1. For scalar x,t in F, the two curves

    L_alpha(x)=(alpha*x, eta*(alpha*x)^2),
    R_alpha(t)=(eta*alpha*t, eta*(alpha*t)^2)

have Witt sum

    (alpha*s, alpha^2*eta*N(s)),  s=x+eta*t.

This lies in the norm-circle connection set whenever s!=0. Elementary
quadratic Hilbert90 shows that every connection is such a scaled sum.
Translating the row curve by p and the column curve by -_W p preserves the
sum. Scales alpha need only range over projective F-lines in E, so there
are q+1 scale classes and q^4*(q+1) vertex blocks of size at most2q.
The Lean argument proves a COVER; no disjoint edge partition is asserted.
The graph induced on a vertex block need not be complete, and the thinning
proof does not assume its edges survive.

### Simpler cover: all characteristic-two fields, including even degree

A direct cover makes the parity restriction unnecessary. In an edge

    N(y+v+x*u)=N(x+u)^2,     x+u!=0,

fix the row label x, center w=v+x*u, and level r=N(x+u)^2. Rows in that
block have first coordinate x and N(y+w)=r. Columns satisfy v=w-x*u
and N(x+u)^2=r. Each side has at most q+1 elements. There are exactly
q^5 possible indices (x,w,r). Every edge determines an index. The open
condition may simply be dropped when passing to the larger covering host.

## Varying-form Witt candidate: exact failures at q4, q8, q32

A different candidate was then investigated. In E/F quadratic, char2, use
the SAME explicit Witt carry sum (Z,X) and impose

    N(Z)!=1,  N(X+Z*X^q)=(1+N(Z))^2.

The norm-form SHAPE varies with Z, so the preceding fixed-fiber theorem
has not been applied to it. It has q^4 vertices per part and
(q^2-q-1)*(q+1) neighbors per vertex. These size formulas are elementary
bookkeeping, not a new Lean degree theorem.

Algebraic parameterization precedes testing. Off N(Z)=1, the transformation
L_Z(X)=X+Z*X^q satisfies L_Z^2=(1+N(Z))*id. Thus a connection has the unique
form

    X=Y+Z/Y,  N(Y)=1.

For the first two rows (0,0),(0,h), with h=1 in the tests, two distinct unit
circle parameters Y,T give a common column

    u=Y*T*(1+h/(Y+T)),  v=Y+u/Y,

provided N(u)!=1. Reversing the pair gives the partner column (u,v+h).
The test works in the quotient by this order-two translation. A repeated
ordered difference of quotient representatives gives rows
0,h,r,r+_W h and two column pairs, hence a K44. This is a derived finite
field link test, not a blind search through arbitrary graph quadruples.

## Additive norm-product model: three independently checked finite failures

For a cubic extension E/F in characteristic two, the candidate has rows
(a,b), columns(z,v) in E x F, with adjacency

    N(a+z)+N(a)*N(z)=b+v.

There are q^4 vertices per part and q^3 neighbors per row (one forced v for
 each z), hence q^7 edges. These counts have not been newly formalized.
Four distinct SCALAR row points are safe: expansion in the scalar point t
has coefficients 1+N(z), Tr(z), s2(z), N(z), so cubic interpolation leaves
at most three z. No corresponding assertion for arbitrary affine lines was
proved. A projective ray-injectivity observation for the first-pair profile
also does not establish freeness.

Fixing rows (0,0),(1,1) gives exactly columns (z,N(z)) with N(z+1)=1.

## A semilinear correction beyond the row-profile theorem: finite failures

A subsequent binary model tried to preserve the safe scalar-row interpolation
while escaping the uniform profile obstruction. For k odd, q=2^k, E/F cubic,
put sigma=2^((3*k+1)/2), A(x)=x^q+x, and

    P(a,z)=Tr_(E/F)(A(a)^(sigma+1)*A(z)+A(a)*A(z)^(sigma+1)).

The relation is

    N(a+z)+N(a)*N(z)+P(a,z)=b+v.

Here sigma squared is squaring on E and its fixed field is F2. The added
term vanishes for scalar a, so the earlier scalar-row cubic interpolation
survives. It depends on more than N(a), so the row-profile theorem above
has NOT been applied to it. No freeness theorem follows from those facts.

## Affine-line polarity replacement: exact framework and finite failures

A different construction architecture was investigated. Let E/F be quadratic,
q=|F|, char F odd, and choose coordinates e:E~F x F. For every nonvertical
line y=m*x+b choose an arbitrary shift C(m,b). Local coordinate t corresponds
to the plane point

    point(C,m,b,t)=(t-C(m,b), m*(t-C(m,b))+b).

Use the local relation

    R(s,t): Re(s)+Re(t)=Im(s)*Im(t),   s!=t.

The global bipartite graph has two copies of E^2. An edge exists when its
endpoints are the points of one line arising from a local R-edge. Distinct
first coordinates determine that line uniquely, so edge counts do not
include multiplicities. This is NOT a claimed free graph construction.

### Kernel-verified framework

`Submission/AffineLineReplacement.lean`,220 lines, imports Packing.
Installed, warning-free compile; log `/tmp/AffineLineReplacement.log`.
Seven printed audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

* `pair_unique`, `pair_injective`: a distinct pair uniquely determines its
  line, its line intercept, and both shifted local coordinates.
* `edge_count`: for ANY relation R and ANY shift table C, the actual graph
  has |E|^2*|{(s,t):s!=t and R(s,t)}| unordered bipartite edges.
* `on_line_iff`: points on a specified line are joined exactly according to
  that line's local relation; edges cannot come from an alternative label.
* `polarity_rectangle`, `local_free`: the local polarity relation, even
  before diagonal deletion, has no rectangle with distinct two rows/columns;
  the actual diagonally trimmed local graph is K22-free.
* `polarity_pattern_card`: q^3-q ordered local edges, assuming 2!=0.
* `polarity_vertex_count`, `polarity_edge_count`: exactly 2*q^4 vertices
  and q^7-q^5 edges for EVERY C(m,b).

The e used in these counting/local theorems is only an equivalence E~F^2;
linearity is unnecessary for them. The numerical candidate below uses actual
quadratic-field coordinates. No global freeness, bound on arbitrary edge
thinnings, or universal obstruction to all shift tables is proved.

### The intercept shift C(m,b)=b fails, including after deleting x=0

Over E=Fq[i], i^2=D nonsquare, the candidate is explicitly

    x!=u,
    b=(x*v-u*y)/(x-u),
    Re(x+u+2*b)=Im(x+b)*Im(u+b),

for points (x,y),(u,v). It uses the line's intercept rather than a fixed
coordinate on every line.

For rows (0,0),(1,0), common columns are parameterized by s!=0,t in F:

    b0=(t^2+s*t-1)/2, b=b0+i*t,
    (u,v)=(i*s,(1-i*s)*b).

`/tmp/affine_line_polarity.sage` checks this parameterization and searches
four-subset collisions in these columns. q3 has no copy for THIS FIRST PAIR
(79 further rows,0 profiles); this is not a freeness proof. q5 and q7 fail,
after4 and6 further rows, respectively. These copies use several x=0 rows.
Indeed, for x=0 the intercept equals y and the relation loses dependence
on v, so deleting that exceptional vertical line is a meaningful repair.

The repair nevertheless fails. In the graph with x,u both NONZERO, take
first rows (1,0),(2,0). For each u not in {0,1,2} and t in F set

    b0=(t^2+Im(u)*t-Re(1+u))/2,
    b=b0+i*t, v=(1-u)*b,

then retain columns also adjacent to (2,0). Script
`/tmp/affine_line_polarity_nonzero.sage` tests precisely this link.
q3:6 common columns,70 further rows,3 profiles, no copy in this link ONLY.
q5:14 columns,27 further rows,31 profiles, exact K44.
q7:56 columns,9 further rows,1191 profiles, exact K44.

## Noncommutative trace-zero quartic norm: local recovery, but finite failures

A different candidate adds an alternating bilinear correction to an additive
quartic norm, breaking one of the earlier pure-conjugate profile obstructions.
Over an odd field F, take u^2=D, v^2=e0+e1*u, with both D and e0^2-D*e1^2
nonsquare and e1 nonzero. E/F is quartic, and V=<u,v,u*v> is its trace-zero
space. For x=(a,b,c), put

    A=e0*(b^2+D*c^2)+2*e1*D*b*c,
    f(a,b,c)=(D*a^2-A)^2-D*(e1*(b^2+D*c^2)+2*e0*b*c)^2.

This is N_E/F(a*u+b*v+c*u*v). Vertices are V x F in each part, and

    f(x+y)=weight(x)+weight(y)+x_a*y_b-x_b*y_a.

It is the product-Cayley equation for the central extension whose cocycle is
the displayed alternating form; the graph is bipartite, not asserted symmetric
on a single copy of V x F. No arbitrary-subgroup or edge-thinning exclusion
has been proved for this candidate.

The special choice e0!=0 is meaningful. Along four distinct scalar row points
(t,0,0), subtracting two column equations cancels the quartic leading term.
The resulting cubic's coefficients recover a, then A, then b. The last recovery
USES the noncommutative correction. The remaining ambiguity satisfies

    (c-c')*(e0*(c+c')+2*e1*b)=0.

Thus there are at most two common columns along this row direction if
D!=0,2!=0,e0!=0. This positive local fact is not global freeness.
For e0=0, this argument degenerates, and there are separable line grids.

The new candidate nevertheless has exact copies at three field sizes:
* q3: (D,e0,e1)=(2,1,1), first rows (0,0,0;0),(1,0,0;0),
  5 common columns,6 further row/weight pairs,1 profile.
* q5: (D,e0,e1)=(2,1,2), same first rows,
  21 common columns,15 further row/weight pairs,178 profiles.
* q7: (D,e0,e1)=(3,1,1), same first rows,
  27 common columns,47 further row/weight pairs,265 profiles.
The other two rows have point coordinates on the c-axis, so these copies do
not contradict the verified scalar-u direction result.

### Further proper refinements: mathematical argument, NOT formalized

For odd q, let H=q^2-q+1 and let m be a proper divisor of H. Both the m-sheet
and 2m-sheet refinements also appear to contain a skew K46. Choose nonsquare

 b -> (b-a)/(b-a^q) bijects P1(Fq3) with the norm-one circle of order q^3+1.
The subgroup of order (q^3+1)/m contains the smaller circle of order q+1,
strictly when m<H. Its preimages include elements b outside Fq. The involution
b -> n/b preserves the subgroup preimage and exchanges square classes, so
some such b is nonsquare. Taking x^2=a,y^2=b gives the skew parameters and
N_E/Fq6(x+y)=b-a an m-th power. The refined weight order then fits the
formal skew-grid theorem. The maximal m=H is not covered by this argument.

## Dickson quintic permutations: a new positive arithmetic tool (Lean verified)

New complete, installed, warning-free file Submission/DicksonPermutation.lean,
sole import FormalConjecturesUtil; log /tmp/DicksonPermutation.log.
All five printed audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
This is an arithmetic result, not a graph construction.

For every finite field F with |F| congruent2 or3 mod5, and EVERY a in F,
including a=0, the actual Mathlib first-kind Dickson polynomial

    D5(x,a)=x^5-5*a*x^3+5*a^2*x

permutes F. In characteristic3 it is x^5+a*x^3-a^2*x. Thus its equation
with ANY right side has exactly one solution. `odd_galois_unique` applies
to every actual GaloisField 3 (2*k+1).

The proof does not assume a finite-field Dickson permutation theorem:
* `cayley_two`, `power_rec`, `trace_power_rec` prove the 2x2 recurrence.
* `trace_power_eq`: trace and determinant determine traces of all powers.
* `trace_recovery`: if d is coprime to |GL2(F)|, equal traces and determinants
  of d-th powers imply equal original traces. A natural exponent inverse
  modulo the ACTUAL group cardinal is used; no conjugator is assumed.
* Companion matrices have trace x and determinant a. Their fifth-power
  traces are D5(x,a). GL2 has order (q^2-1)*(q^2-q), coprime to5 in the
  stated residue classes. For a=0, the field unit group handles x^5.
* `dickson_five_bijective` checks equality with Polynomial.dickson, not only
  a similarly shaped expression; `sparse_quintic_unique` gives unique roots.

Technical note: after expanding the recurrence at n=0, explicitly simplify
Nat.zero_add before pow_one. Otherwise `ring` can retain trace(M^(0+1))
as a separate atom from trace(M), despite their similar pretty-printing.

## Conditional Dickson matrix reconstruction (Lean verified)

New complete installed Submission/DicksonMatrixRecovery.lean, importing
DicksonPermutation and MatrixCubicRecovery. Warning-free log
/tmp/DicksonMatrixRecovery.log; both printed audits use permitted axioms.

For invertible H, with D=det(H), suppose H=D^3*A+D*B. Taking determinants
and cancelling D gives

    det(A)*D^5 + mixed(A,B)*D^3 + det(B)*D = 1.

When det(A)!=0 AND det(A)*det(B)=-mixed(A,B)^2, division by det(A)
puts this in Dickson form with parameter mixed(A,B)/det(A). In the stated
ternary fields, D is unique, hence H is unique. All coefficient and
reconstruction hypotheses are explicit. No row family satisfying them has
been supplied. In particular this result does not overcome the earlier
obstructions to full trace/determinant class fusions or dependent rows.

## Nonsplit-torus quotient of a Bose–Chowla graph: counts and finite obstructions

Let q be odd, L=F_(q^6), E=F_(q^3), and choose nonzero theta in F_(q^2)
with theta^q=-theta. Let H be the multiplicative subgroup of L* of order
h=q^2-q+1. On two copies of G=L*/H, use adjacency xy in

    S = {[t+theta] : t in E}.

This is a nonsplit-torus quotient, not the previously investigated
weighted-power hosts. The cyclic group has size W=(q^3-1)*(q+1).

### Exact counts (derived mathematically, NOT formalized in Lean)

The subgroup H is contained in the norm-one group for L/E. Consequently a
collision [t+theta]=[u+theta] implies t^2-theta^2=u^2-theta^2, so u=+/-t.
The parameters with collisions are the Cayley transforms

    t = theta*(1-h)/(1+h),   h in H.

They lie in E, since the q^3 Frobenius negates theta and inverts h. The
order of H is odd, so -1 is not in H. The identity h=1 corresponds to t=0;
the other h-1 parameters pair under t -> -t. Thus

    |S|=q^3-(q^2-q)/2,
    vertices=2W, degree=|S|, edges=W*|S|.

These are at the desired fourth-case scale, but freeness fails below.

### Structured finite checks

Fix first row0 and second row d=(q^6-1)/(q+1) mod W. Enumerate their common
columns, then hash four-column subsets across all further rows. This is an
exact torus-pair test, not a random numerical search.

* q3: W104, degree24,2496 edges. The specified pair has7 common columns
  and no K44 extension. A separate EXHAUSTIVE test over every second row
  d=1,...,103 finds no K44 anywhere, using translation symmetry.
* q5: W744, degree115,85560 edges; rows0,372,41,92;
  columns42,582,684,732.
* q7: W2736, degree322,880992 edges; rows0,1026,40,68;
  columns1423,1647,1687,2183.
* q9: W7280, degree693,5045040 edges; rows0,2184,42,49;
  columns2518,3068,3118,4448.
* q27: W551096, degree19332,10653787872 edges; rows0,59046,4,11;
  columns33729,232977,405793,507041.

Scripts /tmp/nonsplit_bose_quotient.sage (prime q),
/tmp/nonsplit_bose_quotient_power.sage (prime powers), and
/tmp/nonsplit_bose_quotient3_full.sage. Logs
/tmp/nonsplit_bose_quotient{3,5,7,9,27}.log and

## Norm-times-trace scalar-line recovery, all extension degrees (Lean verified)

New complete installed `Submission/NormTraceLine.lean` (197 lines), importing
only the already verified NormLineBound development. Clean compile log
`/tmp/NormTraceLine.log`. All four printed axiom audits use only propext,
Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No warnings, proof placeholders, or
native_decide occur in the new file. It is not imported into Spec.lean.

### Precise positive result

Let E/F be ANY finite-dimensional field extension of degree d, with
(d:F)!=0 and (d+1:F)!=0. Put

    f(x)=N_(E/F)(x)*Tr_(E/F)(x).

Choose d+1 distinct scalars t_i in F, with arbitrary row weights c_i. The
set of whole column vertices (x,b) in E x F satisfying

    c_i+b=f(x+t_i)   for every i

has size at most d. The theorem is stated for an arbitrary finite subset
of these columns, so no finite-base-field or Galois hypothesis is needed.
For d=3 the characteristic restrictions are exactly char!=2,3. This proves
the scalar-direction control previously observed by finite tests. It does
NOT address arbitrary affine-line directions u outside F, let alone four
noncollinear row points. It does not contradict any norm-times-trace
certificate in the preceding section.

### Polynomial argument and actual semantics

`profile_recovery` is a general polynomial theorem. P,Q have degree at most
d and coefficient1 at degree d. Their next coefficients are T,U. If

    P(t_i)*(T+d*t_i)-b = Q(t_i)*(U+d*t_i)-c

at d+1 distinct t_i, subtract the two polynomials and the constant b-c.
The leading degree d+1 cancels, so the difference has degree at most d.
The d+1 roots force it to be zero. Comparing its degree-d coefficient gives
(d+1)*(T-U)=0, hence T=U. Evaluating at -T/d gives b=c. Cancelling the
nonzero polynomial T+d*X then gives P=Q.

`shiftPoly x` is the ACTUAL characteristic polynomial of the matrix of
multiplication by -x, with respect to Module.finBasis F E. Verified bridges:

* monic and degree d;
* evaluation at t equals the actual Algebra.norm F (x+algebraMap t);
* coefficient d-1 equals the actual Algebra.trace F E x;
* aeval at -x is zero, by matrix Cayley--Hamilton and injectivity of
  leftMulMatrix.

`norm_trace_recovery` applies the polynomial theorem to this actual norm
polynomial, using trace(x+t)=trace(x)+d*t. Thus equal profiles give identical
characteristic polynomials AND identical column weights.

`scalar_line_columns_bound` fixes one solution, maps all solution vertices
injectively to roots of this one polynomial over E via (x,b) -> -x, and uses
the polynomial root count. Injectivity includes the recovered weight, not
merely point-coordinate distinctness. `cubic_scalar_line_bound` specializes
the exact result to degree3 and four row scalars.

### Scope and main task

This is a local positive ingredient only. The full norm-times-trace graph
already has verified finite failures after deletion of zero-trace edges,
including noncollinear failures at q5 and q25. The initial idea of enforcing
an arithmetic restriction on all elimination fibers did not produce a
qualifying construction in this continuation; no such restriction is assumed
in any theorem or claimed as established.

No complete proof or disproof of the original statement has been obtained or
submitted, and no successful asymptotic construction is pending.

### A uniform actual biclique in characteristic three

`cubic_norm_shift` proves the general identity, in ANY characteristic,

    N(x+t)=t^3+T*t^2+S*t+N(x),

It follows from the actual characteristic polynomial, with all norm/trace
coefficient bridges proved in NormTraceLine; no coordinate norm surrogate
or unproved separability bridge is used.

In characteristic3, if Tr(x)=1 then Tr(x+t)=1 and

    N(x+t)*Tr(x+t)=t^3+t^2+S*t+N(x).

The actual trace map is surjective over finite fields. Its trace-one fiber
has exactly q^2 elements by rank-nullity and the checked linear fiber count.
Pigeonholing its coefficient S in F supplies at least four distinct points
with the same S whenever q>=4 (so q>=9 in characteristic3).

Choose any four distinct scalar t_i as row points, with weights

    c_i=t_i^3+t_i^2+S*t_i.

The four column points x_j use weights N(x_j). All16 original incidences
hold, and ALL16 traces equal1. `profileCopy` checks the actual SimpleGraph

### Stronger result: arbitrary edge thinnings, characteristics TWO and THREE

The new NormTraceThinning file supersedes mere full-host nonfreeness for
asymptotic purposes in these characteristics. For EVERY nonzero linear L,
every finite cubic extension E/F in characteristic2 OR3, and EVERY
K44-free spanning edge subgraph H of the full host

it proves the exact integer bound

    e(H)^4 <= 165888*q^27,   q=|F|.

The full host itself has exactly2*q^4 vertices and q^7 edges, now both

`critical_size_bound` and `binary_critical_size_bound` give

    q^7 <= K*e(H)  ==>  q <= 165888*K^4.

The bound includes arbitrary vertex selections, represented by deleting

### Why the thinning theorem applies

`three_parameter_thinning` is a general checked profile result. Let u!=0
in a three-dimensional extension E/F. Suppose an arbitrary f:E->F has
scalar-line profiles

    f(z+t*u)=D(A(z),t)+B(z)*t+C(z),

where A,B,C:E->F and D:F->F->F are arbitrary. Every K44-free edge thinning
of c+d=f(a+x) obeys the same165888*q^27 fourth-power bound.

A functional ell with ell(u)=1 gives an EXPLICIT equivalence

    ker(ell) x F ~= E,  (v,t) -> v+t*u.

`lineChart` checks both inverses. The kernel has dimension2 and cardinalq^2.
On each of these parallel-line coordinate slices, row(a,c) has only three
profile parameters: A(a+v), B(a+v), C(a+v)-c. There are q^4 rows, q^2
slices, q scalar coordinates, and q^3 possible profiles per slice.
The already verified ProfileThinning.critical_scale_bound applies. The
proof transports the SELECTED graph by an honest vertex equivalence,
proves its embedding in the profile code, preserves freeness, and uses the
actual graph isomorphism to identify unordered edge counts. It does not
assume that every edge of a complete block survives in H.

For f=N*Tr in characteristic3:

    f(x+t)=T*t^3+T^2*t^2+(T*S)*t+N(x)*T.

Thus the three profiles are T,T*S,N*T, with D(T,t)=T*t^3+T^2*t^2.

In characteristic2 the cubic coefficient cancels instead:

    f(x+t)=t^4+(T^2+S)*t^2+(T*S+N(x))*t+N(x)*T.

There are again only three profiles, with D(A,t)=t^4+A*t^2.
`cubic_profile` and `cubic_profile_binary` verify these identities with
actual norms and traces, not a numerical field table.

For arbitrary nonzero L(z)=Tr(delta*z), use direction u=delta^-1 and
k=N(u). Then

    N(u*z)*L(u*z)=k*N(z)*Tr(z).

The three profiles rescale accordingly. In characteristic3, the second
leading coefficient becomes A^2/k; k is proved nonzero. In characteristic2
the leading term is simply k*t^4. Both normalized profile applications are
fully checked, including the trace-pairing representation of L.

### General copied-block averaging

`Erdos714LocalAveraging.edge_transitive_local_bound` proves: if G is
edge-transitive, A is a copied graph in G, and every F-free subgraph of A
has at most b edges, then every F-free spanning H<=G satisfies

    e(A)*e(H) <= b*e(G).

The block need not be induced. The proof intersects A with the transported
selected graph, rather than applying the local hypothesis to the full
comap. It counts unordered edges using the existing automorphism edge action.

### Sharp local K44-free bound inside K46

`Erdos714FourBySix.block_bound` proves that every K44-free subgraph of K46
has at most21 edges: at most three columns may meet all four rows, and
all remaining columns have degree at most three. `sharpGraph_free` and
`sharpGraph_edges` attain21 by deleting just the edges from row0 to
columns3,4,5. Consequently an edge-transitive host with a SUPPLIED actual
K46 copy has

    8*e(H) <= 7*e(G)

for every K44-free spanning subgraph H. `weighted_power_bound` applies to
the already established weighted-power graph API, with the K46 copy still
an explicit hypothesis. It does not infer six columns from four columns.

The7/8 factor is sharp for THIS SINGLE BLOCK. No global sharpness claim
for a whole norm graph is made. A fixed loss is compatible with a
constant-density free thinning and cannot disprove Erdős714.

### Important mathematical correction to the initial six-column attempt

The first unfinished version of OrdinaryNormSix made a FALSE claim of a
K46 for every characteristic-three base field. It is now replaced by a
correct conditional theorem; the false file was never compiled successfully.
Its old text is kept only as `/tmp/OrdinaryNormSix.invalid-attempt.txt`.

rows 0,1,-1 with weight1 and row theta with weight-1; its columns are
(theta,d), (theta+1,d), (theta-1,d), (c-theta,-c^3).

The failed attempt appended c+1-theta and c-1-theta with the SAME weight

### Four-point independence and five-point dependence

Work first over any field E, with a ring endomorphism sigma such that
sigma^3=id. No characteristic or finite-field assumption is needed for
the geometric argument. Put

    N(x)=x*sigma(x)*sigma^2(x),
    v(x)=(1,x,sigma(x),sigma^2(x),x*sigma(x),
          x*sigma^2(x),sigma(x)*sigma^2(x),N(x)) in E^8.

`four_independent` proves that any four distinct v(x_i) are linearly
independent OVER E. A product of three affine factors, one in each
conjugate coordinate, is a linear functional on E^8. Assigning one factor
to vanish on each of the other three points isolates any chosen coefficient.
The factors are nonzero at the chosen point by injectivity of sigma.

A nontrivial relation on five distinct points consequently has ALL five
coefficients nonzero (`five_relation_nonzero`). `transform` explicitly
tensors the three conjugate2-by-2 coordinate changes; it is an actual
linear map on E^8. No unproved projective-geometry API is assumed.

Normalize x0,x1,x2 to infinity,0,1 by the parameter

    t_i=((x2-x0)/(x2-x1))*(xi-x1)/(xi-x0).

`dependent_parameters_fixed` proves sigma(t3)=t3 and sigma(t4)=t4.
After normalization, the singleton and pair coordinates of the relation
have the form, for conjugate indices i,j:

    a+b*z_i+c*w_i=0,
    a+b*z_i*z_j+c*w_i*w_j=0,

with a,b,c nonzero. Elimination gives

    b*(b+c)*z_i*z_j + a*b*(z_i+z_j) + a*(a+c)=0.

If z is not fixed, its three conjugates are pairwise distinct. Subtracting
the three pair equations forces b*(b+c)=0 and then a*b=0, a contradiction.
The singleton equations then force w to be fixed as well. Importantly,
this argument DOES NOT assume that the dependence coefficients are in
the fixed field; they may be arbitrary E-elements.

### Dependent rows: a complete common-neighbor bound

Suppose five row points x_i, five column points y_j and nonzero weights
satisfy N(x_i+y_j)=a_i*b_j. Row0 guarantees x0+y_j!=0. Set

    u_i=1/(xi-x0) for i=1,2,3,4,
    w_j=1/(x0+y_j).

Then the original equations imply the exact norm-sphere equations

    N(u_i+w_j)=a_i/(a0*N(xi-x0)).

For dependent rows, `dependent_reciprocal_line` writes u_i=A*t_i+B,
where A!=0, the four t_i are distinct, and sigma(t_i)=t_i. All division
and injectivity hypotheses are verified, not omitted at poles.

`shift` is the explicit monic cubic

    P_z(T)=(T+z)*(T+sigma(z))*(T+sigma^2(z)).

For fixed t, P_z(t)=N(z+t). Four prescribed values determine P_z.
Thus all common points z_j=(B+w_j)/A have the same P_z, and -z_j are
roots of a single NONZERO cubic. There can be at most three such points.
`dependent_no_rectangle` supplies the needed five-point contradiction.

### Independent rows and columns: rank nine

The complete original norm equations are an orthogonality relation between
weighted vectors (v(x_i),a_i) and complementary-coordinate vectors
(reverse(v(y_j)),-b_j) in E^9. `complement_pairing` expands the norm of a
sum and checks the exact coordinate pairing.

If the five unweighted row vectors and five unweighted column vectors are
both independent, their weighted vectors are independent by projection.
The resulting5-by-9 and9-by-5 matrices have ranks5 and5, while their product
is zero. Mathlib's `rank_add_rank_le_card_of_mul_eq_zero` would give10<=9.
This is `independent_no_rectangle`. Combining the dependent and independent
cases yields `no_five_rectangle`, with NO generic-position exception.

### Actual field norm, graph freeness, and counts

For a finite cubic extension E/F, use sigma(z)=z^q. The equality |E|=q^3
proves sigma^3=id. Mathlib's `algebraMap_norm_eq_prod_pow` supplies the
actual field-norm conjugate formula. No coordinate norm is silently
identified with Algebra.norm.

Any graph biclique has distinct point coordinates on each side: sharing
one opposite neighbor and having equal point coordinates forces equal
nonzero weights, hence equal vertices. The Bool sides also agree within
each part. `normGraph_free` transfers `no_five_rectangle` to actual
SimpleGraph.Copy freeness for K55.

`normNeighborEquiv` is an explicit bijection between neighbors of a vertex
and E*, using the nonzero sum coordinate. Thus the graph has exactly

    2*q^3*(q-1) vertices,
    q^3*(q-1)*(q^3-1) unordered edges.

`finite_lower` bounds the corresponding extremal number. For F of order
2^k, use Mathlib's actual cubic `FiniteField.Extension F 2 3`; both its
algebra and degree are checked. For q>=2, the edge count is at leastq^7/4,
and the order is at most2*q^4. At n=32*16^k, `geometric_lower` gives

    (1/16)*n^(7/4) <= ex(n,K55).

The existing monotonic interpolation lemma gives `fifth_lower` at ALL
sufficiently large natural n, with a positive constant independent of n.
`larger_lower` transfers it to every r>=5 using forbidden-graph containment
in the correct direction.

### Denominator-safe sextic

For N(x)=x*sigma(x)*sigma^2(x), prescribe nonzero values
N(x)=a, N(x+1)=b, N(x+u)=c with u!=0,1. Put v=sigma(u),
w=sigma^2(u) and define

    Q(X)=(X+1)(X+a)-bX,
    L(X)=(X+1)(X+u)(w(v-1)X+a(1-w))-cX(X+1)+wbX(X+u),
    P(X)=L(X)^2-(v-w)(X+u)Q(X)L(X)
         +a(v-w)^2 X(X+1)^2(X+u)^2.

`degree_le` proves deg(P)<=6; `eval_neg_u` proves
P(-u)=c^2*u^2*(u-1)^2. Thus P!=0 uniformly, including exceptional
coefficient choices. No generic-leading-coefficient argument is used.

Writing y=sigma(x), elimination of the third coordinate gives

    f=(x+1)(y+1)(xy+a)-bxy=0,
    g=(x+u)(y+v)(wxy+a)-cxy=0.

With M=a(v-w)(x+1)(x+u), one has
L(x)y+M=(x+1)g-w(x+u)f=0, and the verified identity

    a(x+1)P(x)=L(x)^2*f
      -(x(x+1)(L(x)y-M)+Q(x)L(x))*(L(x)y+M).

Only a and x+1 are cancelled, and both are proved nonzero.
`norm_root` and `fiber_card_le_six` give at most SIX solutions.
If sigma(u)=u, P=L^2 with L nonzero of degree<=3, yielding
`fixed_fiber_card_le_three`. This is a conditional improvement;
no universal three-point bound is asserted.

### Actual four-row normalization

`normalize_spheres` sends three centers t0,t1,t2 to 0,1,u,
where u=(t2-t0)/(t1-t0), and divides all norm values by N(t1-t0).
The affine map is injective and all normalized values are nonzero.
`three_spheres_card_le_six` and `fixed_three_spheres_card_le_three`
apply the finite-fiber bounds to arbitrary finite indexed sets.

For N(x_i+y_j)=a_i*b_j with four distinct rows and nonzero weights,
`normalize_rows` uses

    t_i=1/(x_{i+1}-x0), s_j=1/(x0+y_j),
    c_i=a_{i+1}/(a0*N(x_{i+1}-x0)).

It proves N(t_i+s_j)=c_i, injectivity of the reciprocal columns,
and nonvanishing of every denominator and every c_i.
`four_rows_card_le_six` therefore bounds the number of columns by six.
`fixed_four_rows_card_le_three` bounds it by three IF sigma(u)=u.
`parameter_eq_crossRatio` identifies the parameter exactly:

    u=((x2-x0)*(x3-x1))/((x2-x1)*(x3-x0)).

Finally `graph_free_of_norm_formula` and `normGraph_free` transfer the

one shared opposite neighbor, not assumed for graph embeddings.

norm product theorem. The sextic itself needs no sigma^3=id hypothesis.

## Fixed-cross-ratio restrictions: exact point and local edge budgets

Completed `Submission/FixedCrossRatioSize.lean`, importing the self-contained
CubicNormFour chain. Log `/tmp/FixedCrossRatioSize.log`; installed olean is
current. Five audited theorems use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

### Projective-chart size bound

For three distinct field points a,b,c, define

    coordinate(a,b,c,d)=((c-a)/(c-b))*((d-b)/(d-a)).

`coordinate_inj` proves this map injective away from d=a, with every
cancelled difference checked nonzero. The images of b and c are 0 and 1.
For q>1, if all images from a finite set S minus a satisfy z^q=z, they
inject into the roots of the nonzero degree-q polynomial X^q-X. Thus
`card_le_of_chart_fixed` proves |S|<=q+1.

`card_le_of_all_quadruples_fixed` only assumes the fixed-power condition
for DISTINCT quadruples. Sets of size<=2 are handled separately; otherwise
choose three base points, handle b and c by their explicit chart values,
and apply the condition to all remaining points. `finiteField_point_bound`
identifies the power map with the actual finite-field Frobenius.

`coordinate_eq_parameter` checks equality with the four-row reciprocal
normalization parameter from CubicNormFour. Thus this restriction really
is the sufficient condition in the previous three-common-column theorem.

### Stronger local restriction also loses the critical density

For an arbitrary edge subgraph H of the actual weighted norm graph, define
`neighborPoints H p` as the image of the retained neighbors under the point
projection. The projection is injective on each neighborhood: the side is
fixed, and equality of point coordinates forces equality of the weights
by cancelling the nonzero weight of p in the norm equation.

Suppose EVERY distinct quadruple in EVERY neighborPoints H p has fixed
cross-ratio. Then `local_degree_bound` gives

    degree_H(p) <= q+1.

This is a LOCAL hypothesis, weaker than requiring the entire point set
of H to lie on one fixed-field subline. Summing degrees proves

    e(H) <= |E|*(q-1)*(q+1).

For a cubic extension, comparison with the exact norm-graph edge count
proves `local_relative_bound`:

    (q^3-1)*e(H) <= (q+1)*e(normGraph).

Thus this particular sufficient geometric rule retains at most a fraction
(q+1)/(q^3-1), tending to zero, rather than a positive constant fraction.

IMPORTANT SCOPE: A K44-free subgraph need NOT obey this local rule.
Four nonfixed-cross-ratio rows can share ONE neighbor without causing K44.
The theorem therefore does NOT exclude arbitrary constant-density thinnings
of ordinary norm graphs, and does NOT disprove the original conjecture.
No assertion excluding all bounded-degree algebraic or group constructions
has been proved. Broader geometric/code considerations in this continuation
were exploratory only and produced no further candidate or theorem.

Spec was not edited in this continuation. The sole r>=4 sorry remains;
no complete proof or disproof of Erdos714.erdos_714 has been obtained.

base-field weights. The tested kernels were:

   viewed as a TWO-INPUT kernel before applying the cubic field norm.

The unmodified two-term Gold kernel is not a new construction: factoring

on the transformed point set. The map x->x^(sigma-1) is a permutation
when sigma has fixed field F2. This observation motivated the extra terms;
no new formal theorem for this factorization was added here.

## Relative Suzuki norm equality: nonzero certificates at q8 and q32

A further genuinely different candidate replaces the rank-one weight product
by the Suzuki form on the base field itself. With k odd, q=2^k,
E=F_(q^3), sigma(z)=z^(2^((3k+1)/2)), define

    Q_E(x,y)=x^2*sigma(x)+x*y+sigma(y),
    adjacency: N_(E/F)(Q_E(x,y))=Q_F(a,b).

Here Q_F uses the RESTRICTION of the same sigma to the embedded Fq.
This is not the previous equation with right side a*b, nor a change of
vertex coordinates justified to preserve that equation. The tempting
variant with right side Q_F(a,b)^3 has an immediate base-field diagonal
copy (x,a)=(a,a), (y,b)=(b,b), since the cubic norm restricts to cubing;
that variant was not pursued.

Script `/tmp/relative_suzuki_norm.sage` uses the fixed nonzero first row
(1,1), enumerates its nonzero column neighbors by solving Q_F(1,b), then
tests base-field row sets including (1,t,t^2,t+t^2). For each column it
inverts Q_F(a,b) in a and groups compatible row-weight triples. Thus every
reported copy satisfies the ORIGINAL relative equality, not a ratio test
valid only for multiplicative weights.

### Singer argument superseded by an elementary binary sumset obstruction

An informal approach through the cubic Singer difference set was developed:
for odd binary exponent, trace-zero v gives t=v^3/N(v) with norm and trace
one. Perfect-difference-set second moments force a trace-zero element in a
fixed-index subgroup once q is sufficiently large. This was NOT formalized,
because a stronger elementary argument was found:

Four DISTINCT elements a,b,c,d in a characteristic-two additive group with

    a+b+c+d=0

produce K44 in the sum graph: take rows 0,a+b,a+c,a+d and columns a,b,c,d.
Every sum is one of the four columns. Thus a K44-free connection set S must
have distinct sums for all its unordered pairs, and all pair sums are nonzero.
Consequently

    choose(|S|,2) <= |E|-1.

This is not a probabilistic estimate. It applies to EVERY retained set.
In a weighted graph N(x+y)=a*b, fix one label c, take row weight one and
column weight c, and apply this bound to the retained label fiber. The label
map N:E->A can be ANY function into a finite commutative group A.
Cauchy--Schwarz over the fibers gives, writing Q=|E|, W=|A|, d=|D|:

    d^2 <= W*(2*Q*W+d).

Each vertex has exactly d neighbors (sum determines the opposite weight),
so e=Q*W*d. If Q=q^3 and W<=q, then

    d^2 <= 3*q^5,       e^2 <= 3*q^13.

Thus ANY common sum restriction of a cubic binary norm graph loses a power
of q if it is K44-free. In particular it cannot retain a fixed positive
fraction of the original Theta(q^7) edges. This result is stronger than
merely excluding fixed-index multiplicative subgroups, and holds for ALL
binary extension parities, not only odd exponents.

## Arbitrary translation-invariant binary thinnings: uniform power loss

This continuation strengthens the preceding sum-filter theorem. It still
DOES NOT exclude arbitrary thinnings without translation symmetry, and it
DOES NOT settle Erdős714. The main Spec file has not been modified.

### Broader symmetry class

Let E be a finite characteristic-two field, A ANY finite label type (no
multiplication or other structure on A is required), and H a simple graph
on Bool x (E x A). Suppose:

1. Every edge joins distinct Boolean parts.
2. H ITSELF is invariant under simultaneous translation of point coordinates:

    H.Adj (b,x,a) (c,y,d) iff H.Adj (b,x+z,a) (c,y+z,d), for every z in E.

Then, for each ordered pair of labels (a,b), define

    S_ab = {s in E : H.Adj (false,0,a) (true,s,b)}.

The symmetry gives the exact equivalence

    H.Adj (false,x,a) (true,y,b) iff x+y in S_ab.

In contrast to the previous common-D model, S_ab may depend ARBITRARILY
on BOTH labels. No common connection set, norm equation, or algebraic
label map is assumed in the general theorem.

If H is K44-free, the binary sum graph on S_ab copies into H, so its
unordered-pair sums are injective. In particular

    |S_ab|^2 <= 3*|E|.

The neighbor set of (false,x,a) is a disjoint union, over b, of translated
S_ab. Bipartite degree summation gives the EXACT count

    e(H) = |E| * sum_(a,b) |S_ab|.

Cauchy--Schwarz now proves

    e(H)^2 <= 3*|E|^3*|A|^4.

At |E|=q^3 and |A|<=q this is e(H)^2<=3*q^13, even for arbitrary
weight-dependent retained sum sets.

### Scope: what this does and does not exclude

The theorem now excludes ALL point-translation-invariant thinnings, not
only multiplicative subgroup filters or a sum set common to every weight
pair. In particular, changing a retained sum rule separately for each
ordered pair of weights cannot repair the cubic binary norm graph while
preserving a constant fraction of its edges.

It does NOT follow that an arbitrary K44-free subgraph H is invariant
because its HOST is invariant. Averaging or taking the translation closure
of H need not preserve K44-freeness. No such unjustified symmetrization has
been used. Arbitrary symmetry-breaking thinnings of ordinary norm graphs
remain unexcluded by these results.

### Candidate and derived polynomial test

Reviewed lower-degree varieties as alternatives to twisted Segre norm graphs.
No new classification or uniform exclusion of all algebraic constructions
was proved in that review. A concrete different candidate was then examined:
for a quartic finite extension E/F and c in F, use point vertices x in E,
with the diagonal norm weight N(x)+c, and adjacency

    N(x+y)=(N(x)+c)*(N(y)+c),

excluding vertices whose displayed weight is zero. There are O(q^4) point
vertices. The suggested q^7 edge scale was only a parameter-count heuristic;
NO uniform critical-density edge lower bound for this candidate was proved.
This is not a common-sum restriction of the ordinary cubic norm graph, and
it is not covered automatically by the binary translation-invariance theorem.

Take four distinct base-field rows lambda_i, Q(T)=product(T-lambda_i), and
choose k satisfying

    k*(Q(0)+1-c)=1-2*c.

Define the quartic pencil

    p(T)=k*Q(T)+(1-k)*(T^4+c).

At each row p(lambda_i)=(1-k)*(lambda_i^4+c), while the scalar identity gives
p(0)+c=1-k. Therefore

    p(lambda_i)=(lambda_i^4+c)*(p(0)+c).

If p is irreducible of degree4, its four conjugate roots theta_i provide
columns y_i=-theta_i: N(lambda_i+y_j)=p(lambda_i), N(y_j)=p(0).
With nonzero displayed weights this is an actual K44 in the ORIGINAL graph.
This derivation, not a blind full-graph search, guided the finite checks.

`irreducible_map` proves a general field fact: a monic irreducible p remains
irreducible over any finite-dimensional base extension K/F whose degree
is coprime to deg p. Proof: choose a monic irreducible factor g of p over K,
let L=K[T]/g and theta its root. Then minpoly_F(theta)=p, so deg p divides
[L:F]=[K:F]*deg g by the simple-adjoin degree and tower formulas. Coprimality
forces deg p to divide deg g, while divisibility g|p gives deg g<=deg p.
The equal-degree monic factor is p itself. No finite-field-only or
separability assumption is used in this arithmetic lemma.

## Additive-weight rational cubic norm lift: uniform K46 obstruction

New candidate (not the earlier rational interpolation or binary gluing models):
vertices (x,a) in E x F, for a cubic finite extension E/F, relation

    a-b = N((x+y)/(x-y)),

with x,y,a,b,x-y,x+y all nonzero. The formal graph is bipartite, with
two copies of E x F; all six nonzero guards are in the actual relation.

For odd characteristic and |F|>=5, choose u not in {0,1,-1}. Set
R(z)=(z^3-u^2*z)/(z^2-1). Total field division gives R(1)=R(-1)=0,
so R is not injective, and hence not surjective on the finite field.
Choose a missing value t. Then t!=0, and

    p(T)=T^3-t*T^2-u^2*T+t

has no base-field root: outside +-1 a root would give R(z)=t, while
p(+-1) is +- (1-u^2)!=0. Thus p is irreducible.

Let theta_j be its three conjugate roots. The four rows are

    (1,u+1), (-1,u+1), (u,u-1), (-u,u-1),

and the six columns are (theta_j,u), (-theta_j,u), j=0,1,2.
N(lambda-theta)=p(lambda), N(lambda+theta)=-p(-lambda).
At lambda=+-1 the norm ratio is1; at lambda=+-u it is-1.
Replacing theta by -theta reciprocates these two values and keeps them.
All point and weight coordinates, numerators, and denominators are nonzero.
The opposite conjugate triples are disjoint because their norms are -t
and t, distinct in odd characteristic.

A nonzero root x forces c=(-x^3+t*x^2+n)/x. There are only q-1 possible

### Key new mathematical argument

Start from a constant nonzero-norm binary affine plane p+{0,u,v,u+v}.
Its two directions u,v are necessarily F-linearly independent: otherwise
four distinct points of one F-affine line would have the same cubic norm,
contradicting the already checked NormLineBound.cubic_direction_zero.

Let w be the image under the chosen linear equivalence of the central
coordinate (0,0,1). Multiplication by c=w/u aligns u with w. The other
direction v'=c*v cannot be central, by that F-linear independence.

For Q(x,y)=x^2+x*y+eta*y^2 anisotropic, set

  k=Q(first two coordinates of v'), s=1/k.

Then k!=0, and scaling the whole plane by s makes its central direction
(0,0,s), while Q(first two coordinates of s*v')=s^2*k=s.
Choose a group element g whose first two coordinates are those of s*v',
and whose central coordinate cancels the cocycle at the affine base point.
Then g sends the base point to its translate by s*v', and g^2 is exactly
the other (central) plane direction. Thus the four norm-plane points are
an actual cyclic-four group orbit. Four row powers of g and four points
of that orbit give K44 with constant weights on each side.

For the complementary isotropic case, take t with t^2+t+eta=0. On the
coordinate plane x=t*y the bilinear cocycle vanishes BETWEEN directions.
Use exists_plane_in_kernel for that scalar coordinate functional. Correct
each row's central coordinate for its interaction with the affine base
point. The four corrected rows are involutions, and their relative action
on all four columns is the required additive plane translation. This yields
K44 as well. If no such t exists, Q is anisotropic by division by y. Hence
all eta are covered, not merely selected irreducible parameters.

a proof of the main conjecture.

### Candidate and mathematical diagnosis

Let P=Sz(q), q=2^(2m+1), B=U*T a Borel subgroup, and A=AGL(1,q).
The Borel has a quotient map

    phi(U(x,y)*T(c)) = (slope=c, translation=x).

It forgets the central root coordinate y. In P*A take the diagonal subgroup
H={(b,phi(b)):b in B}. Its index is q(q-1)(q^2+1), of order q^4.
For g=(w,tau), where w is the Weyl involution and tau(t)=t+1, the intended
orbital degree is q^2(q-1), of order q^3. The standard Borel intersection and
group-order identities used in these two counts have NOT been formalized
anew in this continuation.

There is, however, an explicit growing grid. The torus factorization is

    T(c)*w*T(c)=w,
    phi(T(c))*tau*phi(T(c)) = (slope=c^2, translation=c).

The latter labels are distinct as c ranges over Fq*. The kernel elements
U(0,y), y in Fq, have distinct opposite Borel cosets. Hence they and the
q-1 labels give K_(q-1,q) in the actual diagonal coset graph. This is a
structural argument; no numerical search was used. In particular, retaining
a fixed positive fraction of edges cannot fix this edge-transitive host:
the averaged KST bound loses a factor of order q^(-1/4).

Scope: the Suzuki specialization here is a mathematical derivation using
its standard Borel identities. The new Lean theorem is the GENERAL kernel
grid criterion with those identities and coset injectivity as explicit
hypotheses. It does not instantiate or classify the Suzuki group in Lean.

`Submission/DoubleCosetAveraging.lean` (about 125 lines), imports
DoubleCosetOrbital and EdgeAveraging. Namespace Erdos714DoubleCoset.

* `rightPerm`: well-defined right multiplication on the actual right cosets.
* `relation_right_iff`, `rightIso`: exact adjacency preservation.
* `edge_transitive`: every double-coset orbital is edge-transitive, with no
  free-pair assumption.
* `biclique_thinning_bound`: for a copied K_(t,t), every K_(r,r)-free
  subgraph J of the host G satisfies

      t^2 * e(J) <= ex(2*t,K_(r,r)) * e(G).

`Submission/DiagonalCosetKernel.lean` (121 lines), imports
DoubleCosetAveraging. Namespace Erdos714DiagonalCosetKernel.

For a subgroup B of P and a homomorphism phi:B->A, `diagonal` is the actual
range of b |-> (b,phi(b)). `kernelCopy` takes:

* u_i*w*v_i=w;
* phi(k_j)=1;
* pairwise distinct labels z_i=phi(u_i)*a*phi(v_i);
* w^-1*k_i^-1*k_j*w in B implies i=j.

It constructs an actual K_(r,s) in the right-coset graph with connecting
representative (w,a)^-1. Representatives are

    left_i  = (1,z_i),
    right_j = (w^-1*k_j^-1,1).

The inverse convention is essential: using (k_j*w,1) in the RIGHT-coset
library would collapse all those columns to the same coset. The proof checks
both injections and every double-coset factorization. `not_free` specializes
to K44, and `thinning_bound` combines the construction with edge averaging.

## Odd cubic norm grids: arbitrary full weight columns excluded (Lean verified)

A new uniform result, distinct from the earlier characteristic-two arbitrary
weight-law theorem and the characteristic-three multiplicative templates.
It does NOT settle the original conjecture.

### Elementary construction, no numerical search

Work over any finite field F with 2 and 3 nonzero, in any cubic extension E.
The map x |-> x^3-x is not injective (zero and one collide), hence not
surjective. Choose d outside its image. Then d!=0 and

    X^3-X-d

is irreducible. Let r0,r1,r2 be its distinct conjugate roots in E. They have
sum zero, each has trace zero, and

    N(ri+t)=t^3-t+d        for t in F.

In particular N(ri), N(ri+1), N(ri-1) all equal d. Put v=r1-r2 and take

    left points:  1+r0, -1+r0, 1-r0, -1-r0;
    right points: 1+v,  -1+v,  1-v,  -1-v.

For each fixed row, all four norm values are equal. They are respectively

    -8d, -8d, 8d, 8d.

Indeed r0+v=-2r2, r0-v=-2r1, -r0+v=2r1, and -r0-v=2r2. Each cross sum
is therefore plus or minus twice one of ri, ri+1, ri-1.

Distinctness is essential. Both r0 and v are nonzero and trace zero. Since
3!=0, neither can equal 1 or -1. Since 2!=0, each four-corner set is
injectively parameterized. This explains exactly why the same template is
not valid in characteristics two or three.

Surjectivity of the actual finite-field norm then scales both point sets to
realize ANY prescribed nonzero opposite values c,c,-c,-c.

### Completed Lean file

`Submission/OddCubicNormGrid.lean`, about 340 lines. Imports
CubicTraceNormPlane and QuinticNormProduct; namespace
Erdos714OddCubicNormGrid. Warning-free compile, installed olean, log
`/tmp/OddCubicNormGrid.log`. All six audited declarations use only propext,
Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

* `exists_irreducible`: the missing-value cubic argument.
* `exists_conjugates`: transfers the actual irreducible cubic to ANY finite
  cubic model, enumerates its Galois conjugates, and proves the norm/trace
  identities. There is no assumed coordinate norm or unproved splitting.
* `exists_grid`: actual injective point sets and all sixteen norm identities.
* `exists_grid_value`: arbitrary nonzero prescribed amplitude, via the
  finite-field norm-surjectivity theorem.
* `graph H`: actual relation N(x+y)=H(a,b), with arbitrary weight-label types
  and an arbitrary, possibly nonlinear/nonseparable law H.
* `contains_copy_of_opposites`, `not_free_of_opposites`: if ONE column b has
  values H(ap,b)=c and H(am,b)=-c with c!=0, the graph contains K44.
* `not_free_of_full_column`: consequently any column attaining every
  nonzero field value rules out freeness. This includes all full Latin-type
  nonzero weight laws, not just multiplication.
* `column_image_bound`: in a free model, every column's set S of distinct
  nonzero values satisfies 2*|S| <= |F|-1. Labels may be repeated.

### Scope and remaining possibilities

This is not a bound for arbitrary edge thinnings, nor for every restricted
weight set. In particular, an image avoiding opposite nonzero values is
not excluded by this theorem; square classes when -1 is nonsquare require
a different argument. The characteristic-three arbitrary nonlinear weight
case is also not covered by this odd-grid theorem.

A review observation, NOT formalized here: for a nonvanishing quadratic
weight column on all of F, each value has at most two preimages, so its image
has at least (q+1)/2 nonzero values. The new image bound would rule that out.
No new theorem for every quadratic weight law or every characteristic is
claimed.

## Nonabelian Dickson-nearfield quotients: two further exact failures

A second, genuinely nonabelian variant retains a fixed factor ell in the
quotient. Suppose q=1 mod 3, M=3*ell*(q-1) divides N=q^3-1. On exponents
modulo M use the ACTUAL group law

    a*b = a + q^(a mod 3)*b (mod M).

The quotient from nearfield exponents modulo N is reduction modulo M, not
the abelian piecewise nu. The group law is associative: q=1 mod 3 means
the product's class is a+b modulo 3, and q^3=1 modulo M means the two
Frobenius powers compose consistently. The inverse of a is
-q^(-a mod 3)*a modulo M. When ell=7 and q has order three modulo 7, the
group is noncommutative.

Actual bipartite adjacency, with E=F_(q^3):

    x+y != 0, log_g(x+y) mod M = a*b.

Its two parts have q^3*M vertices each and degree q^3-1, so FIXED ell
preserves the desired q^4/q^3 scale. This is not the previous dihedral
voltage cover. Normalized first rows (0,0),(1,w) yield direct colors

    color(x,y)=log_g(x+y)-q^((log_g(x+y)-log_g(y)) mod 3)*log_g(y) mod M.

## Quadratic-norm fusion over a Sidon parabola: exact failures

The degree-five review gave no new positive candidate: the existing
QuadraticConeThinning theorem already excludes its displayed chart over
all fields, not just characteristic three. A different construction was
then derived, with its own exact size calculation.

Let q=1 mod 4, d a nonsquare in Fq, E=Fq[T]/(T^4-d), alpha=T^2, and
K=Fq(alpha). The polynomial T^4-d is irreducible. Use the nonzero parabola

    B={a+alpha*a^2 : a in Fq, a!=0} subset K*.

B is an additive Sidon set, including the unordered-pair condition with
repeated summands: the sum determines a+b and a^2+b^2, hence ab, hence the
unordered pair. On two copies of E, join x,y when N_(E/K)(x+y) belongs to B.
Norm surjectivity and its fiber size give exactly

    q^4 vertices per part,
    (q-1)*(q^2+1) neighbors per vertex.

Thus this DOES have the required fourth-case scale. It is not the earlier
Suzuki norm fusion, upper-half-plane fusion, or additive parabola composition.
Writing z=a+b*T+c*T^2+e*T^3, its actual norm is U+alpha*V, where

    U=a^2+d*c^2-2*d*b*e,
    V=2*a*c-b^2-d*e^2.

The exact edge predicate is U!=0 and V=U^2. The Sidon property removes
some rectangular norm-level patterns, but is NOT sufficient for freeness.

At q=5,d=2, a K44 is
 left: 0, 1, 4+2*T^2, 3*T^2;
 right: 3+2*T, 3+3*T, 3+4*T^2+2*T^3, 3+4*T^2+3*T^3.
The norm-level parameters a in B, row by row, are
 [4,4,1,1], [1,1,3,3], [2,2,1,1], [2,2,2,2].
Here the conjugate column pairs explain part of the failure. No claim is
made that every field or every later edge orientation shares that pattern.

At q=13,d=2, another K44 is
 left: 0, 1, 2+T, 4+T;
 right: 10+7*T, 11+5*T^2+T^3,
        4+12*T+3*T^2+4*T^3, 12+3*T+6*T^3.
Its norm-level parameters are
 [9,2,11,7], [4,12,7,6], [1,7,2,9], [1,11,4,4].

The independent Sage verifier constructs the ACTUAL field, verifies the
modulus is irreducible, computes N(z)=z^(q^2+1) rather than using the search's
coordinate formula, verifies the Sidon property and all sixteen edges and
injections, and counts EVERY nonzero norm fiber over B. The checked degrees

### Uniform arithmetic, now Lean verified

For every characteristic-three field, if 2d=3^s+1 and d is even,

    P_d(X^2,-Y^2) = ((X+Y)^d-(X-Y)^d)^2.

In a field E of order3^n with n odd, x^d=y^d implies x=y or x=-y.
Proof for nonzero ratio a: a^d=1 implies a^(3^s)=a^(-1). Iterating that
power n times, oddness gives a^(-1), whereas the finite-field cardinality
identity gives a. Thus a^2=1. This does NOT require coprimality of s and n.
Consequently the displayed square is NONZERO for X,Y both nonzero.

Let F have order q=3^m with m odd, [E:F]=3. Put Sq(K)=the actual subgroup
of squares in K*. Every square/opposite-square point pair therefore has a
nonzero square norm, and

    |Sq(E)|=(q^3-1)/2,  |Sq(F)|=(q-1)/2.

Fix any four distinct square row points. A column point gives only THREE
independent weight ratios after the first weight is normalized. There are
|Sq(F)|^3 profiles. If more than three times that many admissible column
points remain, a fiber of size four supplies the actual K44.

For q>=27, even deleting up to q+26 column point values per row leaves

    3*((q-1)/2)^3 + 4*(q+26) < (q^3-1)/2.

Thus no choice of odd s rescues this FULL weighted polarization family,
including s depending on q. This is stronger than the finite diagnostics.
