## Length-three path amplification: arbitrary thinning bound (Lean verified)

New Submission/PathAmplification.lean imports ColoredTensorThinning and
BlowupThinning. Installed olean; clean log /tmp/PathAmplification.log.
Seven printed axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
This is a construction obstruction, not a proof or disproof of Erdos714.

The general host composes three arbitrary finite set systems

  R:A->Finset B, S:B->Finset C, T:C->Finset D.

Its A-by-D relation is: there exist b in R(a), c in S(b), d in T(c).
Each actual middle edge (b,c), indexed by Sigma b, S(b), supplies the block

  {a : b in R(a)} disjoint-union T(c).

block_size, forward_cover and edge_cover prove the endpoint cover. Multiple
length-three walks may project to the same edge; no uniqueness or equality
between edge counts and path counts is assumed or needed. The index has
exactly sum_b |S(b)| elements, and only an UPPER edge-cover bound is used.

fourth_power proves, for ANY K44-free edge subgraph H of this host, if both
outer sides of every block have size at most d,

  e(H)^4 <= 10368*(sum_b |S(b)|)^4*d^7.

It allows empty blocks and d=0. critical_fourth specializes to

  sum_b |S(b)|<=q^5, d<=q ==> e(H)^4<=10368*q^27.

size_budget: q>0 and q^7<=K*e(H) additionally imply q<=10368*K^4.
This result applies to arbitrary edge selections, not just retention or
removal of entire middle-edge blocks.

walkThree(R)=host(R,dual(R),R) is the exact relation of alternating
length-three WALKS in a base bipartite graph. Simple-path-only and
nonbacktracking variants are subgraphs and hence fall within the same
thinning estimate. walk_thinning proves e(H)^4<=10368*q^27 if the base row
side has at most q^4 vertices and both base degree bounds are at most q.
The proof counts actual middle edges via sum_dual_card and the row-degree
bound. There is no girth or unique-path hypothesis.

Scope: this excludes the naive degree-q, order-q^4 path amplification even
with arbitrary post-selection. It does NOT exclude schemes with larger
base degrees, different parameter scales, endpoint-dependent local factors,
or all graph amplification operations. No exact full-host lower edge count
or new high-girth graph existence theorem was added. The more ambitious
oversampled/local-factor versions remain unconstructed.

Spec.lean is unchanged, with the original theorem type/import and its sole
sorry at line2982 for r>=4. No valid complete proof/disproof has been obtained
or submitted. No active computation or unfinished Lean repair remains.

## Every semilinear coefficient has a four-point fiber; three-term norm excluded (Lean)

New Submission/ReeThreeTerm.lean imports ReePositiveGrid and UnbalancedBounds.
Installed olean; clean log /tmp/ReeThreeTerm.final.log. Twelve printed axiom
audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No external numerical
search was used for the new results. Spec.lean was not modified.

### Uniform coefficient strengthening of the scalar root theorem

For any finite characteristic-three F, sigma:F->F with sigma^2(x)=x^3, and
|F|>3, every_coefficient_fiber proves for EVERY prescribed A!=0:

  exists b, exists f:Fin4 injects into F,
  (f(i))^2-A*sigma(f(i))=b for all i.

exact_four_fiber strengthens this to an actual fiber of cardinality exactly4.
The upper bound uses the already checked quartic eliminant. Neither theorem
needs a square-class assumption on A or on -1.

This is stronger than merely finding some four-function combination with
four roots. centered_fiber first translates the old four roots to remove the
linear term. In the earlier notation c=sigma(t)-t, put

  u=(t^2-sigma(t))/c, a=t*(t-1)/c.

Then x=z-u transforms the original equation into

  x^2-a*sigma(x)=u^2+a*sigma(u),

with a!=0. To reach any target A!=0, use z=A/a and the nonzero scale
s=z^2*sigma(z). scale_identity checks s^2=z*sigma(s), hence
A*sigma(s)=a*s^2. Scaling the four inputs by s produces the required fiber.
All divisions, distinctness, and original equations are verified.

### Even norm and positive translated levels

Define evenNorm(x)=x*sigma(x). normHom maps F^* to its square subgroup.
The kernel has at most2 elements: x*sigma(x)=1, after applying sigma, forces
x^2=1. Cardinality then proves norm_preimage: every nonzero square has a
nonzero preimage. evenNorm(-x)=evenNorm(x) is checked separately.

For -1 nonsquare and |F|>3, two_positive_levels proves that for EVERY b there
are distinct nonzero squares r,s such that b+r and b+s are nonzero squares.
It uses the existing three-consecutive-squares lemma:
* for b square, take r=b*(x-1), s=b*x;
* for b nonsquare, -b is square and use r=(-b)*x, s=(-b)*(x+1);
* b=0 is handled separately.

Choosing preimages u,v of r,s gives four distinct inputs u,-u,v,-v, all with
b+evenNorm(input) nonzero square. four_positive_norm_values proves the actual
embedding and every label condition.

### Precise new graph; not a redefinition of the original norm

This file investigates the SIMPLIFIED three-term kernel

  N(a,b,c)=b*sigma(b)+c^2-a*sigma(c),

not the original seven-term Ree norm. Relative coordinates are exactly the
previously displayed Erdos714ReeNegative.relative formula. Both vertex sides
are F^3 times all nonzero square labels. For an arbitrary predicate P:F->Prop,
adjacency requires

  P(relative(rowPoint,columnPoint).first),
  N(relative(rowPoint,columnPoint))=rowWeight*columnWeight.

copy and not_free prove an actual K44 whenever P accepts ANY nonzero A,
assuming sigma^2=cubing, -1 nonsquare, |F|>3. Thus restricting the first
relative coordinate to a square class, a nonsquare class, or even a singleton
nonzero value cannot repair this FULL graph.

Choose four x_i in the fiber x^2-A*sigma(x)=b, and four y_j from
four_positive_norm_values at that b. The actual vertices are

  rows ((0,0,-x_i),1),
  columns ((A,y_j,0), b+y_j*sigma(y_j)).

axis_identity checks their ORIGINAL relative norms, and copy verifies both
injections, the guard P, all sixteen incidences, and every nonzero-square
label. No associativity or classification of a Ree group is assumed.
finite_not_free specializes the actual twist x^(3^(m+1)) at EVERY field
order 3^(2*m+1), m>=1.

The remaining guard case is also quantified. zero_guard_edges proves that
if P accepts only zero, the full graph has at most q^6 undirected edges.
For a fixed row, the first column coordinate is forced; the other two point
coordinates determine the column weight by division by a unit. Thus every
row degree is at most q^2, and there are at most q^4 rows. Consequently
free_host_edges says EVERY K44-free FULL member of this filtered family
has e<=q^6, below the q^7 target.

IMPORTANT SCOPE: this is NOT an arbitrary-edge-thinning bound for the
three-term kernel, and it does NOT classify every semilinear norm change or
all graphs with positive-square labels. The original ReePositiveGrid theorem
continues to concern the DIFFERENT, original norm. None of these construction
obstructions is the negation of the conjecture in Spec.

Main status remains unresolved. Spec's exact original theorem type/import
are intact; its sole sorry at line2982 covers r>=4. No valid complete proof
or disproof has been obtained or submitted. No pending Lean repair or active
computation remains.

## Crossed scalar tags: exact blocks and arbitrary-thinning obstruction (Lean verified)

New complete file Submission/CrossedScalarNorm.lean (381 lines), importing
Submission.VoltageFusion. Namespace Erdos714CrossedScalar. Installed olean;
/tmp/CrossedScalarNorm.final.log is warning-free and prints fourteen axiom
audits, all using only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry,
extra axiom, or native_decide. Spec.lean was not changed.

### Precise model

Let F be a finite field of order q, X and Y arbitrary finite types,
ν:X->Y->F arbitrary, f:X->F arbitrary, g:Y->F* arbitrary. Rows are (x,a,t)
in X*F*F and columns (y,b,s) in Y*F*F. Adjacency is exactly

  ν(x,y) != 0,    ν(x,y) = (a+s*f(x))*(b+t*g(y)).

The two scalar tag interactions are crossed. Scalar coordinates a,b,t,s
may be zero; only g(y) and the actual ν value are required nonzero.
The result does NOT assume polynomial degree, rank, or fiber-size bounds.
It does not concern all doubly endpoint-dependent permutations of whole
local K33-free factors.

### Complete blocks and exact edge partition

Index i=(x,s,B,D), with D in F*. Rows indexed by u in F* are

  (x, D/u-s*f(x), u-B).

Columns are

  (y, B*g(y), s), where ν(x,y)=D*g(y).

These are actual injective maps, and block_incidence verifies the original
relation. An edge recovers B=b/g(y), D=ν(x,y)/g(y), u=B+t uniquely.
edge_partition proves an exact bijection for arbitrary selected edges,
not merely a cover. block_free transfers actual graph freeness.

fiber_sum: summing the nonzero D-fiber sizes counts exactly those y with
ν(x,y)!=0. No uniform fiber bound is needed.

Each selected block has at most q-1 rows. If its column size is m, the
unbalanced estimate and q>=1 imply

  e_block^4 <= 672*q^3*(m+q)^4.

The existing homogeneous sum lemma passes this bound to the sum without
an additional factor in the number of blocks. weight_sum bounds the total
of the weights m+q by |X|*q^2*(|Y|+q^2).

Consequently set_system_fourth and graph_fourth prove, when |X|,|Y|<=q^2,
for EVERY K44-free arbitrary edge thinning H:

  e(H)^4 <= 10752*q^27.

size_budget: q^7<=K*e(H) implies q<=10752*K^4. Thus no fixed positive
critical-scale edge fraction survives at unbounded q.

edge_count gives the exact full-host count

  e(G)=q^2*(q-1)*sum_x |{y:ν(x,y)!=0}|.

not_free constructs a K44 whenever q>=5 and some x has more than
3*(q-1) nonzero ν values, by finding a fiber with at least four columns.

### Quadratic norm specialization

For E/F quadratic, |E|=q^2, X=Y=E, ν(x,y)=N(x+y), with ANY f:E->F and
ANY g:E->F*, norm_host_size proves

  |V(G)|=2*q^4,    e(G)=q^4*(q-1)*(q^2-1).

norm_thinning is the same 10752*q^27 arbitrary-thinning bound.
norm_not_free proves the full host contains K44 for every q>=5.

The ordinary cubic norm-graph arbitrary-thinning review produced no

The new crossed-scalar theorem concerns a different quadratic-norm tag

The genuinely arbitrary two-sided local-factor permutation scheme remains

## Bounded-common-neighbor thinning review: no new theorem

Reviewed CubicNormFive, FourBySix, RandomVoltage, UniformPackingReduction,
and SmallDoublingPacking again. No Lean source was modified in this review.

The ordinary norm graph's bounded common-neighbor property is not itself a
proved positive-density thinning construction. The local K46 deletion bound
is sharp (21 of24 edges), but averaging gives only an upper bound7/8 on
retained density. It neither constructs a globally compatible deletion nor
allows repeated multiplication of7/8. No theorem excluding all arbitrary
norm-graph edge thinnings has been established.

The random-voltage exact expectation and the uniform-packing reduction are
conditional tools, not the missing construction. In particular, growing
block sizes and a coverage bound<=3 do not permit an unproved application
of fixed-uniformity design/nibble results or an exact-design obstruction.

The remaining goal is still the original diagonal Zarankiewicz lower bound,
beginning with r=4 and exponent7/4. No new surviving construction, universal
upper bound, proof, or disproof was obtained. Spec still has its sole sorry
at line2982. No proof was submitted and no computation or Lean repair is
pending.

## Quartic additive norm: arbitrary thinning in ALL characteristics (Lean verified)

This continuation obtained a new uniform obstruction to an entire candidate
family, but did NOT settle the original conjecture. Three new complete files:

  Submission/ScalarProfileTranslation.lean     91 lines
  Submission/QuarticAdditiveThinning.lean     308 lines
  Submission/QuarticAdditiveAll.lean          247 lines

All three have installed oleans and warning-free logs:

  /tmp/ScalarProfileTranslation.log
  /tmp/QuarticAdditiveThinning.final.log
  /tmp/QuarticAdditiveAll.final.log

Their28 printed axiom audits in total use only propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound. No sorry, native_decide, or extra axiom. Spec was not modified.

### General one-scalar transverse profile

ScalarProfileTranslation works over any finite field F of order q and any
finite additive abelian group V with |V|<=q^2. P:F->F->F and Q,R:V->F are
COMPLETELY ARBITRARY functions. On V*F put

  kernel(v,t)=P(t,Q(v))+R(v).

The additive-weight graph has two copies of (V*F)*F and relation

  kernel(v+w,t+s)=a+b.

Fix a transverse row v. A column ((w,s),b) has only three scalar profile
coordinates:

  (s, Q(v+w), R(v+w)-b).

code_eq identifies this with the existing ProfileThinning model.
fourth_power proves for EVERY K44-free arbitrary edge thinning H:

  e(H)^4 <= 165888*q^27.

edge_count gives |V|^2*q^3 for the full host. size_budget gives
q^7<=K*e(H) ==> q<=165888*K^4.

### Actual quartic norm and trace, odd characteristic

QuarticAdditiveThinning uses any actual finite quartic extension E/F.
Point is ker(Algebra.trace F E), and the graph has two copies of Point*F,
with ORIGINAL adjacency

  Algebra.norm F (x+y)=a+b.

No coordinate substitute for norm or trace is assumed. Let sigma be the
actual Frobenius automorphism. The prior normal-basis argument supplies a
nonzero u with sigma(u)=-u. Let

  V={v in E:sigma^2(v)=-v}.

coordinates(v,t)=v+t*u is proved bijective onto Point. The surjectivity
proof uses

  v=(x-sigma^2(x))/2,
  t=(x+sigma^2(x))/(2*u),

and checks t is Frobenius-fixed before descending it to F. Rank-nullity
and trace surjectivity prove |Point|=q^3; the coordinate bijection then
proves |V|=q^2. No unproved basis or cardinal hypothesis is hidden.

norm_coordinates proves exactly

  N(v+t*u)=N(u)*t^4 + (N(u+v)-N(u)-N(v))*t^2 + N(v).

The norm is even in this scalar direction. Thus it fits ScalarProfileTranslation.
hostIso bundles the isomorphism between the coordinate graph and the actual
norm graph. fourth_power applies to ANY spanning edge subgraph, without
translation invariance or any symmetry assumption on the selected graph.

### Characteristic two and unconditional theorem

QuarticAdditiveAll adds a separate argument for characteristic2.
normPolynomial(x) is the characteristic polynomial of multiplication by -x,
using an actual finite basis. normPolynomial_eval identifies evaluation at t
with N(x+t). For trace-zero x, its cubic coefficient vanishes. norm_shift gives

  N(x+t)=t^4+c2(x)*t^2+c1(x)*t+N(x).

In characteristic2, 1 belongs to Point since Tr(1)=4=0. A linear functional
ell on Point with ell(1)=1 supplies a verified splitting

  ker(ell)*F equiv Point,  (v,t) |-> v+t.

Its transverse space has q^2 elements. For a fixed transverse row v and
arbitrary column (y,b), only the three scalar coefficients

  (c2(v+y), c1(v+y), N(v+y)-b)

are needed. The existing ProfileThinning bound therefore applies in binary
characteristic too. This proof does NOT assume that an arbitrary retained
graph preserves any translation symmetry.

all_fourth_power is unconditional in the characteristic:

  [E:F]=4, H<=G, K44.Free H  ==>  e(H)^4<=165888*q^27.

all_host_size proves exact counts |V(G)|=2*q^4 and e(G)=q^7.
all_relative_bound gives q*e(H)^4<=165888*e(G)^4.
all_size_budget gives q^7<=K*e(H) ==> q<=165888*K^4.

Thus EVERY critical-density edge restriction of this full additive norm host
fails eventually. This is NOT a statement about multiplicative norm weights,
ordinary cubic norm graphs, or all possible extremal constructions.

### Motivating filtered diagnostic (external exact, not used in Lean)

A more elaborate restriction was investigated before the general proof.
For q=5 mod8, take E=Fq[z]/(z^4-D), D nonsquare, and write trace-zero points
as A*z+B*z^2+C*z^3. Restrict connection points by

  A is a nonzero square,   B^2-4*A*C is nonsquare.

The second condition removes an obvious diagonal Kummer grid, while the
first cuts a four-conjugate orbit. The norm polynomial used by the producer is

  -D*A^4+2*D^2*A^2*C^2-D^3*C^4-4*D^2*A*C*B^2+D^2*B^4.

/tmp/quartic_additive_filtered.py performs exact finite-prime-field arithmetic.
At q5,D2 the connection set has20 elements. Its exhaustive normalized-first-row
check finds no K44; this is only a finite result, not a Lean certificate or
an asymptotic construction. Log /tmp/quartic_additive_filtered5.log.

At q13,D2 there are468 connection points and an actual K44:

  rows (A,B,C,a):
    (0,0,0,0), (0,1,0,11), (0,4,0,5), (0,6,0,2);
  cols:
    (1,0,2,6), (3,0,5,5), (4,0,7,7), (9,0,6,7).

The four columns all have A*C=2. More generally, for any fixed product P,

  N(A*z+t*z^2+C*z^3)-N(A*z+C*z^3)=D^2*t^4-4*D^2*P*t^2,

so the middle-coordinate increment is shared by the entire hyperbola.
This led to the successful profile analysis, rather than extrapolating from
an isolated finite failure.

Certificate/log: /tmp/quartic_additive_filtered13.{json,log}.
Independent verifier /tmp/verify_quartic_additive_filtered.sage constructs the
actual irreducible quartic field and checks trace zero, both injections,
all16 ACTUAL field norms, and both filters. It does not reuse the producer's
quartic norm formula. Verified log:
/tmp/quartic_additive_filtered13.independent.log.

The final Lean proofs are independent of both finite computations and are
stronger: all edge filters of the full host are included, in every characteristic.

## Product-set and triple-sum Cayley hosts: arbitrary-thinning obstruction (Lean verified)

New complete auxiliary file:

  Submission/ProductSetThinning.lean

Installed olean; clean log /tmp/ProductSetThinning.final.log. All twelve
printed axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. There
are no sorries, extra axioms or native_decide calls in this new file.
The original conjecture remains unresolved; Spec was not edited.

### General rectangle cover

Erdos714RectangleCover works with an arbitrary indexed set system and
injective row/column embeddings for each rectangle. edge_count_le uses an
actual surjection from selected local incidences onto selected global
incidences. It allows overlaps; no false edge-partition assertion is used.
block_free transfers freeness along the actual embeddings. fourth_power
proves, with M rectangles each having side sizes a,b,

  e(H)^4 <= M^4*(24*a^3*b^4+648*a^4).

relative_fourth gives, when L<=a,b,

  L*e(H)^4 <= 672*(M*a*b)^4.

No regularity or invariance of H is assumed.

### Actual noncommutative group host

For a finite group G and finite sets A,B, product A B is the ordered product
set. graph T has two disjoint copies of G, with x adjacent to y iff x*y in T.
edge_count proves exactly e(graph T)=|G|*|T|.

Each g in G gives a genuine complete rectangle:

  rows a*g^-1 (a in A), columns g*b (b in B).

All these maps are injective and all original incidences hold. For an edge
x*y=a*b, choose g=x^-1*a to recover its rectangle. cover checks this order
of multiplication explicitly; commutativity is NOT assumed.

fourth_power applies to EVERY edge subgraph H of graph(A*B):

  e(H)^4 <= |G|^4*(24*|A|^3*|B|^4+648*|A|^4).

relative_fourth gives L*e(H)^4<=672*(|G|*|A|*|B|)^4 for L<=|A|,|B|.
bounded_representations further proves

  L*e(H)^4 <=672*M^4*e(graph(A*B))^4

when every product value has at most M representations in A times B.
The multiplicity hypothesis is explicit; the absolute bound needs none.

### Critical triple-sum/triple-product exclusion

critical_fourth: if |G|<=q^4, |A|<=q, |B|<=q^2, q>0, and H is K44-free,

  e(H)^4 <=672*q^27.

size_budget: under those hypotheses, q^7<=K*e(H) implies q<=672*K^4.
triple_fourth includes A*(B*C) for any three sets of size at most q. The
additive version Erdos714SumSet.triple_fourth covers A+(B+C), also without
assuming commutativity. The additive transfer explicitly uses the original
Fintype instance on Multiplicative G, so there is no instance mismatch.

This rules out the contemplated route of taking three-fold sums of a B4
set in a group of order O(q^4), even after arbitrary edge thinning. It does
NOT assert anything about arbitrary critical graphs, arbitrary Sidon-based
constructions with different parameters, or the unsolved conjecture itself.
No numerical search or external finite-field certificate was used.

### Arbitrary two-input shifts, including both scalar weights

WeightedTagShift has finite fields E/F, |E|=q^2, tag types U,V of size<=q,
row labels (a,t) in F* times U, and column labels (b,s) in F* times V.
The shift is ANY function of BOTH ENTIRE weighted tags:

  shift : (F* times U) -> (F* times V) -> E.

Rows/columns also carry x,y in E. Original adjacency is

  N_E/F(x+y+shift((a,t),(b,s)))=a*b.

Thus the explicitly proposed N(x+y+t*s*theta)=a*b is included, but the
proof does not require a polynomial or separable shift table. It uses the
previous TwoInputFiberThinning theorem after checking the actual norm-fiber
bound and the scalar-level fiber bound. The latter uses a!=0 to recover b;
there are at most |V| column tags at a fixed norm level.

neighborEquiv is an actual change of variables in each original neighborhood.
Using the verified q+1 size of nonzero norm fibers, neighbors_card and
edge_count prove exactly

  degree=(q-1)*|V|*(q+1),
  e(G)=q^2*|U|*|V|*(q-1)^2*(q+1).

For U=V=F, host_size gives

  |V(G)|=2*q^3*(q-1), e(G)=q^4*(q-1)^2*(q+1).

Every arbitrary K44-free edge subgraph satisfies

  e(H)^4<=1327104*q^27.

size_budget consequently proves q^7<=K*e(H) implies q<=1327104*K^4.
No symmetry or retained-Cayley hypothesis is imposed on H.

### Affine dependence on the row point, arbitrary column/tag data

WeightedAffineNormThinning is a different, complementary generalization.
Take arbitrary C with |C|<=q^4 and U with |U|<=q. Data are

  L : U -> C -> (E ->_F E),
  d : U -> C -> E,
  b : C -> F*.

Columns are c in C; rows are ((u,x),a) with u in U, x in E, a in F.
Original adjacency is exactly

  N_E/F(L(u,c)(x)+d(u,c))=a*b(c).

The F-linear maps L need not be invertible. L and d may depend arbitrarily
on the row tag and the WHOLE column, not just a column tag. No degree/rank
bound on that parameter dependence is used. Dependence on the row scalar
weight a is NOT included in this affine model. Rows with weight zero are
included in the full host; any spanning edge restriction deleting their
edges is of course covered too.

norm_affine proves, in every characteristic, the identity for the ACTUAL
finite-field norm:

  N(u+t*v)=N(u)+(N(u+v)-N(u)-N(v))*t+N(v)*t^2.

The proof uses the checked finite-field norm/Frobenius product, not an assumed
norm polynomial. Cardinality gives finrank(E/F)=2, and a genuine linear
equivalence F^2 -> E supplies the scalar-line coordinates. Fixing u and the
first point coordinate leaves a quadratic profile in the second coordinate.
The three coefficients after division by b(c) fit QuadraticProfileThinning.
An actual graph isomorphism transfers the edge count and freeness back to
the original graph.

fourth_power proves for every arbitrary K44-free edge subgraph

  e(H)^4<=165888*q^27.

The exact host edge count is |C|*|U|*|E|. When |C|=q^4 and |U|=q, host_size
proves |V(G)|=2*q^4 and e(G)=q^7. size_budget gives
q^7<=K*e(H) ==> q<=165888*K^4.

In particular, all kernels N(lambda(t,s)*x+mu(t,s)*y+delta(t,s))=a*b
are covered in the affine-point model, regardless of how nonlinear the
coefficient tables are in the tags (and including many more general choices).
Increasing tag-polynomial degree alone cannot evade the scalar-line profile
in the point coordinate. This was checked before any numerical search.

### Scope and unchanged main task

These are NOT obstructions for arbitrary permutations of the entire local
norm-graph vertex set that may depend on both endpoints. Such permutations
can mix the point and weight nonlinearly, and neither proof supplies the
missing hypothesis for them. That full critical gluing scheme is still
unconstructed and unexcluded. Nor are these universal bounds for arbitrary
K44-free graphs. No proof/disproof of Erdos714 was obtained or submitted.

r>=4. No unfinished Lean repair or computation is pending.

## Homogeneous quartic twisted norms: subfield blocks and exact torus failures

This continuation did NOT change Spec.lean and did not resolve Erdos714.
No new Lean theorem is claimed in this entry. The algebraic reductions below
are paper arguments; the finite certificates were checked by exact external
arithmetic, independently of their Sage producer.

### Host and normalization

Let E/F be quartic, q=|F| even, c nonzero with N_E/F(c)!=1. The candidate
has two copies of E*, with adjacency

  N_E/F(x*y-c*x^q*y^(q^3))=1.

For each nonzero fixed endpoint the corresponding F-linear map is bijective:
a nonzero zero would imply N(c)=1. Thus the degree is
D=q^3+q^2+q+1 and each part has q^4-1 vertices. This is at the critical
q^7 edge scale. It is not the previous affine model N(1+B(x,y))=a*b.

Put z=y^(q^3), so y=z^q. Then B=x*z*(z^(q-1)-c*x^(q-1)). In even
characteristic x |-> (x^(q-1),N(x)) bijects E* with T times F*, where
T=ker N. The kernel is trivial: equality of the first coordinates gives
a scalar ratio, and equality of norms gives its fourth power=1. Domain and
codomain have equal cardinality. Inverting the scalar norm coordinates
therefore gives the actual weighted torus model

  N(v-c*u)=a*b,  u,v in T, a,b in F*.

The parameter can be normalized to c0 in F*: fourth powering is bijective
on F*, choose c0^4=N(c). Then c/c0 belongs to T, and replacing the row
coordinate u by (c/c0)*u identifies the weighted torus models. No identification
with the prior biquadratic norm graph is asserted.

### Different twist fixing the quadratic subfield

For the separate model B(x,y)=x*y-c*sigma(x)*y^(q^2), with sigma a
norm-preserving Frobenius, K=F_(q^2) satisfies B(x,y*k)=k*B(x,y).
The subgroup {k in K*:N_E/F(k)=1} has q+1 elements, all of which give
identical-neighborhood column twins on each multiplicative coset.
Equivalently, partition columns into K-lines and then nonzero norm levels.
This gives M=(q^2+1)(q-1) disjoint complete edge blocks, each with D rows
and q+1 columns. The rows have size D because x |-> B(x,u) is bijective.
The restriction N_E/F(k)=N_K/F(k)^2 and bijectivity of squaring give the
column-fiber count q+1.

Applying the already proved unbalanced rectangle-cover bound would give

  e(H)^4 <= M^4 * (24*D^3*(q+1)^4 + 648*D^4) = O(q^25)

for arbitrary K44-free thinnings. This is stronger than the previously
anticipated loose O(q^27) bound. The finite-field block construction itself
was NOT added to Lean here. This fixed-subfield argument does not apply
to the q,q^3 twist, where neither endpoint twist fixes K.

### Conjugate-pair diagnostic for the q,q^3 twist

Inside T let S be the norm-one subgroup of K*, of size q+1. For u in S
and c in F, N(v-c*u)=N(v^(q^2)-c*u). Thus every non-fixed q^2-conjugate
column pair has the same profile on all rows from S. If two distinct pairs
have proportional nonzero profiles on four distinct rows, column weights
make an actual K44. This is a precise algebraic diagnostic, not a blind
random search. At q=4 the 40 non-fixed column pairs already exceed the
27 possible nonzero projective four-coordinate profiles, so a collision
is forced for any four distinct points of S.

The producer /tmp/quartic_twisted_torus.sage uses the four fixed row
parameters 1,s,s^2,s^3, with s a generator of S, and scans one representative
per non-fixed q^2-conjugate orbit in T. It found a collision for EVERY
nonzero c!=1 in F for q=4,8,16 (respectively 2,6,14 parameters).
It then recovers actual x,y in E* through the inverse scalar normalization
and checks all sixteen ORIGINAL equations N(x*y-c*x^q*y^(q^3))=1.
Certificates contain the binary field modulus and original endpoint bit
encodings, not merely reduced profile coincidences:

  /tmp/quartic_twisted_torus{4,8,16}.{log,json}

The independent /tmp/verify_quartic_twisted.py uses plain Python binary
polynomial multiplication, reduction, exponentiation, and gcd. It verifies
Rabin irreducibility of each field modulus, the subfield and norm condition
on c, nonzero/distinct endpoints on each side, and all16 equations. All22
certificates passed, log /tmp/verify_quartic_twisted.log. The independent
checker did NOT reuse Sage's field operations or the profile computation.

Scope: these are exact finite full-host failures. No all-q nonfreeness
result, arbitrary-thinning bound for the q,q^3 twist, or theorem concerning
all K44-free graphs follows from them. The torus parameter normalization is
an algebraic reduction, not a replacement for a Lean-verified graph isomorphism.
No completed solution has been submitted. Spec still has its unchanged
conjecture type, sole FormalConjecturesUtil import, and sole sorry at line2982.

## Quadratic evaluation mixing point and weight: repeated-tag obstructions (Lean)

Two new complete auxiliary files:

  Submission/QuadraticEvaluationGluing.lean  (302 lines)
  Submission/QuadraticEvaluationBinary.lean (253 lines)

Installed builds are warning-free. Logs:

  /tmp/QuadraticEvaluationGluing.final.log
  /tmp/QuadraticEvaluationBinary.final.log

All sixteen printed axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound. Neither file has sorry, added axioms, or native_decide. They are
construction obstructions, not a proof/disproof of the original conjecture.
Spec.lean was not changed or submitted.

### Why this model was examined

A Vandermonde relation can obstruct rectangles with four distinct tags on
both sides in certain linear schemes, but repetitions destroy that argument.
We examined gluing quadratic-norm factors using maps that mix ALL three local
coordinates (point and scalar weight), rather than merely moving the point.
The earlier WeightedAffineNormThinning theorem does not automatically apply
when the chosen weight coordinate depends on the other endpoint's tag.
No assertion that a distinct-tag Vandermonde proof applies to the new norm
graph is made here; only its actual repeated-tag failure was proved.

A vertex is (s,p), where s in F and p(T)=a*T^2+b*T+c. The displayed graph
requires a!=0 on both endpoints. For a quadratic extension E/F and generator
theta, its ORIGINAL adjacency from (s,p) to (t,g) is

  p(t)!=0, g(s)!=0,
  N_E/F(p(t+theta)+g(s+theta)) = p(t)*g(s).

Thus every vertex polynomial has exact degree two, and both edge weights
are nonzero. For each fixed pair of tags the evaluation maps are invertible
linear maps from three coefficients to the local norm point and weight,
when theta and its conjugate are distinct from the base field. The local
norm graph observation is motivation, not a global freeness inference.
The critical host counts were NOT formalized in these new files.

extensionEval is the original polynomial evaluation in E. normGraph uses
Algebra.norm directly; it does not assume a formal norm polynomial.
Both files compute the genuine multiplication matrix in a SUPPLIED basis
1,theta to prove their norm formulas. Existence of these normalized bases
in every finite extension was not newly packaged as a theorem here.

### Odd characteristic: a signed conic configuration

Assume theta^2=delta, delta nonsquare, with a supplied quadratic power basis.
For a coefficient triple p=(a,b,c),

  p(t+theta) = [a*(t^2+delta)+b*t+c] + [2*a*t+b]*theta.

norm_pair and extensionEval_eq prove this and the actual norm identity.
normGraph_eq identifies the original norm graph with the expanded coordinate
relation, including all its guards.

Choose u,c nonzero, u!=+/-delta, satisfying

  16*u^2+(4-delta)*c^2 = 64*delta.

All four rows have tag0 and polynomials

  +/-u +/- (T^2-delta-1).

Columns have tag t=+/-1, and independently signed c, with polynomials

  -(c/(2*delta))*T^2 + (c/(4*t))*T + c.

signed_edge checks the original coordinate equation. The row edge weights
are +/-u +/-delta and the column weights are +/-c, so none vanish. Both
vertex injections are proved; in particular the two repeated-tag column
pairs do not identify vertices.

parameters obtains u,c uniformly for |F|>10 and any delta!=0,4 in odd
characteristic. It uses the previously proved BinaryConicPoints lower bound
of q-2 points on a nonsingular conic. The vertical slices u=0,delta,-delta
and the horizontal slice c=0 each have at most two points. Thus at most
eight points are excluded. This does not rely on a numerical search or an
unproved character-sum estimate. Nonsquareness of delta implies delta!=0,4.

not_free proves the coordinate host obstruction. normGraph_not_free transfers
it to the ORIGINAL field-norm graph using the verified multiplication matrix.

### Characteristic two: two tags and a conjugate pair

Assume theta^2=theta+delta with the supplied power basis. Its actual norm is

  N(A+B*theta)=A^2+A*B+delta*B^2.

parameter_ne_zero derives delta!=0 from basis independence, rather than
assuming it. Select k!=0,delta and define

  v(w)=(w+1+delta)^2+(w+1+delta)*k+delta*k^2,
  a(w)=(v(w)+w)/delta.

Rows have tag0 and polynomial a(w)*T^2+a(w)*T+v(w). At either column tag
0 or1, their evaluated weight is v(w), and their extension evaluation is w.
The value v(w) is an actual norm of w+1+delta+k*theta and is nonzero by basis
independence and k!=0. The guard a(w)!=0 excludes at most two w-values,
because v(w)+w is a monic quadratic. good_card proves this root bound.
For q>=6 there are at least four acceptable w-values and a genuine embedding
of Fin4 in their finite set.

The two column polynomials have leading coefficients A=1 and A=1+k/delta,
linear coefficients k+A, and constant1. Each is used at both tags0 and1.
Their extension evaluations are the two conjugate elements

  1+delta+k*theta,  1+delta+k+k*theta.

Both leading coefficients are nonzero. Their weights at the row tag are1.
shifted_norm proves that both evaluations have norm v(w) after adding any
selected w. row_extensionEval, column_extensionEval, and the injection proofs
therefore give all sixteen ORIGINAL norm edges. not_free is a theorem about
the same normGraph definition as in the odd-characteristic file, not a new
assumed coordinate norm. In a finite binary field q>=6 of course means q>=8.

Scope caveats: the binary rows have equal leading and linear coefficients.
An additional vertex filter deleting that locus is NOT covered by this
certificate. Likewise no arbitrary square-coefficient restriction, bounded
edge coloring, or arbitrary-thinning sparsity is proved. The results do not
exclude all affine maps of the three local coordinates, much less all
endpoint-dependent permutations.

### Other review and main status

The ordinary cubic norm graph coloring review produced no new partition or
positive-density thinning theorem. The verified host is K55-free, NOT
K45-free; the four-row bound is six common neighbors. Neither that bound
nor the sharp local7/8 density loss was used to infer an unproved coloring
or iterated loss.

Completed three auxiliary files; the main conjecture remains unresolved.

Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No numerical experiments or assumed norm
formula are used by these theorems.

### Nonzero, unequal coefficient filter

QuadraticEvaluationFiltered strengthens the binary full-host obstruction.
It retains only polynomials with all three coefficients nonzero and with
leading-plus-linear coefficient nonzero. All original normGraph guards
(nonzero leading coefficients and both scalar evaluation weights) remain.

Assume theta^2=theta+delta and the supplied basis 1,theta. Choose k!=0,1,
L=k+1, h!=0,L, b=h^2+h*L!=0, and a center z avoiding at most eight values.
Define Q(L,x)=x^2+x*L+delta*L^2, v(w)=Q(L,w+z)/b,
a(w)=(v(w)+w)/delta. The four rows have tag0 and polynomial

  a(w)*T^2+(a(w)+1)*T+v(w).

At most four w are excluded by a(w)!=0 and a(w)+1!=0. The four columns,
indexed by independent bits t,e, have tag t and polynomial

  A(t,e)*T^2+(k+A(t,e))*T+b,
  A(t,e)=(z+t*(h+1)+e*L+b)/delta.

The center exclusions ensure their leading and linear coefficients are
nonzero. Row and column leading-plus-linear coefficients are1 and k.
The actual extension-evaluation sum has imaginary coefficient L, and
its norm is b*(v(w)+t). Basis independence proves v(w)+t!=0. All sixteen
original norm edges, four row/column injections, and the valid guards are
verified. `not_free` applies for q>8 (binary q>=16). This alone would not
exclude tag filters avoiding the two particular tags, but the arbitrary-
thinning theorem below does not have that limitation.

### General affine additive-fiber energy theorem

AffineFiberThinning applies to a finite additive row group V, any finite
column type Y, and an additive alphabet A (not required finite). For each
y, let l_y:V ->+ A be an arbitrary additive homomorphism, let a_y be its
selected level, and assume |ker l_y|<=K. The selected neighborhood N_y
is an arbitrary subset of l_y^{-1}(a_y). If its incidence graph is K44-free,
then `fourth_power` proves

  (sum_y |N_y|)^4 <= |Y|^3*K*(3*|V|^3+4*|Y|*K^2).

Key improvement over EnergyThinning: degenerate parallelograms in S are
bounded by4*|S|^2, rather than4*|V|*|S|. The four cases are zero first step,
zero second step, equal steps, and steps summing to zero. Each case injects
into S x S. Every nondegenerate parallelogram has at most three common
selected columns, by K44-freeness. Thus the total neighborhood energy is
at most3*|V|^3+4*sum_y |N_y|^2. Combining fiber energy lower bounds and the
fourth-moment inequality gives the stated result.

`critical_layer` specializes |V|<=q^2, |Y|<=q^4, K=q, obtaining

  e_layer^4 <= 7*q^19.

Different columns can use different maps and levels. No complete code-level
parametrization, symmetry, injective profiles, or regular selected graph is
assumed.

### Application to the ORIGINAL binary normGraph, arbitrary edge selection

QuadraticEvaluationThinning freezes the row tag s and the leading-plus-linear
coefficient r. Its row coordinates are

  (a,c) |-> (s, a*T^2+(a+r)*T+c).

For a column y=(t,A*T^2+B*T+C), write

  m=t^2+t, h=m+delta,
  beta=A*s^2+B*s+C,
  ell=r+A+B.

The actual norm formula proved from the supplied basis is
N(U+V*theta)=U^2+U*V+delta*V^2. Direct expansion proves that each genuine
norm edge lies in the additive fiber

  (h*a+c)^2+ell*(h*a+c)+beta*(m*a+c)
    = beta*r*t+Q(ell,r*t+beta+delta*A).

`fiberMap` is additive in characteristic two. For beta!=0, its kernel has
at most q elements: sending (a,c) to U=h*a+c is injective on the kernel.
Equality of U and the kernel equations give equality of V=m*a+c; then
U+V=delta*a, with delta!=0, recovers a and c. `parameter_ne_zero` derives
delta!=0 from the actual basis hypothesis.

Columns with beta=0 have no edges in this layer because of the original
scalar-weight guard. The additive map uses effectiveBeta=1 on such columns,
keeping its kernel bound while retaining the FULL column type of size q^4.
For actual edges effectiveBeta=beta, and `edge_fiber` verifies the equation.

For an arbitrary H<=normGraph theta, `neighborhoods` uses its ACTUAL selected
adjacency. `layerCopy` embeds the corresponding incidence graph into H, so
K44-freeness transfers without a host-neighborhood or inducedness assumption.
`layer_bound` proves e_layer^4<=7*q^19.

`rowEquiv` proves that the q^2 layers partition all original row vertices:

  ((s,r),(a,c)) |-> (s,a,a+r,c),
  (s,a,b,c) |-> ((s,a+b),(a,c)).

`thinningIso` identifies the entire selected H with the reindexed incidence
graph, swapping its two sides. `edge_partition` counts each undirected edge
exactly once. A second fourth-moment inequality over the q^2 layers gives

  fourth_power: H.edgeFinset.card^4 <= 7*q^27.

`size_budget` derives the exact consequence

  q^7 <= K*H.edgeFinset.card  ==>  q <= 7*K^4.

Consequently no arbitrary edge thinning of these hosts, including tag or
vertex filters, yields critical q^7-scale K44-free graphs at unbounded q.
No host-edge-count theorem was added here; the proved obstruction is stated
directly at the critical edge scale and needs no regularity or host count.

### Scope and main status

This excludes the entire characteristic-two quadratic-evaluation candidate
at the desired scale, not just its earlier signed/bit templates. It does
NOT exclude odd-characteristic arbitrary thinnings, arbitrary permutations
of whole local norm-graph vertices, or general graphs. In particular this
is NOT a disproof of the original conjecture.

## Odd quadratic evaluation: two square edge filters also fail (Lean verified)

New complete file:

  Submission/QuadraticEvaluationCharacters.lean

Installed olean and clean compilation:

sparsity in odd characteristic.

### Proposed restriction and why it was investigated

For odd characteristic, theta^2=delta with delta nonsquare, write row/column
vertices as (s,p),(t,g), with leading coefficients a,A and scalar evaluations
alpha=p(t), beta=g(s). In addition to the original field-norm edge equation,
we tested retaining only edges for which BOTH quantities

  alpha+delta*(a+A),  beta+delta*(a+A)

are nonzero squares. For delta=-1 and q=3 mod4, the earlier signed-conic K44
certificate cannot survive the first of these requirements: it forces both
some nonzero value and its negative to be squares. This made the restriction
worth checking separately; the old certificate did not settle it.

The new graph also requires, for every vertex polynomial a*T^2+b*T+c,

  a!=0, b!=0, c!=0, a+b!=0, a-b!=0.

All original scalar-weight guards remain. `graph` uses the ACTUAL normGraph
and these guards, not a replacement norm formula.

### Derived common-neighbor calculation

The diagnostic began with four rows at tag0 and even quadratics
p_i(T)=a_i*T^2+c_i. For a column (t,A*T^2+B*T+C), put z=t^2, U=delta*A+C.
The norm equation expands to the conic in the row coordinates (a,c)

  a^2*(z-delta)^2+2*a*c*(z+delta)+c^2 + L*a+M*c+K=0,

where

  L=2*(z+delta)*U-4*delta*t*B-z*C,
  M=2*U-C, K=U^2-delta*B^2.

When the first three (a_i,c_i,1) rows are independent, they determine L,M,K
as quadratic polynomials in z. The fourth row imposes a quadratic equation
in z. For each nonzero square z and each of its two tags t, define Z=z*M-L.
Then U satisfies the quadratic

  4*delta*(4*z-delta)*U^2-4*delta*Z*U-Z^2-16*delta*z*K=0.

Recover C=2*U-M, A=(M-U)/delta and B=(2*delta*U+Z)/(4*delta*t).
Thus at most eight candidate columns are tested against the original norm
relation and the two square restrictions. This is an algebraically derived
fiber calculation, not enumeration of arbitrary graph quadruples.

### Translation makes all coefficients nonzero

The simultaneous transformation

  (s,p(T)) |-> (s-1,p(T+1))

## Constant cubic norm rectangles from seventh roots (Lean verified)

New complete file:

  Submission/CubicNormSeventhRoots.lean

Installed olean and clean log:

Seven printed axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
No numerical certificate is used by this proof.

### Uniform construction, q=2 or4 modulo7

Let E/F be any finite cubic field extension and q=|F|. If q mod7 is2 or4,
then7 dividesq^3-1. `exists_root` obtains a primitive seventh root zeta in E
by Cauchy's theorem applied to E's multiplicative group. This uses the
actual extension cardinality from its dimension; root existence is not an
extra hypothesis in the final theorem.

The elementary identity

  (1+zeta)*(1+zeta^2)*(1+zeta^4)
    = sum_(i=0..6) zeta^i+zeta^7 = 1

and the actual finite-field norm product prove

  norm_root: N(zeta)=1,
  norm_one_add_root: N(1+zeta)=1.

Frobenius permutes zeta,zeta^2,zeta^4 when q=2 or4 mod7. The same argument
applies to every nontrivial power zeta^k, because k=1..6 is coprime to7.
Consequently N(zeta^i+zeta^j)=1 for any0<=i<j<7, by factoring out zeta^i.
These norm statements are about Algebra.norm, not a surrogate form.

Use the four row points

  1, zeta, zeta^2, zeta^3

and four column points

  0, zeta^4, zeta^5, zeta^6.

Both injections are proved from primitivity and nonvanishing.
`constant_edges` proves all sixteen sums have norm ONE.
`exists_constant_rectangle` gives the actual injected lists uniformly.
`exists_constant_value` uses finite-field norm surjectivity and nonzero
multiplicative scaling to replace1 by ANY prescribed nonzero d in F.

### Arbitrary scalar-weight laws, no density assumption on labels

For arbitrary label types A,D and arbitrary W:A->D->F, the existing graph
Erdos714EqualRowCubicNorm.graph W has vertices (E x A) + (E x D) and edges

  N(x+y)=W(a,b),  W(a,b)!=0.

`not_free_of_nonzero_value` proves that just ONE pair a,b with W(a,b)!=0
already gives a genuine K44 copy, with all four row labels equal a and all
four column labels equal b. There is no full-row, co-large-row, square-class,
subgroup, Latin-law, or injective-label hypothesis.

`free_iff_zero` states the exact consequence: in these fields this full-point
model is K44-free if and only if W(a,b)=0 for every a,b, i.e. it has no edges.
This strengthens the previous co-large-weight-row results on the stated
congruence class, and explains the earlier constant-norm failures atq9,q11,
andq25 without searching for certificates.

Scope: q=2 or4 mod7 is REQUIRED. This does not coverq31 (a different known
finite failure), q=1 mod7, or all sufficiently large odd fields. The column
list includes0. No independent nonzero-point guard, arbitrary point subset,
or arbitrary edge thinning is claimed. The result is NOT a disproof of the
original extremal conjecture.

### Low-rank review of the odd quadratic-evaluation host

Fixing a row tag s and leading coefficient a leaves row variables b,c.
For a column (t,A,B,C), put

  beta=A*s^2+B*s+C,
  d=a*(t^2+delta)+beta+delta*A,
  j=2*a*t+2*A*s+B.

The norm equation is quadratic in(b,c), with row features
(b^2,b*c,c^2,b,c,1) and column coefficients

  (t^2-delta, 2*t, 1,
   t*(2*d-beta)-2*delta*j, 2*d-beta,
   d^2-delta*j^2-a*t^2*beta).

The column coefficient map has at most two fibers when2*delta!=0: the fixed
coefficient1 determines the projective scale;2*t determines t; the two linear
coefficients determine j and2*d-beta; the constant determines a quadratic
in beta, after which A,B,C are recovered. This was a PAPER calculation, not
a newly installed Lean theorem.

This representation does not produce a useful arbitrary-thinning bound.
The layer hasq^2 rows andq^4 columns: their dimension budget equals the six
coordinates. The complementary-block method no longer has growing average
row AND column block sizes. The existing balanced rank-six theorem would
giveq^(27/4) even for a layer whose whole host scale is onlyq^5. It was not
misapplied to infer the desiredq^(19/4) layer bound. The binary additive-fiber
argument remains genuinely characteristic-dependent.

### Broader constant-norm orbit calculation: unresolved

A separate SYMBOLIC investigation used rows0 plus the three conjugates ofu,
and columns1 plus the three conjugates ofv. Forv=r+s*u+t*u^2 andu having

For t!=0 this can be parametrized by w=u+z and v=z+d/w. Write A=Tr(w),

  C^2+A*C*d+B*d^2+d^3=C,
  B^2-3*A*C+d*(A^2-3*B)=0.

These calculations motivate, but are NOT premises of, the seventh-root

 +2*d*h^2+h^4+3*h^2=0.

## Quartic norm-one torus: uniform four-profile obstruction (Lean verified)

Completed `Submission/QuarticNormOneTorus.lean`, importing only
FormalConjecturesUtil. Installed olean; clean build and six permitted-axiom
audits in `/tmp/QuarticNormOneTorus.final.log`. This is a construction
obstruction, NOT a proof or disproof of Erdős714. Spec was not changed.

### The previously unexamined untwisted endpoint

Let E/F be a finite quartic extension, q=|F|, and T={v:N_E/F(v)=1}.
The host has two copies of T x F*, with actual relation

  N_E/F(v-u)=a*b.

This is c=1 in the earlier weighted twisted-torus model. The original
homogeneous bilinear construction required N(c)!=1, so its earlier finite
certificates did not treat this endpoint. The expected sizes are
|T|=D=q^3+q^2+q+1, order2D(q-1), and D(q-1)(D-1) edges. These host-count
identities were not formalized in this new file and are not premises of
its nonfreeness theorem.

### Algebraic source of four identical profiles

On the quadratic-subfield circle u^(q+1)=1, the transformation

  tau(v)=v^(-q)

preserves the full norm profile whenever N(v)=1:

  N(tau(v)-u)=N(v-u).

`profile` proves this from the actual field identity

  (v^q)^(-1)-u = (-u/v^q)*(v-u)^q,

N(u)=N(v)=N(-1)=1, and Frobenius invariance. Norm(u)=1 is derived from
u^(q+1)=1 and D=(q+1)(q^2+1). Degree4 is used to prove N(-1)=1. This is
valid in both parities, with no assumed coordinate norm polynomial.

`exists_root` obtains a primitive D-th root v in E from cyclicity of E*,
whose cardinality is q^4-1=(q-1)D. `norm_root` proves N(v)=1. The element
s=v^(q^2+1) is primitive of orderq+1. For q>=3 use row points

  1,s,s^2,s^3

and column points

  v, v^(-q), v^(q^2), v^(-q^3).

For the injection proof the latter are represented by powers with exponents

  1, q^3+q^2+1, q^2, q^2+q+1.

All four exponents are distinct and less thanD. `right_twists` identifies
these with the iterated twists, `twist_twice` gives tau^2(v)=v^(q^2), and
`edges` iterates the actual profile identity. Both endpoint lists have
norm1. `weights_ne_zero` proves N(v-s^i)!=0: equality v=s^i would imply
D dividesq+1, impossible.

Assign row weight N(v-s^i) and all four column weights1. `not_free` builds
an actual injective SimpleGraph.Copy of K44 into the subtype/unit host.
Every field restriction, norm equation, nonzero weight, and distinctness
condition is verified. No extension basis or primitive root is assumed
without an existence theorem.

### Scope and remaining main gap

The theorem applies to EVERY finite quartic extension over a field of order
at least3. The field of order2 was not separately formalized. This excludes
the FULL host only. It neither proves arbitrary edge thinnings sparse nor
provides a K44-free construction. In particular, deleting vertices or
selecting one representative from certain orbits is not excluded just by
this theorem; no unsupported symmetrization argument was made.

The main construction and packing routes were reviewed again. General
packing/design existence does not supply the required growing-block
parameters. Restricting a bounded-degree algebraic host by an unproved
orientation, character, or bounded coloring was not assumed to preserve a
constant edge density while excluding K44. No new surviving construction
or universal upper bound contradicting the conjecture was obtained.

## Two binary norm charts and arbitrary varying evaluation bases (Lean verified)

New complete auxiliary files, both installed and warning-free:

  Submission/TwoQuadraticCharts.lean          211 lines
  Submission/VaryingQuadraticEvaluation.lean  266 lines

The first imports QuadraticEvaluationBinary; the second imports the first.
Their thirteen printed axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound. No sorry, added axiom, or native_decide occurs. Logs:

  /tmp/TwoQuadraticCharts.final.log
  /tmp/VaryingQuadraticEvaluation.final.log

Spec was not edited. These are construction obstructions, NOT a proof or
disproof of Erdős714. No numerical search was used in this development.

### Why the varying-basis family was considered

The earlier binary quadratic-evaluation thinning theorem fixes the extension
basis coefficient. Its additive row layers need not remain common to all
columns if the extension evaluation point varies arbitrarily with the tag.
We therefore considered genuinely varying points

  zeta(t)=alpha(t)+beta(t)*theta,

with theta^2=theta+delta and beta(t)!=0 at the tags used. The two-sided
host now has vertices (s,p), p(T)=a*T^2+b*T+c with ALL coefficients allowed,
and actual adjacency

  s,t != 0,
  p(t),g(s) != 0,
  N(p(zeta(t))+g(zeta(s)))=p(t)*g(s).

This is `gluingGraph`. It is not the previous exact-degree-two graph:
NO leading-coefficient or other polynomial-coefficient guard is assumed.
The tag and edge-weight nonzero guards are part of its actual definition.
In particular the scaled model zeta(t)=t*theta is a new specialization,
not an application of the old fixed-imaginary-part thinning theorem.

### General two-chart algebraic obstruction

TwoQuadraticCharts works on a vector space V over a finite characteristic-two
field F, |F|>6. There are two linear maps z_j:V->E and a_j:V->F, where E/F
has a supplied actual quadratic power basis 1,theta. The graph joins a row
v in V to a column (j,y,b), j in Bool, y in E, b in F*, precisely when

  N(z_j(v)+y)=a_j(v)*b,  a_j(v)!=0.

The theorem `not_free` assumes u,w in V, with eta_j=z_j(u)!=0, and

  z_false(w)=0,
  z_true(w)=gamma_true*eta_true,
  gamma_false=0, gamma_true in {0,1},
  Delta_j=a_j(w)+gamma_j*a_j(u)!=0,

and that (a_false,a_true):V->F^2 is surjective. The binary parameter epsilon
selects gamma_true. Thus both common and distinct point-kernel cases are
explicitly permitted. No automatic assertion about arbitrary permutations
or all linear equivalences is made without these hypotheses.

Put B_j=a_j(u). `parameter` selects x such that

  kappa=x*(x+1)!=0,
  Delta_j+B_j*kappa!=0 for both j.

Its proof is the nonvanishing of

  X*(X+1)*(Delta_0+B_0*X*(X+1))*(Delta_1+B_1*X*(X+1)),

a NONZERO polynomial of degree at most6. Each quadratic factor is nonzero
because its value at0 is Delta_j. |F|>6 supplies a nonroot. There is no
unproved trace distribution or point-existence estimate.

Define

  beta_j=kappa/Delta_j,
  d_j=1+B_j*beta_j,
  A_j=delta*d_j^2/beta_j,
  b_j=N(eta_j)*beta_j.

All beta_j,d_j,b_j are nonzero. Choose p with a_j(p)=A_j by joint
surjectivity. The four rows are

  p, p+u, p+x*u+w, p+(x+1)*u+w.

The two columns for each tag j have point coordinates

  eta_j*d_j*theta-z_j(p),
  eta_j*d_j*(theta+1)-z_j(p),

and common scalar weight b_j. Their distinction follows from eta_j*d_j!=0.
Row injectivity follows by applying z_false and a_false, not from a generic
rank assertion. `norm_identity` computes the ACTUAL norm of
eta*(mu+e*d+d*theta), using the existing verified multiplication-matrix norm
formula. The four offsets mu satisfy

  mu^2+mu = step_i*kappa,  step_i in {0,1}.

These identities prove all16 edges. `norm_point_ne_zero` uses the actual
basis to prove every involved field sum nonzero; hence every row edge
weight is nonzero. The final Copy uses all four injected rows and columns.

### Evaluation application, including coincident extension points

VaryingQuadraticEvaluation defines the actual linear maps

  point(zeta)(p)=p(zeta),  weight(t)(p)=p(t).

For zeta=alpha+beta*theta its quadratic minimal polynomial is represented
by the coefficient triple

  k_zeta=(1,beta,alpha^2+alpha*beta+delta*beta^2).

`root` verifies p(zeta)=0 in E. `weight_norm` identifies k_zeta(t) with
N((t+alpha)+beta*theta), so k_zeta(t)!=0 for every base-field t when
beta!=0, by the actual basis and norm nonvanishing.

For DISTINCT k_0,k_1 take u=k_0+k_1, w=k_0, gamma_true=1. The point images
of u are nonzero. If beta_0+beta_1!=0, their imaginary coefficients are
nonzero; otherwise their nonzero constant coefficient separates the two
minimal polynomials. The two Delta values reduce to k_0(t_0),k_1(t_1).

If k_0=k_1, take u=1, w=k_0, gamma_true=0 instead. This handles coincident
OR conjugate extension evaluation points, with no omission of that case.
The two distinct scalar tags t_0!=t_1 make the weight pair surjective by
ordinary degree-one interpolation. `all_charts_not_free` therefore requires
ONLY distinct scalar tags and nonzero imaginary coefficients at both tags;
it has no distinctness condition on the extension points themselves.

### Transfer back to the full two-sided host

`evaluation_surjective` proves that, for beta!=0, a polynomial of degree at
most2 can prescribe both p(zeta)=y in E and p(t)=v in F. First choose a linear
polynomial with extension value y, using the supplied basis; then add a
multiple of k_zeta to correct its scalar value without changing p(zeta).

`gluing_not_free` fixes one nonzero row tag s with beta(s)!=0 and chooses two
distinct nonzero column tags t_0,t_1 with beta(t_j)!=0. Column recovery uses
the preceding surjectivity theorem, and point/weight recovery proves its
injectivity. It constructs a Copy from the two-chart graph into the ORIGINAL
two-sided gluingGraph, checks both tag guards, both nonzero weights, and every
actual norm equation. Thus arbitrary alpha,beta values at all these tags are
allowed, not merely affine functions or a selected numerical family.

`scaled_not_free` specializes alpha=0,beta=id. It uses tags1 andc with
c!=0,1, and row tag1, so even the nonzero-tag restriction does not rescue
zeta(t)=t*theta. This applies uniformly to every finite base field of
characteristic2 and order>6, with any supplied actual quadratic power basis.

### Scope and main status

The new results concern FULL polynomial coefficient sets and full column
point/weight sets. They do NOT exclude arbitrary coefficient guards, vertex
selections, or arbitrary edge thinnings. In particular they must NOT be
misreported as a thinning theorem for every varying-basis host, or as a
classification of arbitrary endpoint-dependent local-vertex permutations.
The earlier fixed-basis arbitrary-thinning theorem keeps its original scope.

A paper-level reason not to reuse that thinning proof indiscriminately:
for zeta(t)=t*theta, the point-evaluation kernel triples are (1,t,delta*t^2),
a projective conic, rather than the collinear kernel family of fixed-imaginary
translations. The existing common additive-plane partition is therefore not
automatically available. No new arbitrary-thinning estimate was asserted.

## Critical density forces many exact-three quadruples (Lean verified)

This continuation obtained a new universal NECESSARY CONDITION, but did NOT
settle Erdős714. New complete file:

  Submission/TripleCommonDensity.lean   269 lines

It imports Submission.UnbalancedBounds, not Spec. Installed olean; clean final
build `/tmp/TripleCommonDensity.final.log`. All eight printed axiom audits use
only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry or numerical certificates.
The proofs do not assert a new extremal exponent.

### Universal ordered-rectangle count

For an arbitrary finite incidence system S:A->Finset B, let e=sum_a |S(a)|,
m=|A|, n=|Emb(Fin3,B)|, and

  T=sum_(g:Emb(Fin3,B)) |common(dual S,g)|.

`truncated_moment` proves the general natural-number Hölder/falling-factorial
inequality, with no freeness assumption. `rectangleEquiv` is an actual
bijection between ordered r-by-s and s-by-r rectangles, and `rectangle_count`
proves equality of their counts. The two applications give

  (e-2*m)^3 <= m^2*T,
  (T-3*n)^4 <= n^3*6*Z,

where natural subtraction is truncated and, under K44-freeness,

  Z = #{f:Fin4 embedding A : |common(S,f)|=3}.

The second identity uses common-neighbor sizes in {0,1,2,3}: their third
falling factorial is exactly6 at3 and0 otherwise. The count Z is of ORDERED
four-tuples, not unordered sets. Every unordered four-set is represented24
times; no quotient-count identity was separately formalized.

### Critical-scale theorem and direct graph version

`critical_exact_three` assumes

  C>0, q>=48*C^3, |A|,|B|<=q^4,
  K44-freeness of incidence(S), q^7<=C*e.

It proves

  q^16 <= 393216*C^12*Z.

The proof first gets q^7<=2*C*(e-2*m), then q^13<=8*C^3*T, then
q^13<=16*C^3*(T-3*n), and cancels q^36 after the fourth-power estimate.
The constants are explicit and nonsharp. This establishes that the
exact-three common-neighbor tuples cannot be confined to a negligible
fraction of all q^16 possible ordered row tuples.

`neighbor_incidence_free` checks the bipartite double-cover transfer for an
arbitrary simple graph. A projected overlap would force a loop; Mathlib's
actual complete-bipartite Copy constructor supplies the transfer.
`graph_critical_exact_three` consequently proves the same bound directly for
a K44-free graph with at most q^4 vertices and q^7<=C*|edges|, counting common
neighbors in its actual neighborFinset system. No bipartiteness of the
original graph is required.

### Exceptional-tuples and exact quartic-root models

`exceptional_budget` assumes additionally that a specified exceptional family
X of ordered four-row tuples has |X|<=D*q^15, and that all tuples OUTSIDE X
have at most TWO common neighbors. It proves

  q <= 393216*C^12*D.

This is a conditional exclusion for unbounded q, not an assertion that every
algebraic graph has such an exceptional-family bound. In particular no
unproved codimension, Lang-Weil, or monodromy estimate appears in the proof.

`separable_quartic_not_three` proves that a separable degree-four polynomial
cannot have exactly three base-field roots. Divide out its full root multiset:
the remaining root-free factor would have degree1, which splits, contradiction.
Separability identifies multiset cardinality with distinct-root cardinality.

`quartic_model_budget` combines that fact with the universal counting result.
Outside X it explicitly requires a degree-four separable polynomial p(f) and
EQUALITY between the common-neighbor count and the cardinality of ALL of
p(f)'s base-field roots. Under that hypothesis it gives the same bound on q.
An injection into a quartic root set is NOT sufficient: the fourth root might
be excluded by a vertex or edge filter. The theorem does not silently replace
an injection by a bijection or cover arbitrary quartic-based graphs.

### Review scope and main status

The exceptional-quintic tool was reconsidered along with its prior affine-
slice, quadratic-profile, and V5 obstructions. None was bypassed. No new
threefold or noncommutative construction with a global three-neighbor bound
was obtained. The new counting theorem explains an additional obstruction to
models with generically <=2 common neighbors, while still allowing a genuine
quintic model with three roots on a positive fraction of tuples. It is NOT a
universal disproof of the conjecture.

## All-r maximal common-neighbor density (Lean verified)

Generalized the previous fourth-case counting development. New complete file:

  Submission/CriticalCommonDensity.lean   253 lines

Import: Submission.TripleCommonDensity. Clean installed build:
/tmp/CriticalCommonDensity.final.log. All nine printed axiom audits use only
propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry, native_decide, or added axiom.
This is a necessary condition and a conditional model obstruction, NOT a
construction or a resolution of Erdős714.

For r>=2 and a finite incidence system S:A->Finset B, write Z_r for the number
of ORDERED embeddings f:Fin r -> A whose common columns have cardinality r-1.
If

  C>0, q>=2*(r-1)*(2*C)^(r-1),
  |A|,|B|<=q^r, K_(r,r)-freeness, q^(2*r-1)<=C*e,

then `critical_maximal_common` proves

  q^(r^2) <= M(r,C)*Z_r,
  M(r,C)=(2*(2*C)^(r-1))^r*(r-1)!.

The proof is first written with r=s+1. With m=|A|,
n=|Emb(Fin s,B)|, and T=sum_g |common(dual S,g)|, the exact moments are

  (e-(s-1)*m)^s <= m^(s-1)*T,
  (T-s*n)^(s+1) <= n^s*s!*Z_(s+1).

Natural subtraction is truncated. Freeness ensures common sizes<=s, and
x.descFactorial(s) is s! at x=s and zero at every smaller x. The already
checked rectangle bijection identifies the two ways of counting these
ordered complete rectangles. All variable-exponent arithmetic, density
thresholds, and cancellations are verified, including s=1/r=2.

`neighbor_incidence_free` generalizes the actual bipartite double-cover
transfer to every positive r. `graph_critical_maximal_common` applies the
same bound directly to arbitrary simple graphs with at most q^r vertices
and q^(2*r-1)<=C*|edges|, using their actual neighborFinsets. The original
graph need not be bipartite.

`exceptional_budget` assumes a specified exceptional set X of ordered
r-tuples with |X|<=D*q^(r^2-1), and at most r-2 common neighbors outside X.
It concludes q<=M(r,C)*D. The cardinality hypothesis on X is explicit;
no algebraic-geometric dimension or point-count estimate is supplied by
this theorem.

`separable_not_degree_sub_one` proves over ANY field that a separable
polynomial of positive degree r cannot have exactly r-1 base-field roots.
It factors out the whole root multiset; the remaining degree-one root-free
factor would split, contradiction. `separable_root_model_budget` applies
this to exact degree-r root models outside X and gives the same bound on q.
The model hypothesis is EQUALITY with the cardinality of ALL base-field
roots. An injection of neighbors into roots, or a selected root subset,
is explicitly not enough.

No new family realizing the critical density was found. The inequalities
remain compatible with sufficiently small positive critical constants and
with positive-density maximal-common tuples. They cannot be used as a
universal little-o upper bound or a negation of the conjecture.

## Power-quadratic sparse root bound (Lean verified)

New complete file: Submission/PowerQuadraticRoots.lean. Sole import:
FormalConjecturesUtil. Installed build /tmp/PowerQuadraticRoots.log is clean;
five printed axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.

For k>0 and b not a k-th power, all roots of

  X^(2*k) + a*X^k + b

have the same k-th power, hence there are at most k roots. Subtracting the
equations of x and y gives (x^k-y^k)*(x^k+y^k+a)=0. If their powers differ,
the second factor vanishes, so b=x^k*y^k=(x*y)^k, contradiction.

With a supplied primitive k-th root of unity, the full solution set has
cardinality zero or exactly k. At a=-(1+b), the polynomial factors as
(X^k-1)*(X^k-b), so exactly k roots occur. In a finite field containing a
primitive k-th root with k>1, the power map is not injective, hence not
surjective, proving that such a b exists.

Public results: same_power, finite_root_bound, nonpower_ne_zero,
sharp_equation, solution_card_zero_or_k, sharp_card, exists_nonpower.
For k=3 this is a sextic with zero or three roots, consistent with the
necessary exact-three common-neighbor counts. No graph application was
found. Ordinary cubic norm common-neighbor sextics are not generically of
this sparse form. Previously disproved V5 orbit seeds with this shape do
not acquire a common-neighbor bound merely from their seed root count.
No unbounded finite-field family with chosen primitive roots was packaged.

Spec is unchanged; its sole sorry at line2982 remains. This root-count
result is not a proof or disproof of Erdős714.

## Pure zero-or-three root models: exact moments and a quantified limitation (Lean verified)

New complete file: Submission/PureCommonMoments.lean. Imports the polynomial
exceptional-density file and PowerQuadraticRoots. Clean installed build:
/tmp/PureCommonMoments.final.log. All ten printed audits use only propext,
Classical.choice, Quot.sound. This is NOT an upper bound for arbitrary
K44-free graphs; the near-full degree/codegree assumptions below matter.

For any incidence system, write d_b for the column degree and d_g for the
common row count of an ORDERED pair of distinct columns. If every ordered
r-row tuple has either 0 or k common columns, then `pure_moment_identity`
proves

  sum_g (d_g)_r = (k-1)*sum_b (d_b)_r.

Here (x)_r is the descending factorial. `degree_pair_budget` deduces, for
nonempty B, minimum column degree d and maximum pair codegree t,

  (k-1)*(d)_r <= (|B|-1)*(t)_r.

At r=4,k=3, if q>=16, 0<|B|<=q^4, every column degree>=q^3-q^2, and every
column-pair codegree<=q^2+q, this is impossible (`zero_or_three_not_regular`).
`sparse_sextic_not_regular` explicitly applies the earlier root theorem to
an exact all-root model X^6+a_f X^3+b_f, b_f noncube, with a primitive cube
root supplied. No assertion is made that every such algebraic construction
has the required degree/codegree estimates.

The stronger quantitative result does NOT assume the pure condition. Let
Z_12 count ordered four-row embeddings with common-neighbor count 1 OR 2.
For ANY K44-free system, `intermediate_moment_identity` proves

  2*sum_b (d_b)_4 = sum_g (d_g)_4 + 2*Z_12.

Under the preceding q>=16, |B|<=q^4 and explicit degree/codegree bounds,
`intermediate_density` proves |B|*q^12 <= 10*Z_12. If additionally
q^4<=D*|B|, then `scaled_intermediate_density` gives q^16<=10*D*Z_12.

`intermediate_polynomial_budget` combines that with actual Schwartz–Zippel:
if rows inject into F^4, q=|F|, and a NONZERO P in 16 variables vanishes on
all intermediate-count tuples, then q<=10*D*deg(P). In
`sparse_sextic_polynomial_budget` the sparse noncube sextic root model is
required only outside P=0. Consequently the sparse model cannot be saved
by a bounded-degree exceptional hypersurface under these same explicit
near-full degree/codegree assumptions. Root-count equality is required,
not merely an injection into all roots.

This explains a limitation of the newest sparse-root ingredient, not a
universal obstruction. K44-free graphs with more irregular pair codegrees,
selected-root models, or different generic common-neighbor distributions
are not ruled out. No construction or proof/disproof of Erdős714 resulted.

## Pure zero-or-three models: universal subcritical bound (Lean verified)

This continuation removed ALL degree and pair-codegree regularity assumptions
from the exact zero-or-three-model obstruction. Three new complete files:

  Submission/NonuniformFourthDesign.lean   250 lines
  Submission/PureFourStructure.lean        166 lines
  Submission/PureFourUpper.lean            263 lines

Clean installed logs:
/tmp/NonuniformFourthDesign.final.log
/tmp/PureFourStructure.final.log
/tmp/PureFourUpper.final.log
All seventeen printed axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound. No sorry, added axiom, admit, or native_decide in these files.
No numerical search was used. These are special-model restrictions, NOT a
proof/disproof of Erdős714 or a new upper exponent for general K44-free graphs.

### Nonuniform local design argument

`pair_fisher` proves Fisher's inequality for indexed PROPER blocks with
constant pair coverage l>0, allowing arbitrary block sizes and point degrees.
At each point v, its replication d_v is strictly greater than l: choose a
block containing v and a point missing from that proper block. Pair coverage
is a strict subset of the blocks containing v. The real incidence Gram
matrix is diag(d_v-l)+l*J, hence positive definite and full rank.

`pair_coverage_lower`: if every four-subset of v points belongs to l>0
proper blocks, the blocks containing any fixed pair induce a pairwise
balanced design on the other v-2 points. Thus at least v-2 blocks contain
each point-pair. This does not assume uniform block sizes.

`small_pair_union_bound`: for indexed sets U_i with pair intersections <=l,

  2*sum_i |U_i| <= 2*|ground| + l*(|I|)_2.

`matching_budget` applies this to the coverage sets of m disjoint point-pairs.
When l<=2, it gives m*(v-2)<=b+m*(m-1). Taking m=floor(v/2), using an actual
embedding Fin m x Bool -> V, yields `fourth_design_bound`:

  (v-2)^2 <= 4*b.

This is a coarse bound for exact fourth-order designs of index 1 OR 2 with
proper blocks, not the earlier uniform-block Ray-Chaudhuri--Wilson theorem.

### Large-block structure in a pure system

For S:B->Finset V assume every four-subset of V is contained in exactly
0 or 3 indexed blocks. Every four-subset of any one block therefore has
coverage 3.

`block_size_or_three_containers`: for a block of size d>=4, either

  (d-2)^2 <= 4*|B|,

or exactly three indexed blocks contain it. For the proof, remove its k
full containers. If k<3, the intersections with the other blocks form a
proper fourth-order design of index 3-k, either 1 or 2, on that block.
Apply the actual nonuniform bound above; the finite restriction and coverage
bijections are proved explicitly.

`large_block_isolated`: above that size threshold, every block outside the
three full containers meets the large block in at most 3 points.
`large_block_twins`: the three containers must all be IDENTICAL to the large
block. Apply the same result to a larger container and compare its three
containers with the original three. No maximal-block choice is needed.

### Universal edge bound for the pure model

`pure_four_square_bound`: for |B|,|V|<=N, N>=1, and the exact zero-or-three
four-point coverage condition, the incidence count e obeys

  e^2 <= 104*N^3.

Small blocks have d^2<=16*N, so Cauchy--Schwarz gives e_small^2<=16*N^3.
For the large blocks, collapse the three identical copies to distinct
neighborhoods. Any two resulting blocks meet in at most3 points. Ordered
pair counting and Cauchy--Schwarz give E_distinct^2<=4*N^3, hence
 e_large^2<=36*N^3. Finally (e_small+e_large)^2<=2*(e_small^2+e_large^2).
The finite image, its multiplicities, and every edge-count transfer are
included in the Lean proof.

`common_zero_three_square` gives the same bound for an incidence system
S:A->Finset B whose ordered four-row common counts are all 0 or 3, by actual
finite-set/embedding and duality transfers. `critical_pure_budget` proves

  q^2 <= 104*C^2

whenever q>0, both parts have size<=q^4, q^7<=C*e, and all four-row common
counts are 0 or3. NO degree/codegree regularity is assumed.

`critical_exists_intermediate`: if additionally K44-free and q>11*C, there
must be a quadruple with exactly1 or exactly2 common neighbors. This is only
an existence statement, not a positive-density count or stability theorem.

`sparse_sextic_critical_budget` applies the unrestricted pure bound to the
EXACT all-root model X^6+a_f X^3+b_f, b_f noncube, with a primitive cube root
supplied. This excludes unbounded critical families of that exact model,
regardless of degree/codegree irregularity. Equality with ALL roots is
required. This theorem does NOT automatically allow a bounded-degree
exceptional set; the earlier exceptional-model result still needs its
explicit near-full degree/codegree assumptions. No stability theorem was
proved to bridge that distinction.

`graph_pure_square` gives the direct simple-graph version with N vertices:

  |E(G)|^2 <= 26*N^3,

if every ordered four-vertex tuple has 0 or3 common neighbors. The factor
improves because the incidence sum is exactly twice the edge count.

### Other review and unchanged main task

The quartic norm-one torus orientation gap was reconsidered. Its profile
symmetry on rows x*C depends on the coset x*C, so selecting representatives
of one fixed twist does not prove freeness for all row cosets. No universal
arbitrary-thinning theorem or viable orientation resulted. This was analysis
only; no new torus construction or torus exclusion is claimed.

General K44-free graphs allow common counts 0,1,2,3, so the pure-model upper
bound is NOT a negation of the conjecture. No way to remove or universally
control the intermediate counts was found. The critical K44 lower bound
and every unresolved larger-r instance remain open in this submission.

## Missing count two: local exact designs, not an improved exponent (Lean verified)

New complete auxiliary file Submission/NoTwoCommon.lean, 171 lines, importing
PureFourStructure. Installed clean build /tmp/NoTwoCommon.log. All FOUR printed
axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry, admit,
native_decide, or added axiom. No numerical experiment was used.

The pure zero-or-three bound does not immediately extend when only ONE of
the intermediate counts is excluded. This continuation examined that gap.

`local_container_alternative` generalizes the previous block argument to an
arbitrary point subset U of size>=4 with at least one full container. Assume
EVERY four-subset of U has indexed coverage exactly3. Then either

  (|U|-2)^2 <= 4*|B|,

or exactly three blocks contain U. The proof removes its full containers
and applies the verified nonuniform fourth-design bound to the proper
intersection family. It does not require any coverage condition outside U.
`local_container_isolation`: in the latter case, all blocks not containing
U meet it in at most3 points.

`pair_four_coverage`: assume every four-point coverage is <=3 and NEVER2.
For distinct blocks b,c, every four-subset of U=S_b intersect S_c already
has at least two containers, hence exactly3. The local theorem applies.

`pair_intersection_alternative`: for every distinct b,c, either

  (|S_b intersect S_c|-2)^2 <= 4*|B|,

or exactly three blocks contain their intersection, including an actual
third index d distinct from b and c; every other block meets that
intersection in at most3 points. The third index and all incidence/subset
conditions are proved, not assumed.

Crucial scope: this is a PAIR-intersection bound, not the earlier bound on
whole column neighborhoods. When |B| is on the q^4 scale, it permits pair
codegrees on the q^2 scale, exactly as the critical heuristic predicts.
It gives no subcritical edge bound and does not disprove the conjecture.
Allowing coverage1 destroys the exact design on a single column's whole
neighborhood. Conversely, forbidding only coverage1 leaves local coverages
1 or2 after removing that column, not a constant; Fisher's exact-coverage
proof was not applied to that varying-coverage system.

Other review: arithmetic quintic models, V5 twists/line-free orbit sections,
and cubic scalar-weight modifications were reconsidered against the existing
certificates and arbitrary-thinning obstructions. No new viable construction
or theorem excluding all of those broader families resulted. In particular,
the already documented finite V5 failures include line-free points and
reduced zero-dimensional sections; excluding rational-line points or
singular fibers alone was not assumed to repair them. The cubic weight law
N(x-y)=ab(a-b) was recognized as already tested, not treated as a new candidate.
