## Arbitrary linear quadratic-norm charts in characteristic two (Lean verified)

New complete file Submission/LinearQuadraticCharts.lean, 345 lines, imports
TwoQuadraticCharts. Installed clean build /tmp/LinearQuadraticCharts.final.log.
All SEVEN printed audits use only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound.
No sorry, admit, native_decide, or added axiom. This excludes a full linear
candidate class, NOT arbitrary nonlinear relabelings or edge thinnings, and
NOT the original extremal conjecture.

### Exact scope

F is a finite field of characteristic2 with |F|>6. E/F has a supplied ACTUAL
quadratic power basis 1,theta, with theta^2=theta+delta. Let V be an F-module
and let Phi_0,Phi_1 be ARBITRARY linear isomorphisms V -> E x F. Write
z_j=first coordinate, a_j=second coordinate of Phi_j.

`all_linear_charts_not_free` proves that the full two-chart host

  rows v in V,
  columns (j,y,b) in Bool x E x F*,
  N(z_j(v)+y)=a_j(v)*b, a_j(v)!=0

contains K44. There is NO remaining hypothesis on relative point kernels,
weight-map independence, or compatibility of the two isomorphisms. This
strictly strengthens the earlier evaluation-chart application.

### Algebra completing the old two-chart criterion

`kernelVector Phi=Phi^(-1)(0,1)` and `pointVector Phi=Phi^(-1)(1,0)` have
verified coordinates. `kernel_line` explicitly parametrizes the point
kernel, and `common_kernel` handles coincident kernels without an unproved
dimension assertion.

`weight_dichotomy` proves either the two weights jointly prescribe arbitrary
values, OR a_1=c*a_0 for a nonzero c. If not proportional, an explicit vector
with a_0=0 and a_1!=0, together with kernelVector Phi_0, gives interpolation.

For independent weights, the earlier TwoQuadraticCharts.not_free applies:
if the point kernels differ use u=k_0+k_1, w=k_0, epsilon=true. Then the two
Delta values are1. If they coincide use u=pointVector Phi_0, w=k_0 and
epsilon=false. All nonvanishing assumptions are derived from the actual
linear isomorphisms.

For proportional weights, the new `zero_slope_not_free` removes the joint
surjectivity requirement. If both a_j(u)=0, the required row parameter is
chosen on a single line:

  p=(delta/kappa(x))*w, kappa(x)=x*(x+1).

This makes a_j(p)=delta*Delta_j/kappa(x) simultaneously. The norm identities,
four injected rows, two columns of each tag, and nonzero row/column weights
are all checked as in the original two-chart proof.

For distinct kernels in this case use u=k_0+c*k_1, w=k_0. The normalization
c*a_0(k_1)=1 implies a_0(u)=a_1(u)=0. For common kernels the pointVector has
both weights zero. Thus no proportional-weight case is omitted.

### Actual endpoint-dependent gluing

`gluingGraph L R` has vertices (I x V) + (J x V), where BOTH linear
isomorphisms L(i,j), R(i,j):V -> E x F may depend on BOTH endpoint tags.
Adjacency uses

  N(z_L(x)+z_R(y))=a_L(x)*a_R(y),
  a_L(x)!=0, a_R(y)!=0.

`chartCopy` embeds the full two-chart graph at any fixed row tag i and any
injection Bool -> J. Column points and weights are recovered using the
actual inverses R(i,j)^(-1)(y,b). The copy proves both part injections,
every norm equality, and BOTH transformed-weight guards.

`gluing_not_free` therefore excludes this full linear gluing whenever one
row tag and two distinct column tags are available. No shared point change,
shared weight map, or endpoint-independence is assumed. It is NOT a claim
about arbitrary permutations of the nonlinear seed set E x F*, affine

## General permutation covers: exact lifting and regularization (Lean verified)

New complete auxiliary file:

  Submission/PermutationVoltage.lean

Imports Submission.Voltage; namespace Erdos714PermutationVoltage. The
Voltage olean was refreshed; /tmp/Voltage.refresh.log audits its existing
results with permitted axioms only. New clean installed log:
/tmp/PermutationVoltage.final.log. All FIFTEEN printed audits use only
propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. No sorry, admit, native_decide, or
added axiom in the new file. This is a positive reduction of a possible
construction problem, NOT an existence theorem or conjecture solution.

### Arbitrary matching covers

For sheet set Omega and edge permutations M(x,y), the lifted edge is

  (x,s) ~ (y,M(x,y)(s)).

`matching_representation` derives this presentation from the abstract
perfect-matching axioms: each base edge has exactly one neighbor from every
left sheet, the right endpoints uniquely determine the left sheet, and
no edge projects outside the base incidence. Finiteness of the sheet set
turns each chosen injection into a bijection. Thus the presentation does
not impose a group-regularity assumption.

`projection_injective` proves that in every lifted biclique, the base
coordinates on each part are injected. For a rectangle, define

  H_ij = M_0j^(-1) * M_ij * M_i0^(-1) * M_00,

where permutation multiplication is composition. `liftsEquivFixed` is an
actual equivalence between all sheet assignments and the sheets fixed by
EVERY H_ij. `lifts_card` supplies its cardinality equality.
`free_iff_no_fixed_sheet` is the exact global freeness criterion.

The distinction from regular covers is important: fixed sheets do NOT
require H_ij to be the identity permutation. `nonflat_lift` explicitly
exhibits a matrix with a lift but nonflat inverse labels, whenever one
nonidentity permutation fixes a sheet. This prevents a false converse.

### Bounded nonregular covers reduce to bounded regular covers

`regularization` proves: if the permutation cover on nonempty Omega is
Krr-free, then the regular symmetric-group cover with edge voltage
M(x,y)^(-1) is also Krr-free. The inverse is required because the earlier
regular cover uses RIGHT multiplication. A flat inverse-label rectangle
has sheet assignments a_i,b_j with b_j=a_i*M_ij^(-1); evaluating inverse
permutations at a fixed sheet supplies a forbidden permutation-cover lift.

`regular_as_permutation` identifies any regular group cover with its
right-multiplication permutation presentation. Thus allowing arbitrary
matching covers does not enlarge the EXISTENCE question for some bounded
number of sheets: m sheets can be regularized to m! sheets. This does not
claim the converse for a particular symmetric-group label table.

Exact counts:

  permutation cover vertices = m*(|X|+|Y|), edges = m*e(base);
  regularized cover vertices = m!*(|X|+|Y|), edges = m!*e(base).

Consequently a bound on m independent of the field size would preserve the
critical exponent. No such successful uniform labeling was obtained.

### Necessary edge-coloring and density conditions

For fixed left sheet s, `phase S M s t` selects the base edges with
M(x,y)(s)=t. `phase_free` proves every phase is Krr-free when the cover is.
`phase_edge_partition` counts their edges exactly. `extract_dense_phase`
extracts an actual free base subgraph with

  e(base) <= m*e(selected).

This is a necessary condition, not a converse construction of a cover from
one dense free subgraph or an arbitrary edge-coloring.

`not_free_of_edge_ramsey` excludes a cover IF every coloring of the base
edges by Omega has a monochromatic Krr. The Ramsey hypothesis is fully
explicit. It was NOT established for cubic norm graphs, and bounded
common-neighbor counts do NOT supply it. No universal impossibility for
all bounded covers was inferred.

### EvenAdditiveProduct.lean: uniform structural theorem

Imports AdditiveCoding and TwistedQuadraticProduct. Namespace

The abstract theorem not_free assumes:
  E,F finite fields of characteristic3;
  |F|>=5 and |E|=|F|^3;
  Q:E->F is ANY even function, Q(-x)=Q(x);
  L:E->+F is ANY additive map.

It proves that the full code graph
  f_(a,s)(x)=Q(a*x)+L(a*x)+s,  a,x in E*, s in F
contains K44. Q need not be a polynomial, and L need not be F-linear.
No algebra structure between E and F is needed for the abstract theorem.
No surjectivity of L, degree regularity, or codegree bound is assumed.

Proof:
1. K=ker(L) has cardinality at least q^2 by the additive-homomorphism fiber
   bound, where q=|F|. Let J_b={x : L(x)=L(b*x)=0}.
2. joint_sum exactly double-counts
     sum_(b in E) |J_b| = |E|+(|K|-1)|K|.
3. If all b outside {0,1,-1} had |J_b|<=q, that identity would contradict
   |K|>=q^2, |E|=q^3, q>=5. exists_large_joint therefore supplies b!=0,+/-1
   with |J_b|>q. The proof permits nonsurjective L.
4. J_b is an additive subgroup, hence a ZMod3-submodule. joint_card_power
   proves its cardinality is a power of3, using an actual ZMod algebra and
   Module.card_eq_pow_finrank. Since q is also a power of3, joint_card_gap
   improves |J_b|>q to |J_b|>=3q.
5. Remove0. There are >2q remaining points. D(x)=Q(x)-Q(b*x) is even, so
   every D-fiber on this negation-closed set is negation-closed without a
   fixed point. Pigeonhole gives a fiber with >2 points; four_of_neg_closed
   explicitly supplies four distinct members x,-x,y,-y.
6. copy_of_joint_fiber uses rows1,-1,b,-b, with symbols0,0,t,t, and those four
   nonzero columns, with symbolsQ(x). All sixteen original code incidences
   and both injections are proved.

**Correction/precision to the earlier discussion:** Over a finite field of
characteristic3 with -1 nonsquare, X^5+aX^3+b has 0,1,or3 DISTINCT rational
roots; it NEVER has exactly2. The previous bound <=3 was not wrong, but
mentioning intermediate counts must not suggest that2 is available in this
specific all-root model. Count1 is available at positive density, so the
robust pure0/3 obstruction still does NOT exclude the quintic approach.

The proof is elementary and does not assume a polynomial-discriminant
Galois-group theorem:

* linear_cubic_bijective: x -> x^3+kx is bijective whenever -k is nonsquare.
  Its injectivity follows by factoring the difference; finiteness gives
  surjectivity.
* cubic_has_root: x^3+a*x^2+b*x+c has a rational root if its characteristic3
  discriminant D=a^2*b^2-b^3-a^3*c is nonsquare. When a=0 this is the preceding
  additive-cubic statement. When a!=0, choose z solving
      z^3-(a^4/D)*z=a^3/D,
  and use x=z^-1+b/a. The proof establishes D,z nonzero, the nonsquare
  hypothesis for the additive cubic, and the complete rational identity
      a^3*z^3*p(z^-1+b/a)=a^3+a^4*z-D*z^3.
* Two normalized roots t,t+1 force
      A(t)=-(2t^4+t^3+t^2+2t+1),
      B(t)=t^3*(t+1)^3*(2t+1).
  The exact residual cubic is
      R_t(x)=x^3+(1-t)x^2+t(t-1)^2(t+1)x-t^2(t+1)^2(t-1).
  Its discriminant is -(t(t-1)(t+1))^4. Its evaluations at the two known
  roots are t^4 and -(t+1)^4. Outside t=0,+/-1 this gives a third DISTINCT
  root. Those three exceptional t values are handled directly, not deleted.
* scaled_eval and normalized_coefficients transport arbitrary distinct
  roots r,s to t=s/(r-s),t+1. third_root includes constant term b=0.
* root_count combines third_root with the previous <=3 theorem to obtain
  the exact allowed cardinalities0,1,3.

## Global subsystem closure and bounded completion palettes (Lean verified)

This continuation examined whether the newly constructed exceptional-quintic
Steiner triple system could supply large neighborhoods as CLOSED SUBSYSTEMS.
It obtained a uniform subcritical theorem for that strategy, not a solution
or disproof of Erdős714. No numerical search was used in this continuation.

The earlier tensor, additive-code, uniform-packing, V5, low-rank, and norm-graph
cover results were reviewed to avoid treating a known exclusion as a new
construction. No fixed-block-size design theorem was applied with growing

### SubsystemClosure.lean

New complete file (imports ExceptionalQuinticCounts), namespace
Erdos714SubsystemClosure. Clean installed build, six permitted-axiom audits:
  /tmp/SubsystemClosure.final.log

PairCompletion S is the following GLOBAL condition on an indexed set system:
for every distinct pair x,y, there exists z!=x,y such that EVERY block S_b
containing x,y also contains z. The chosen z can depend on the pair but not
on the block. The theorem does not require the operation to be commutative,
associative, linear, a quasigroup, or invariant under any group.

The main arbitrary-size bound is
  e^3 <= M^2*(3*N^3+4*M*N^2),
where e=sum_b |S_b|, M=|B|, N=|V|, and incidence(S) is K44-free.
No degree, pair-codegree, or regularity assumptions occur.

Proof:
1. Choose a completion operation op, using op(x,x)=x for equal inputs.
2. For a triple of distinct points x,y,z with z!=op(x,y), every block
   containing the triple also contains the distinct fourth point op(x,y).
   K44-freeness therefore bounds the number of such blocks by3.
3. In the ordered-triple sum, exceptions are x=y, x=z, y=z, or z=op(x,y).
   Each has at most N^2 choices, and at most M blocks can contain any triple.
   triple_pointwise and degree_cube_bound give
      sum_b |S_b|^3 <= 3*N^3+4*M*N^2.
   degree_cube_identity proves the actual double-counting identity, not an
   assumption about regularity or generic intersections.
4. The finite Hölder inequality gives e^3<=M^2*sum_b |S_b|^3.

balanced_bound specializes to |B|,|V|<=N:
  e^3 <= 7*N^5.
Thus these K44-free incidence systems have O(N^(5/3)) edges.
critical_budget proves the exact integer obstruction
  q>0, |B|,|V|<=q^4, q^7<=C*e ==> q<=7*C^3.

QuinticClosed T explicitly says that whenever T contains two distinct roots
of one exceptional quintic, it contains the entire root triple.
quintic_pair_completion uses the verified two-root parameter formulas and
third_root theorem to establish PairCompletion for ANY family of these
closed subsets. quintic_subsystem_bound then applies the subcritical bound.
This excludes using arbitrary nonlinear Steiner subsystems in this direct
way, not merely subspaces of an affine Steiner triple system.

### CompletionPalettes.lean

The fixed completion point is relaxed to a set P(x,y) of at most K candidates,
none equal to x or y when x!=y. Every block containing x,y is required to
contain AT LEAST ONE candidate. Different blocks may choose different points.
No single common third point, symmetry, or uniqueness is required.

For a distinct triple x,y,z with z outside P(x,y), the blocks containing the
triple are covered by the union, over w in P(x,y), of the blocks containing
{x,y,z,w}. Each term has at most3 members by K44-freeness. Thus the generic
triple count is at most3*K. The palette exceptions contribute at most
K*M*N^2, and repeated coordinates contribute at most3*M*N^2. This gives
  sum_b |S_b|^3 <= 3*K*N^3+(K+3)*M*N^2.

The resulting balanced theorem is
  e^3 <= (4*K+3)*N^5,  when |B|,|V|<=N.
critical_budget proves
  q>0, |B|,|V|<=q^4, q^7<=C*e ==> q<=(4*K+3)*C^3.
A palette bounded independently of q therefore cannot repair the subsystem
construction. Palettes whose size grows proportionally to q are NOT ruled
out by this bound. Arbitrary graphs are not claimed to have bounded palettes.

## Cross-paired quadratic/cubic seven-coordinate candidate (Lean verified failure)

This continuation returned to a positive construction search rather than
extending the power-cover obstruction. It reviewed the exceptional-quintic,
Ree/ovoid, additive-code, low-degree-profile, and existing rank-six barriers.
No hypothesis of the all-root quintic model was obtained for a new graph.
A concrete different seven-coordinate candidate was then derived and ruled
out uniformly. This is not a solution of Erdos714.

### Candidate and scope

In characteristic3 write x=(u,v), with u,v in F^2, and set
  Q(u)=u0^2+u1^2,
  C(v)=v0^3-v0*v1^2-v1^3.
Use two copies of the points satisfying
  Q(u)!=0, C(v)!=0, IsSquare(C(v)),
and the ORIGINAL cross-paired incidence
  u dot v' + v dot u' = Q(u)*Q(u') + C(v)*C(v') + 1.
This has a seven-coordinate bilinear representation (four coordinates,
Q,C,1); the earlier six-coordinate theorem was not applied to it.
The cross-pairing differs from the uncoupled dot-product variant.

If -1 is nonsquare, Q is anisotropic. If no z has z^3-z=1, then C is
anisotropic: a nonzero second coordinate of a zero of C would produce such
a z by division. Thus the construction is not dismissed by a split-form
zero direction. The Lean lemmas Q_zero and C_zero prove these implications.
The displayed cubic is the usual binary restriction of an Artin-Schreier
cubic norm; the new graph and its copy are defined directly by the displayed
polynomials, without assuming a norm-coordinate identification.

The expected q^4 vertex/q^7 edge scale was only a parameter-count motivation.
No exact edge count or uniform critical edge LOWER BOUND was proved for this
candidate. Its freeness failure suffices to discard it as a positive route.

### Translated-circle calculation

Choose distinct nonzero squares A,B with A*B*(A+B)=1, and let
  k=-(A-B)^2.
In characteristic3, both A and B are roots of X^3+k*X+1. Moreover k!=0.
If k+1=0, the equation for A gives (-A)^3-(-A)=1, contradicting the
Artin-Schreier assumption. Thus the translated circle
  Q(u-(0,1))=k+1, equivalently Q(u)+u1=k,
has a nonzero radius. Every point on it has Q(u)!=0: anisotropy would otherwise
force u=0 and then k=0.

Use rows (u,(1,0)) on this circle. Let s^2=A and t^2=B. The four columns are
  ((0,w),(0,-w^2)), w in {s,-s,t,-t}.
Their Q-values are w^2 and C-values are w^6, all nonzero squares. The row
C-value is1. Each ORIGINAL cross-pairing equation reduces to
  w^6+k*w^2+1=0,
which is precisely the cubic equation for A or B. The four column points
are distinct because A,B are distinct and nonzero, and2!=0.

The parameters are obtained uniformly, not assumed to exist. The previously
proved character-sum lemma supplies t,t-1,t+1 all nonzero squares for every
finite characteristic3 field with -1 nonsquare and size>3. Choose a cube root
a of a square root of 1/(t*(t+1)), using Frobenius surjectivity, and put
  A=a^2, B=t*A.
Then A,B are distinct nonzero squares and A*B*(A+B)=1. The extra t-1 square
condition is stronger than needed but ensures t!=1.

The earlier BinaryConicPoints rational parametrization and norm transport
produce an INJECTION from the whole field into the nonzero-radius circle.
All denominators are nonzero by the nonsquare -1 hypothesis. Four distinct
parameters yield four distinct rows. There is no assumed conic point count,
generic-rank condition, or discarded boundary point hiding a copy failure.

## Seed pair-neighborhood projection: a rigorous obstruction to one packing route

This continuation revisited the genuinely unexcluded amplification regime:
a K_(q,q) base with q^3-by-q^3 degree-q^2 K33-free local factors, and arbitrary
row AND column relabelings depending on BOTH base endpoints. No compatible
permutation family or positive critical construction was obtained.

### Packing idea and precise limitation

For a fixed row tag, four rows with two common columns in each of two
opposite tags already make K44. It is therefore necessary that the associated
four-row shadows of two-column common neighborhoods avoid overlap across
tags. This is not sufficient for global freeness: patterns2+1+1 and1+1+1+1
across column tags, and rows in several tags, must also be controlled.

A possible polynomial packing would put every local two-column common
neighborhood into the form of a graph over ONE coordinate set of size q,
then use polynomial-agreement bounds to pack different copies. The implicit
step of finding that coordinate projection is impossible at the seed scale.
This conclusion was proved without assuming the seed is algebraic or K33-free.
It does NOT exclude coordinate systems that depend on the individual column
pair, sparse variable domains over larger coordinate sets, or arbitrary
nonlinear permutations of the full local factors.

This is exactly the one-point-per-coordinate property required for those

the whole seed or of an unrelated host.

m-by-M incidence system with e edges:

It combines the verified ordered-star bijection on the dual incidence system,

For M<=q^3, D=q^2, q>=2, fiber_card_bound proves EVERY pi fiber has size

In particular, |A|>=q^3 and |T|<=q are impossible.

### Uniform obstruction

Choose c,k!=0 with c2!=1 and c2+k2=-1. conic_parameters constructs them in
EVERY eligible F of order>3, using a parameter t outside{0,1,-1}:
  c=(t2+t-1)/(1+t2), k=(1+t-t2)/(1+t2).
The denominator is nonzero by -1 nonsquare. The conic identity and every
nonzero/distinctness condition are proved in Lean, not inferred from counts.

  v=1,-1,c,-c.
For every nonzero column tag t, put R=1+delta*t. The decisive identity is

  b=-c2*N(R),  y=P_b^(-1)(R*i*k).

### Uniform quartic norm fiber, without Weil bounds or numerics

BinaryQuarticFiber works over ANY binary field of size>4 and any actual
quadratic extension; odd degree is not needed for this algebraic lemma.
Write tau for the explicit binary trace sum, already identified with the
actual absolute trace by the imported BinaryArtinSchreier development.

Choose t with t^4!=t by the polynomial root bound; put A=t^2+t. Then A and
A+1 are nonzero. The additive polynomial

  L(w)=w^4+(A+1)w^2+A*w

has kernel {0,1,t,t+1}. Let C=(A+1)/A^2 and D=(A+1)/A. The key identity is

  C*L(w)=C*w^4+(D*w)^2+D*w,
  tau(C*L(w))=tau(C*w^4).

Fourth powering is bijective and the trace is surjective, so choose w with
tau(C*L(w))=1. In particular z=L(w)!=0. The four nonzero distinct elements
w,w+1,w+t,w+t+1 all have the same L-value z. Their reciprocals v_i satisfy

  v_i^4+T*v_i^3+K*v_i^2=b,
  T=A/z, K=(A+1)/z, b=1/z,
  tau(K/T^2)=1.

All denominators and injections are proved. norm_quadratic realizes the
trace-one parameter in the ACTUAL quadratic extension by an Artin--Schreier
root y with conjugate y+1. Taking Z=T*y proves

  N(v+Z)=v^2+T*v+K.

Consequently norm_four_fiber proves, uniformly and with Z,b,v_i all nonzero,

  v_i^2*N(v_i+Z)=b,  i=0,1,2,3.

## Ternary polar matrix relation: uniform elliptic obstruction (Lean verified)

New complete auxiliary file: Submission/TernaryPolarMatrix.lean (364 lines),
sole import Submission.ConsecutiveSquares. It compiles without warnings,

For a finite characteristic-three field with -1 nonsquare, |F|>3, and a
ring endomorphism sigma satisfying sigma^2(x)=x^3, the actual candidate is

  vertices: two copies of M_2(F),
  vertex guard: tr(X)^2-4 det(X) is nonsquare,
  incidence: det(X+Y)+tr(X^sigma Y+X Y^sigma)=1.

The guard is included in the graph relation, and irreducible_charpoly
proves irreducibility of Mathlib's actual characteristic polynomial from

### Uniform copy

Rows have X(a)=[[a,1],[-1,0]]. Columns have

  Y(R,w)=[[0,R-w],[-R-w,0]], w^2=R^2+sigma(R).

Then z-y=R and yz=sigma(R) for the off-diagonal entries y,z, and the
ORIGINAL incidence expression is 1 for every a. The column discriminant
is sigma(R). Every matrix used satisfies the nonsquare guard.

The twisted-power map R(t)=t^2*sigma(t) is injective. Its identity
R(t)^2=t*sigma(R(t)) follows from sigma^2=cubing. Choose t and t+1 both
nonzero nonsquares; the existing consecutive-square lemma supplies this
in every stated field. The second parameter -t/(t+1) has the same two
nonsquare properties and is distinct. Moreover

  R(t)^2+sigma(R(t))=(t*sigma(t))^2*t*(t+1)

is a nonzero square. The two signs of its square root for each of the two
parameters give four distinct column matrices. Their two matrix-entry
sum/difference identities prove injectivity, not merely distinct roots.

Four distinct nonzero square parameters s=1,x,x-1,x+1 give row parameters
(s-1)/(s+1); their discriminants are -s/(s+1)^2, all nonsquare. Both side
embeddings and all sixteen incidences are checked in exists_copy/not_free.
finite_not_free discharges sigma and -1 for every |F|=3^(2m+1), m>0.
family_not_free specializes to GF(3^(2k+3)) for every k.

Scope: this is a full-host obstruction. The displayed columns have trace
ZERO. The uniform Lean theorem does NOT assert survival under a nonzero-
trace restriction or arbitrary edge thinning.

### Separate nonzero-trace variant: exact external failures

The nonzero-trace restriction was checked through a different derived row
pencil, not by reusing the preceding zero-trace columns. For t a field
generator, use

  X(a)=[[a,1-a*t],[-1,0]],
  Y(c)=[[sigma(t)*c,b],[c,d]],
  d=t-t*c-(t^3-t)*sigma(c),
  sigma(b)+c*b=sigma(t)*c*d+sigma(c).

## Full rank-six hosts with arbitrary vertex multiplicities (Lean verified)

New complete auxiliary file:

  Submission/RankSixFullHost.lean

Imports RankSixThinning and QuadraticRecoveryAll. Namespace
Erdos714RankSixFull. Clean installed log: /tmp/RankSixFullHost.final.log.
All eleven printed axiom audits use only propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound. No sorry, admit, native_decide, or new axiom is present.

### Exact full-host theorem

Let F be a finite field, q=|F|, |A|,|B|<=q^4, and let

  R:A -> F^6, C:B -> F^6

be ARBITRARY maps: no injectivity, projective-injectivity, nonzero, or
polynomial hypothesis. Let E be the FULL relation R(a) dot C(b)=0.
If E has no K44 rectangle, then

  |E|^4 <= K*q^27,
  K = 8*(9^4*(456976*720^4)+12^4).

Thus the full host has O(q^(27/4)) edges, not the critical q^7.
`full_fourth_power` proves the relation theorem; `graph_fourth_power`
proves the actual SimpleGraph statement and the undirected edge count.
`critical_field_budget` proves that q^7<=d*|E| implies q<=K*d^4.

### Multiplicities and exceptional vertices are actually handled

`large_twins` bounds every repeated neighborhood profile of size at least4
by3 in a free full incidence system. `ray_neighbors` proves that nonzero
proportional row vectors have exactly the same FULL neighborhood.
`good_colors` splits the high-degree nonzero vertices into three classes
whose vector maps are ray-injective. It colors actual neighborhood profiles;
no projective representative or classification is assumed.

`row_count` counts all edges on degree-at-most3 rows. `zero_rows` bounds the
number of zero-vector rows by3 when there are at least4 columns. The small
opposite-side case is handled separately in `full_decomposition`.

`bad_rows_bound` gives <=3*(|A|+|B|) edges incident to rows which are zero
or have degree below4. The analogous column bound is applied after proving
`transpose_free`. Removing both types costs at most6*(|A|+|B|).
The remaining edges are covered by nine actual pairs of color classes.
The existing RankSixThinning.fourth_power applies to each class pair, with
its embeddings, nonzero hypotheses, and inherited freeness proved.
The fourth-power sum inequality and the lower-order edge budget give K.

### Arbitrary nonlinear matrix recovery laws

`two_feature_graph_fourth_power` applies to the FULL relation

  x(a) dot y(b) = u(a)*f(b)+v(a)*g(b),

where x,y have FOUR coordinates and u,v,f,g are completely arbitrary.
It explicitly embeds the equation in six-coordinate orthogonality.

`matrix_recovery_fourth_power` specializes this to the actual relation

  trace(R(a)*C(b)) = u(a)*f(b)+v(a)*g(b)

for 2-by2 matrices. The trace-to-four-coordinate-dot identity is proved
from matrix multiplication and trace, not assumed. Arbitrary endpoint
restrictions can be encoded by A and B, and arbitrary repeated matrix
values are allowed. Thus changing determinant exponents or replacing the
two scalar features by nonlinear functions cannot rescue this FULL-host
recovery pattern at unbounded critical density.

### Essential scope distinction

This is NOT an arbitrary-edge-thinning theorem when projective multiplicities
are unrestricted. For example, nonzero constant vectors e0 and e1 give a
complete orthogonality host, which can contain ANY selected bipartite graph.
Extending the new bound to all such free selections would therefore require
a universal extremal upper bound, not the twin argument proved here.

In particular, a complete host alone is NOT a counterexample to an upper
bound on its FREE thinnings: the complete host is not free. No claim that
the proposed universal upper bound is known false is justified by that
example. What is established here is only the full-host result, while the
older arbitrary-thinning theorem retains its ray-injectivity assumptions.

obstructions at their stated scopes; no global classification of all forms,
all field subsequences, or all nonlinear codes has been inferred.
No new qualifying construction or universal extremal upper bound was found.

## Fractional-cover formulation of positive-density thinning (Lean verified)

  Submission/FractionalThinning.lean

### Positive extraction, with the global hypothesis retained

`weighted_count` proves exact double counting with arbitrary real weights.
`extract_dense` says that if B_i are subsets of a finite universe E,
weights w_i are nonnegative, every e is covered with total weight at least1,
and sum_i w_i<=D, then some B_i satisfies |E|<=D*|B_i|.
The index type is explicitly nonempty. `extract_property` retains any
property P satisfied by EVERY B_i; it does not construct P-blocks.

`graph_extract` is the actual SimpleGraph version: every covering graph H_i
must be a spanning subgraph of G and globally F-free. It extracts an F-free
H<=G with e(G)<=D*e(H). Merely choosing free pieces inside local blocks,
then taking their union, does NOT satisfy its hypotheses automatically.

### Exact converse for edge-transitive hosts

For a transitive finite permutation action and nonempty S,
`translated_cover` proves that all translates cover each universe element
exactly m>0 times, with |Gamma|*|S|=|E|*m. `fractional_translates` assigns
weight1/m to each translate, giving exact coverage1 and total mass |E|/|S|.

`dense_iff_fractional_cover` gives the equivalence for any translate-invariant
global set property. `translated_edge_membership` identifies the edge-set
action with pulling a spanning graph back along the inverse automorphism.
`graph_dense_iff_fractional_cover` consequently proves, for any nonempty
edge-transitive host G and forbidden graph F, the exact equivalence between

  some F-free H<=G with e(G)<=D*e(H),

and a fractional cover of G's edges by globally F-free spanning subgraphs,
with total mass at most D. The indexing set in the converse is the actual
finite graph-automorphism group. Freeness is transported by an actual
comap embedding; no integral-coloring converse is asserted.

### Scope and remaining task

This is a positive reduction, NOT a construction of the requisite covering
graphs or weights for cubic norm graphs. It makes precise a weaker target
than a bounded integral coloring or bounded matching cover. The existence
problem remains unchanged: all covering graphs must already be globally
K44-free. No new positive-density selection was obtained.

The scalar-line, local-seed, and semilinear recovery reviews still do not
supply a critical construction or a universal upper bound contradicting
the conjecture. No local block property was promoted to global freeness,
and no fixed7/8 loss was iterated without a separate independence argument.

### Actual candidate and non-exhaustive diagnostics

For q=2^k with k odd, sigma(x)=x^(2^((k+1)/2)), use two copies of GL2(Fq).
For the relative matrix M=g^(-1)*h require ALL of

  trace(M*sigma(M))=1,
  the ordinary characteristic polynomial of M is irreducible,
  M*sigma(M)*...*sigma^(k-1)(M)=I.

The last condition selects identity semilinear norm, not the elliptic
semilinear norm of the earlier no-invariant-line model. In the checked

parameterized by three field entries without enumerating the entire graph.
This is an exact finite parameterization, not a newly proved asymptotic
edge count or freeness theorem.

  A([a,b;c,d])=[a,b+c;c,d],

four rows and columns M,A(M),C(M),C(A(M)), hence an actual K44.
